Consequently, the average magnetic reconnection rates and associated heating rates, determined through the upstream fields, could become orders of magnitude higher than those predicted using the turbulence amplitude at the dissipation scale. We then use a simplified model of the heating of reconnection exhausts to estimate the ratio of this reconnection heating rate to the overall energy cascade rate due to turbulence. Estimates from the PIC simulations and the MMS observations yield a ratio on the order of $1/5$, indicating that direct reconnection heating is playing a substantial role in dissipating the turbulent fluctuations.

authors.name: M. Bilal Khan, Michael A. Shay, Riddhi Bandyopadhyay, Subash Adhikari, William H. Matthaeus, Paul A. Cassak, Julia E. Stawarz, Sohom Roy, Sean Oughton, Colby C. Haggerty, Yan Yang, Francesco Pecora, Jason M. TenBarge

papers.title: Resilient Transmission of Highly Structured Light via Active Convolved Illumination
papers.summary: Wave propagation through lossy and noisy systems as well as spatiotemporally dynamic random media often limits the complex information that can be reliably transmitted or retrieved. Progress in adaptive optics, wavefront shaping, machine learning, and wave propagation theories has significantly advanced physical and computational correction techniques. However, many approaches remain constrained by restrictive operating conditions, limiting their ability to meet growing application-specific demands, such as higher spatial resolution in imaging and greater data capacity in communications, particularly in highly dynamic environments. Recently, active convolved illumination (ACI) was proposed as a novel framework for preserving the spatial structure of optical modes during propagation through strongly distorting environments, such as atmospheric turbulence. ACI aims to bypass the prohibitive complexity of global distortion tracking by combining spectrally localized characterization with compensation using a correlated auxiliary source. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of ACI, detailing the formulation of correlation-injecting and auxiliary sources and the role of segmented reciprocal-space characterization and distortion compensation. We explore extensions in free-space optical communication and potential high-precision phase measurement, and numerically evaluate interferometric strategies for experimental implementation. This work highlights ACI as a potentially versatile framework for distortion-resilient light transmission, with broad interdisciplinary utility ranging from atmospheric physics and remote sensing to telecommunications, target tracking, and biomedical diagnosis, offering flexible deployment either as a standalone paradigm or hybridized with existing optical systems.

authors.name: Anindya Ghoshroy, James Davis, Martin Wilkens, Sahin K. Ozdemir, Durdu O. Guney

papers.title: Equilibrium Elongation of Charged Nanoclusters
papers.summary: When internal electrostatic stresses from electron repulsions overcome surface tension, charged nanoclusters elongate. However, the exact shape they reach at equilibrium has been unknown. We present an analytical model for the equilibrium structure of charged ellipsoidal nanoclusters via a free energy analysis. Energy maps are constructed that determine the equilibrium states as a function of cluster size, net charge, surface tension, and local curvature. The model is compared with molecular dynamics simulations of ice nanoclusters having solvated electrons. Despite the discreteness of the simulated atoms and electrons, both the predictions of the continuum analytical model for elongation and the equilibrium elongated shape show good agreement. The model could therefore predict nanocluster shape evolution in astrophysical and laboratory complex plasmas and atmospheric aerosols.

authors.name: Efstratios M. Kritikos, William A. Goddard III, Paul M. Bellan

papers.title: Oversampled Filter Bank Channelizer for Cryogenic Detectors
papers.summary: We present the field programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of an oversampled gener- alized DFT (GDFT) filter bank, optimized for its usage in the readout of cryogenic detectors, such as the microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKID). A polyphase structure is derived underlin- ing the efficiency of complex valued subband processing, raised by a GDFT modulation. For the latter, a fast Fourier algorithm realization may be used, yielding a highly efficient polyphase imple- mentation for arbitrary integer decimation ratios. The filter bank is tested through a 16-channel GDFT channelizer. The implementation is based on the Xilinx Zynq family of FPGAs and aims to show the data reuse and flexibility offered by the GDFT channelizer structure. General design criteria are summarized for the 16-channel polyphase filter bank channelizer. The performance in hardware resource usage is also presented, taking into account one of the main objetives of the current physics experiments, aiming to have extremely large readout format.

authors.name: L. H. Arnaldi, D. Dellavale

papers.title: Influence of transverse oscillatory shear on the viscous fingering instability
papers.summary: Oscillatory shear can delay the onset of viscous fingering. In addition, uniaxial translational shear also breaks the symmetry of the resulting pattern so that the interface evolves differently depending on its direction of propagation relative to the shear axis. We observe a delayed fingering onset and reduced subsequent finger growth rate for all directions as shear speed or amplitude increases. However, shear widens fingers growing in the direction perpendicular to shear and elongates those in the parallel directions. After onset, neighboring fingers in the perpendicular directions can reconnect near their base when the shear amplitude exceeds approximately five times the excess linear finger wavelength at the onset. Concentration profiles reveal smoother azimuthal edges and overlapping structures behind the tips. These observations show that shear smears individual fingers and connects neighboring ones. This correlates lateral fingering interactions with radial propagation.

authors.name: Zhaoning Liu

papers.title: 1.56 THz Full-Field Rydberg-Atom Imaging with 0.3 mm-scale Spatial Response
papers.summary: THz imaging via Rydberg-atom up-conversion offers a powerful full-field modality with high sensitivity and rapid acquisition. However sub-millimeter imaging above 1 THz is still constrained by source power and beam-delivery loss. In this paper, we demonstrate a \(50~\mathrm{mm} \times 50~\mathrm{mm}\) full-field imaging at 1.56~THz by implementing the \(11P_{3/2} \rightarrow 10D_{5/2}\) transition of a cesium Rydberg-atom vapor. The measured spatial response FWHMs are \(0.314~\mathrm{mm}\) in horizontal and \(0.354~\mathrm{mm}\) in vertical for a \(0.5~\mathrm{mm}\) pinhole, alongside a sensitivity of \(31.7~\mathrm{fW}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1/2}/(6.5 \times 6.5)~\mu\mathrm{m}^{2}\), and a frame rate up to \(300~\mathrm{fps}\). Under matched illumination, relay, and image-processing conditions, mask imaging at 1.56 THz reproduces finer features and edges with substantially higher edge contrast, deeper intensity-trough separation in line profiles, and recovered detail that remains blurred or unresolved at 0.55 THz. Furthermore, preliminary imaging of a \(200~\mu\mathrm{m}\) tissue slice suggests morphological correspondence with H\&E histology histology, offered as a proof-of-concept for label-free tissue characterization. By validating the wavelength-dependent resolution scaling in Rydberg THz imaging, this work establishes frequency scaling as a general design principle for sub-millimeter Rydberg-THz imaging.

authors.name: Xianzhe Li, Yibin Huang, Zhiwen Chen, Kaiqing Zhang, Haixiao Deng

papers.title: Deep, label-free, volumetric lifetime microscopy via low-noise, single pulse sampling
papers.summary: Fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIM) provides label-free metabolic contrast, but conventional time-correlated single-photon counting requires thousands of excitation pulses per pixel to avoid pile-up distortion, limiting imaging speed and increasing motion artifacts and photodamage. Here, we develop single-pulse analog sampling that combines sub-photoelectron read noise with a jitter-immune, frequency-domain estimator for accurate lifetime measurement at low photon counts. Single low-flux traces achieve a photon economy of $F < 1.5$ at 100--150 detected photons, enabling accurate lifetime estimation from a single excitation pulse in label-free, volumetric samples. In in vivo zebrafish eyes, single-shot acquisition recovered the lifetime content of 20-pulse averaging at one-twentieth the exposure, resolving endogenous lipofuscin heterogeneity. In intact mouse kidney, scattering and reduced photon throughput impaired lifetime contrast; this was mitigated by lightweight denoisers that enabled label-free lifetime imaging to 200 micron depth at one pulse per pixel. These results establish single-shot FLIM as a route to deeper, faster, motion-tolerant, low-photodamage lifetime imaging.

authors.name: Jack Tomkiewicz, Federico Presutti, Tade Marozsak, Jia Zhao, Hatoon Baazim, Hernandez Moura-Silva, Eliezer Calo, Sixian You

papers.title: Multiple spontaneous otoacoustic emissions as a single standing wave unstable to modulation
papers.summary: Spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs) have been interpreted either as cochlear standing waves or as local oscillations of hair cells. Multiple SOAE lines test both views, because each view must explain how the lines coexist. In the standing-wave view, each line is a separate resonance. In the intermodulation view, some lines are distortion products of others. Both explanations assume several independent oscillations. Independent oscillations, however, compete through the saturating cochlear amplifier, and the dominant oscillation suppresses the others. The saturation has another role besides suppression. The saturation also induces an oscillation of the gain at twice the frequency of the oscillation. In lasers, this oscillation of the gain, called the \textit{pump}, creates sidebands. This paper examines whether a cochlear standing wave can pump the gain by itself. A two-dimensional cochlear model with a step in the gain produced a single standing wave. The pump destabilized a pair of lines near the neighboring resonances. The other lines were phase-locked intermodulation products of the main line and the pair. A group of equally spaced SOAEs can thus arise from one self-sustained oscillation. The spacing follows the resonances of the standing wave, and the two explanations can hold together.

authors.name: Yasuki Murakami

papers.title: Horizontal component of the ion drag force in a plasma sheath
papers.summary: The ion drag force is responsible for the underlying physics behind many important phenomena in complex (dusty) plasma, such as void formation, particle alignment in an ion flow, shadow-like attraction between the particles, dust clouds rotation in the presence of a magnetic field etc. In this paper, we investigate the ion drag force acting on particles levitating near the sheath edge of a capacitively coupled discharge in xenon. In particular, we calculate the radial (horizontal) component of the ion drag force directed parallel to the lower electrode above which the particles levitate. The calculation is based on the actual information about the ion flow, which is directly obtained using Laser Induced Fluorescence. The calculated horizontal component is comparable in magnitude to the vertical one, which pushes the particles toward the electrode surface, and is higher than previously expected. This unexpected finding must be taken into account in future research. The very possibility of the measurements we report opens the door for detailed studies of dusty plasma phenomena governed by ions and their flows.

authors.name: S. Jaiswal, S. A. Khrapak, E. M. Aguirre

papers.title: Global saddle selection and exact absolute-instability boundaries for convection in porous media with throughflow
papers.summary: In the Darcy-Prats problem, horizontal throughflow leaves the temporal onset of convection unchanged but raises the heating required for a localized disturbance to grow at a fixed point. The saddle equations give five candidates, but only the saddles reached by deformation of the Fourier contour contribute to the growth. For $Ra>\pi^2$, $Pe>0$ we prove that the same off-axis pair contributes throughout the domain: no Stokes transition can change its contribution. Its growth gives a unique analytic absolute threshold, first reached by the lowest vertical mode. Rescaling transfers the selection to Forchheimer drag, transverse rolls of a power-law fluid, anisotropic permeability, an open upper boundary and a vertical magnetic field. A shift of the same growth function accounts for interphase heat exchange in a model of metallic foam. At prescribed throughflow the threshold increases strictly with either resistance coefficient. In particular, a vertical magnetic field raises the absolute threshold at fixed P\'eclet number. Tabulated thresholds check the reduction. Algebraic elimination gives the boundary polynomial, and frequency recovery selects its physical branch. At the Darcy level the selected saddles trace an arc of the elliptic curve 11a3, a degeneration of a genus-two family at nonzero shifted levels. Series inversion on this arc gives an integer weak-throughflow series and an all-order strong-throughflow expansion. Rational certificates establish the exact convergence radii of both series on the selected sheets.

authors.name: Oleg N. Kirillov

papers.title: An Inverse-Designed Multilayer Selective Emitter for High-Efficiency Thermophotovoltaics
papers.summary: High thermophotovoltaic (TPV) conversion efficiencies have typically relied on photovoltaic cells that reflect sub-bandgap radiation back toward the emitter. Here, we numerically investigate an alternative approach in which spectral selectivity is engineered primarily on the emitter side. We optimize an emitter consisting of 16-layer aperiodic MgO/Si coating on tungsten, for coupling to a GaSb cell with an antireflection coating and an Au mirror. A detailed-balance framework incorporates polarization- and angle-resolved emissivity, multiple reflections, and Auger nonradiative recombination. At an emitter temperature of 1500 K, the optimized structure suppresses 97.1% of the incident-blackbody-equivalent sub-bandgap power at the source; a further 1.9% is returned to the emitter by the cell, leaving 1.0% absorbed parasitically in the cell. The resulting modeled radiative-to-electrical conversion efficiency reaches 47.0%, compared with 30.8% for a SiC emitter paired with the same cell, while maintaining a comparable maximum electrical power density. These findings indicate that emitter-side spectral engineering could substantially relax cell-side photon-recycling requirements and provide significant improvement in TPV conversion.

authors.name: Md Anwar Hosen, Kavyashree Keremane, Bed Poudel, Linxiao Zhu

papers.title: Spatial scaling of heterogeneity transfer from boron concentration to absorbed dose in boron neutron capture therapy
papers.summary: We investigate how the amplitude and spatial correlation length of boron-concentration fluctuations affect the boron-induced absorbed-dose distribution in boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT). The spatial energy-deposition response of alpha particles and lithium nuclei is obtained using Geant4 and convolved with three-dimensional correlated lognormal boron fields under a uniform neutron field. Approximately $90\%$ of the reaction-product energy is deposited within a radius of $6.00~\mu\mathrm{m}$, with a characteristic deposition length of $\ell_B\approx2.05~\mu\mathrm{m}$. Dose heterogeneity increases with both the fluctuation amplitude $H$ and correlation length $\xi$, while the transfer factor $S=CV_D/H$ exhibits an approximate scaling collapse as a function of $\xi/\ell_B$. Analytical Gaussian and lognormal--Gaussian models provide reference predictions for this behavior. At short correlation lengths, the Geant4 response yields a higher transfer factor than a Gaussian response with the same characteristic length, highlighting the influence of the energy-deposition shape on dose smoothing. For $D_{95}$, defined as the dose received by at least $95\%$ of the modeled volume, the relative difference between homogeneous and heterogeneous boron-dose models reaches $(86.62\pm1.07)\%$ at $H=1.2$ and a target ratio $\xi/\ell_B=6$. We show that mean boron concentration alone is insufficient to characterize spatial nonuniformity of the boron-dose component.

authors.name: Roni Muslim, Bidhari Pidhatika, Sutanto Sutanto, Ramacos Fardela, Rio Natanel Wijaya

papers.title: Learning and Generating Time Trajectories of Multidimensional Stochastic Processes
papers.summary: We present a multidimensional statistics-informed neural network (SINN) framework for learning and generating trajectories of multicomponent stochastic processes. SINN is built upon a deterministic recurrent neural network that takes streams of white-noise sequences as input and generates ensembles of stochastic trajectories whose statistical properties match those of the underlying stochastic dynamics. While SINN has been demonstrated for various one-dimensional non-Markovian processes, extending it to multidimensional processes is essential for real-world applications. Here, we present key developments toward this goal. First, because direct estimation of multivariate probability density functions (PDFs) becomes computationally challenging with increasing dimension, we represent joint-distribution information using collections of one-dimensional PDFs constructed from linear combinations of the process components. Second, to accommodate the larger set of statistical objectives required to characterize multidimensional processes, we adopt a self-adaptive loss-balancing strategy that dynamically weights the components of the total loss function. Third, we introduce a reference-normalized validation framework that interprets statistical discrepancies relative to the finite-sample variability between independent target ensembles. We also investigate the role of the input white-noise dimension in SINN performance. We evaluate the proposed approach using a Langevin benchmark based on two coupled Duffing oscillators and further demonstrate its applicability to the Langevin dynamics of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam chain and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of a lattice Lotka-Volterra model. Our results demonstrate that the multidimensional SINN framework provides a practical approach for modeling multidimensional stochastic dynamics.

authors.name: Zihan Xu, Changho Kim, Andy J. Nonaka, Yuanran Zhu

papers.title: A passive, battery-free flexible metasurface for implantable millimetre-wave radar glucose sensing
papers.summary: Continuous glucose monitors (CGM) break the skin barrier and require periodic sensor replacement. We investigated whether a passive, battery-free flexible metasurface, implanted beneath tissue and read by a commercial 60 GHz radar, can track blood glucose levels. The metasurface contained no electronics or reagents. We fitted a conical helix to the in-phase and quadrature radar signals across the frequency sweep and used its mean radius (the spiral radius) as the glucose-dependent feature. We tested glucose concentrations of 25 to 400 mg/dL in saline solution with and without the metasurface, and 196 to 596 mg/dL of total glucose in porcine whole blood beneath ex vivo porcine tissue and in a murine cadaver model with pulsatile blood flow. The metasurface was essential for achieving a monotonic sensor response; in saline, the coefficient of determination ($R^2$) of a logarithmic fit increased from 0.18 without the metasurface to 0.90 with it. In a murine (rat) cadaver model, the signal's spiral radius increased monotonically with glucose concentration despite pulsatile flow ($R^2$ = 0.91), and this monotonic behavior persisted through up to 6 mm of tissue. Although sensitivity decreased at higher glucose levels, each discrete concentration step remained clearly detectable. These results demonstrate that a shallow, passive implant paired with a commercial radar can effectively track blood glucose without requiring onboard electronics or batteries.

authors.name: Kavya Saravanan, Rohini Ramachandran, Jean Pierre Ndabakuranye, Isabelle Shearer, Gursimran Singh, Bobbi Fleiss, Omid Kavehei, Akram Al-Hourani, Francisco J. Tovar Lopez, Margaret Lech, Arman Ahnood

papers.title: Uncertainty evaluation of length measurement by spectral domain interferometry with super-Gaussian windowing
papers.summary: In this study, we evaluate the measurement uncertainty of spectral domain interferometry with super-Gaussian windowing, which has significant potential for interferometer-based dimensional calibration services owing to its simple configuration and nanometer-level precision. A super-luminescent diode (SLD) with a broadband spectrum was used as the light source for high-precision length measurement, and a frequency-calibrated spectrometer captured the spectral interference signal. The length measurement results were compared with a laser displacement interferometer. To evaluate the measurement uncertainty, numerical simulations were performed by considering the intensity-noise level of the CCD in the spectrometer and the frequency-axis uncertainty of the spectrometer. Through a comprehensive uncertainty analysis supported by numerical simulations, the combined standard uncertainty of the measured length was evaluated as sqrt((10 nm)^2 + (9.7x10^(-6)xL)^2). The resulting uncertainty budget provides a metrological basis for extending SLD-based SDI with super-Gaussian windowing toward interferometric dimensional calibration tasks over the millimeter-scale range.

authors.name: Dae Hee Kim, Yoonkwon On, Sunghoon Eom, Chu-Shik Kang, Yoon-Soo Jang

papers.title: Polarization Lifetime as a Design Axis for Task-Adaptive Photonic Reservoir Computing
papers.summary: Photonic time-delayed reservoir computing (TDRC) based on conventional Class B lasers is limited by fragile external cavity mode (ECM) locking dynamics. Here, we show that engineering the polarization lifetime (T$_2$) with the carrier lifetime ($T$) reshapes the topology and stability of TDRC. Comparing four laser classes (Class A, Class B, Class C$_A$, and Class C$_B$), a finite polarization lifetime acts as an intrinsic dynamic filter, dissolving discrete ECM chaos grids into continuous, phase-tolerant operational basins. Information processing capacity (IPC) decomposition further exposes distinct computational profiles: matched Class C$_A$ achieves the highest nonlinear capacity (16.28) and the highest total capacity (19.29), whereas Class A exhibits the highest linear capacity (4.70). A task-dependent reversal governs hardware design: Class A and Class C$_A$ achieve comparable, and the lowest, NRMSE on short-horizon Mackey--Glass prediction (0.0103 and 0.0105, within one standard deviation), while the time-scale-matched Class C$_A$ dominates the higher-dimensional Lorenz (0.0506) and the experimental Santa Fe (0.4251) tasks. Linear-IPC ranking matches Mackey-Glass accuracy; nonlinear-IPC ranking matches the Lorenz exactly and Santa Fe within the mask-to-mask uncertainty. Under realistic quantum noise, resilience is dictated mainly by $T$, not T$_2$: Class A retains the lowest NRMSE (0.47) even at spontaneous emission factor $\beta$ = $10^{-1}$, whereas the long-carrier Class B degrades (0.98). A residual T$_2$-mediated benefit of 20$\%$ persists in the slow-carrier Class C$_B$ (0.78 vs. 0.98). Time-scale engineering thus offers a nuanced design paradigm for optical computing, where optimal hardware is set by the task's time-scale hierarchy rather than a universal figure of merit.

authors.name: Tao Wang, Kathy L\"udge

papers.title: Sign-switchable and tunable macroscopic curvature of liquid jets by microscopic laser-induced cavitation
papers.summary: Localized forcing of liquid jets can trigger Rayleigh-Plateau breakup at low perturbation amplitudes or explosive fragmentation at high amplitudes, while controlled bending in the intermediate regime has remained unexplored. We show that femtosecond-laser-induced cavitation, seeded at the interface of a 100 micrometre-diameter water jet, produces a selectable curvature in 0.4-1 mm long segments. Cavitation rupturing at the liquid-air interface drives fast outward jetting and induces a slower recoil on the opposite boundary, which evolves on the capillary-inertial timescale and results in curving of the liquid segment. The curvature is governed by three laser parameters. Off-axis laser illumination on the jet shifts the refractive caustics and redistributes energy deposition between the front and rear interfaces. The resulting recoil imbalance determines the curvature sign, with a straight configuration in the balanced case. Laser energy offers additional control over the recoil impulse via plasma defocusing and nonlinear absorption in the liquid jet, where the response is bounded by axisymmetric deformation at low energy and explosive vaporization at high energy. Repetition rate sets the spacing between successive cavitation events and hence the length of the bent segment. Curvature extends across the segment for lengths of 6-10 jet diameters; shorter segments undergo Rayleigh-Plateau breakup, whereas longer ones bend mainly near their retracting ends. Our results offer a platform for optofluidic control of switchable and tunable macroscopic curvature in flowing liquid jets.

authors.name: Sourabh Singh, S. Sree Harsha, Prashant Kumar Singh

papers.title: Antihelical Edge States in Photonic Metacrystals
papers.summary: Antihelical edge states represent a gapless form of boundary transport in which modes with opposite spin counterpropagate along a given boundary, while modes sharing the same spin propagate in the same direction on opposite boundaries. Here we show that such states arise naturally within a modified Kane-Mele framework realized in an electromagnetic-dual photonic metacrystal with staggered bianisotropy. Reversing the spin-dependent next-nearest-neighbor coupling on one sublattice reorganizes the bulk spectrum into a spin-polarized Dirac semimetal characterized by spin-dependent energy shifts of the Dirac cones rather than a bulk gap. This bulk reorganization generates tilted edge-mode dispersions in zigzag ribbons and gives rise to antihelical edge transport coexisting with bulk states. Full-wave simulations confirm the corresponding bulk and edge behaviors. Extending the analysis to finite geometries, simulations further reveal discrete corner-localized modes. A realistic design based on split-ring metaatoms is proposed to realize the required staggered bianisotropy and spin-dependent energy shifts of the Dirac cones. Furthermore, we show that the tensorial freedom of the bianisotropic constitutive relations enables continuous manipulation of the electromagnetic pseudospin basis while preserving the antihelical boundary transport. These results provide a practical route for engineering unconventional gapless boundary transport in photonic Dirac systems.

authors.name: Ke-Yi Zeng, Zi-Xuan Gao, Zhou Zhou, Xiao-Dong Chen, Jian-Wen Dong

papers.title: A Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Complete TE/TM Separability in Fully Anisotropic Waveguides
papers.summary: A necessary and sufficient condition is established for complete transverse-electric/transverse-magnetic (TE/TM) separability in waveguides homogeneously filled with a fully anisotropic and lossless medium. The permittivity and permeability tensors are Hermitian positive-definite and may contain nonzero transverse--longitudinal coupling terms. Complete TE/TM separation occurs if and only if the transverse permeability block is proportional to the transpose of the transverse permittivity block and the corresponding transverse--longitudinal coupling vectors satisfy the same proportionality relation after complex conjugation. The longitudinal constitutive entries remain independent apart from positive definiteness. The condition is derived directly from the source-free Maxwell equations, and independent analyses of the TE and TM modes lead to the same material relation. Since no boundary condition enters the derivation, the criterion is independent of the boundary type. Full-vector waveguide mode analyses using our in-house programs for perfect-electric-conductor and Bloch-periodic waveguides, with material tensors satisfying and violating the condition, agree with the theoretical results.

authors.name: Wei Jiang, Jie Liu

papers.title: Reactive feedback for suppression of the periodic transient beam loading effect in storage rings: theory and simulations
papers.summary: In fourth-generation synchrotron light sources, harmonic cavities are often employed for bunch lengthening. The reduced longitudinal focusing, combined with high total $R/Q$ of these cavities, can make the beam susceptible to the periodic transient beam loading (PTBL) effect, a multibunch instability characterized by slow oscillations in bunch centroids and lengths and by its resistance to conventional feedback damping. In this work, building on a recent proposal of applying reactive feedback to control the PTBL effect, we developed a frequency-domain theoretical model, including the feedback voltage in the linearized Vlasov equation to derive a Lebedev equation modified by the feedback transfer function. The reactive feedback was also implemented in the time domain in the macroparticle tracking code \texttt{STABLE}. The methods were applied to the parameters of the double-rf system of the MAX IV storage ring. Both approaches show that, above a threshold gain, an idealized pure reactive feedback is able to suppress the PTBL effect, with good agreement between theory and simulations across beam currents and $R/Q$ values. Realistic hardware limitations were included in the analysis, determining the limits for feedback gain, latency, and bandwidth, which are compatible with existing bunch-by-bunch feedback systems. Using the HALF storage ring parameters, the semi-analytical results indicate that the reactive feedback can be extended to suppress the PTBL effect in triple-rf systems, albeit at higher threshold gains than for double-rf systems.

authors.name: PeiZhi Fang, Murilo B. Alves, Hongjuan Yao, Shuxin Zheng, Chuanxiang Tang

papers.title: Near-wall sedimentation of short cylinders at low Reynolds numbers: Translational and angular velocity models and experimental validation
papers.summary: The sedimentation of short cylinders near rigid walls involves coupled translational and rotational motion, for which readily applicable kinematic descriptions remain limited. In this study, theoretical expressions for the translational and angular velocities were derived by combining slender-body theory, semi-empirical finite-aspect-ratio corrections, and hydrodynamic descriptions of fluid inertia and wall effects. The resulting expressions were assessed through time-resolved sedimentation experiments with rigid cylinders of mean aspect ratios $\bar{\chi}\approx3.8$--$5.8$ in a rectangular duct at particle Reynolds numbers of $Re_{\mathrm P}\approx O(10^{-1})$. The experiments revealed distinct near-wall trajectories, including non-contact glancing motion and contact-induced flipping. For glancing trajectories, the predicted translational and angular velocities reproduced the principal features of the measured kinematics, with good qualitative and, over substantial parts of the trajectories, quantitative agreement. The comparisons also identified different ranges of applicability for the investigated wall corrections and showed that wall-induced effects dominated the angular velocity under the conditions studied. The resulting, experimentally validated expressions provide readily applicable estimates of the instantaneous translational and angular velocities of short cylinders near rigid walls and a reference for investigating additional influences on their sedimentation dynamics, including lower Reynolds numbers and particle or wall elasticity.

authors.name: Isabell Noichl, Clarissa Sch\"onecker

papers.title: Spectral dependence of Berry phase and topological bound states in the continuum in M\"obius resonators
papers.summary: The M\"obius strip and the bulk M\"obius resonator are of great interest to specialists in optics, acoustics, and quantum physics. Despite the apparent simplicity of the object and numerous publications, the M\"obius resonator, like a magic box, still holds many surprises. Here, we demonstrate experimentally, theoretically and with a simple illustrative example that in a "thin" M\"obius resonator with an odd number of twists, the longitudinal wavenumber is determined by the additional phase shift {\pi} (traditionally called the geometrical Berry phase) only if the total transverse index of the photonic mode is odd. For an even index, the Berry phase is zero. We also discovered "topological" quasi-bound states in the continuum in M\"obius resonators with a square cross-section; they differ from "ordinary" ones by the exchange of azimuthal indices of the interfering modes in the anti-crossing region. Finally, we demonstrate an example of resonant topology by determining the dependence of the Berry phase on the M\"obius resonator geometry based on the frequency difference between the eigenmodes of planar ring resonators and those of M\"obius resonators. The discovered effects significantly expand our knowledge of the topology of single resonators and promise new practical applications.

authors.name: Mikhail E. Bochkarev, Timur Z. Seidov, Nikolay S. Solodovchenko, Kirill B. Samusev, Mikhail F. Limonov

papers.title: Flow structure, heat transport, and dissipation in vertical-field magnetoconvection at similar Reynolds numbers
papers.summary: We employ direct numerical simulations to investigate the effect of a vertical magnetic field on the flow structures, heat transport, and dissipation rates in Rayleigh--B\'enard convection of a low-Prandtl-number fluid ($\mathrm{Pr} = 0.025$) at an approximately fixed Reynolds number ($\mathrm{Re} \approx 880$), maintained by adjusting the Rayleigh number to compensate for the Lorentz force. As the Hartmann number increases, the flow becomes more anisotropic, which strengthens the positive convective heat fluxes relative to the negative ones and thereby raises the Nusselt number, accompanied by a thinning of the thermal boundary layers. The total viscous and thermal dissipation rates are dominated by the boundary layers, whereas the total magnetic dissipation rate is dominated by the bulk. With increasing Hartmann number, the boundary-layer fraction of the viscous and magnetic dissipation rates increases, whereas that of the thermal dissipation computed from the temperature fluctuations decreases, owing to the suppression of temperature fluctuations near the boundary layers. The dissipation rates deviate from log-normality and are well described by stretched exponential distributions, whose tails become more extended with increasing Hartmann number.

authors.name: Md Shahid Raza, Akanksha Bhardwaj, Shashwat Bhattacharya

papers.title: ADfiRe: An empirical- and CFD-informed advection-diffusion-reaction thermal model for wildfire spread
papers.summary: Real-time wildfire forecasting requires a trade-off between rapid yet physically relevant models and high fidelity but computationally costly models of flame spread over heterogeneous, multiphase solid fuel. The present study introduces ADfiRe, a hybrid framework that integrates empirical correlations and CFD-informed parameterizations into a physics-based advection-diffusion-reaction (ADR) formulation. The key features of ADfiRe are the use of established fuel databases, the capacity to handle multiple fuels, and a methodology to capture the effect of arbitrary topography. Furthermore, it includes the effect of flame tilting due to wind, thus accounting for the differences between plume- and wind-dominated fire propagation. ADfiRe resolves explicitly the coupled thermochemical degradation as well as heat and mass transport mechanisms of the advancing fire front. The wind field is modeled based on an appropriately defined Byram number. The model is validated against five well-documented experimental field-scale fires in Mediterranean shrublands, showing quantitative agreement with key metrics such as the rate of spread (ROS) and the fireline intensity, through a two-stage, Arrhenius-based heterogeneous reaction scheme coupling solid-fuel pyrolysis and oxygen-limited char/volatile combustion.

authors.name: Konstantinos Vogiatzoglou, Nikolaos Sdiros, Costas Papadimitriou, Konstantinos Ampountolas, Petros Koumoutsakos, Vasilis Bontozoglou

papers.title: Symmerty-Engineered Moire Metasurface for Multibeam Control
papers.summary: Moir\'e metasurfaces offer a versatile platform for wavefront engineering through the relative rotation of periodic structures. Despite extensive demonstrations of continuous beam steering, the physical mechanisms governing beam multiplicity remain poorly understood, hindering the systematic design of multibeam radiation states. Here, we establish a predictive framework for engineering beam multiplicity in reflective moir\'e metasurfaces based on the dominant Fourier coefficients of their constituent patterns. We reveal that the rotational symmetry of these Fourier components in reciprocal space fully determines the symmetry of the resulting moir\'e unit cell and, consequently, its radiation characteristics. By further incorporating their phase information, both beam multiplicity and steering trajectories can be accurately predicted. We demonstrate this approach using reflective moir\'e metasurfaces constructed from patterns with p6m, p3m1, and p4m plane-group symmetries, achieving one-, two-, three-, four-, and six-beam radiation states with continuously tunable steering trajectories. Beyond symmetry-based design, we identify two additional degrees of freedom for beam multiplicity control. Selecting different rotation centers reshapes the phase distributions of the dominant Fourier coefficients, enabling further manipulation of beam multiplicity and spatial arrangement, while varying the relative twist angle alters the pairing of Fourier components, inducing transitions between distinct beam multiplicities. These findings establish a systematic framework for versatile and reconfigurable multibeam wavefront engineering.

authors.name: Yu Chen, Lan Ke, Shaojie Ma, Shuo Liu

papers.title: Optical Representation Neural Networks Enabled by Weakly Supervised Learning
papers.summary: Diffractive optical neural networks (ONNs) show remarkable promise in high-speed and energy-efficient optical computing. However, most existing ONNs are optimized to reproduce predefined output intensity distributions, with the desired optical responses explicitly specified before training. Here, we introduce optical representation neural networks (ORNNs) enabled by coarse-grained weak supervision. Using handwritten Devanagari, Arabic, and English characters as three semantic groups, a modified contrastive objective encourages samples from the same script to cluster into similar optical representations. Remarkably, ORNNs improve the classification accuracy by approximately 9% over conventional supervised ONNs, while requiring only around 18% of the training steps to reach a stable test accuracy of 84.5%. These features can be selectively interpreted using corresponding semantic decoders. Building on this concept, we further realized semantic optical encryption with electronic neural network (ENN) decryption using experimentally acquired representations from a single-layer diffractive network fabricated by two-photon polymerization lithography (TPL). Here, we combine information from different scripts into a mixed optical ciphertext that is then first optically classified before being decrypted with a matched ENN. This work broadens the training paradigm of ONNs by coupling upstream optical representation learning with downstream task-specific decoding, opening new avenues for optical information processing.

authors.name: Bochang Wu, Cheng-Feng Pan, Xuhao Luo, John You En Chan, Shutao Zhang, Zhenchao Liu, Hao Wang, Deepshikha Arora, Nur Qalishah Adanan, Ho Soon Yee, Lei Chen, Hongtao Wang, Wang Zhang, Cheng-Wei Qiu, Joel K. W. Yang

papers.title: Finite-Larmor-radius vortex interaction from {\delta}f to full-f gyrofluid dynamics
papers.summary: We study finite-size electrostatic gyrofluid vortex pairs in a two-dimensional isothermal model, focusing on finite-Larmor-radius effects and the transition from local perturbative to finite-amplitude full-distribution dynamics. An effective response kernel based on Pad\'e ion gyroaveraging regularizes the short-range Euler interaction on the Larmor-radius scale while preserving its logarithmic far field, yielding a finite- core prediction for the orbital frequency. Local-model scans show that increasing the ion temperature relative to the electron temperature enhances gyrospinning and filamentation and drives a separation-dependent transition from merger to long-lived co-rotation. Long-wavelength simulations reproduce the predicted finite-Larmor- radius-induced dip in orbital angular frequency, corresponding to a pronounced slowdown of the vortex-pair rotation. For the full-distribution regime, we introduce a quasi-neutrality-consistent initialization that reconstructs the ion gyrocenter density from prescribed electron density and electrostatic potential. It recovers the local limit at small amplitude, whereas finite-amplitude simulations reveal additional mean-density polarization vorticity, delayed or arrested merger, and a loss of density- vorticity sign symmetry already in the cold-ion full-f system. An independent sign scan of density and vorticity then shows how this nonlinear NOB asymmetry combines with the local warm-ion FLR symmetry breaking identified in earlier {\delta}f vortex studies; for warm ions, Pad\'e-based arbitrary-wavelength NOB and NOB+LWL polarization additionally produce distinct morphologies and trajectories. These results demonstrate that nonlinear density-dependent polarization and FLR physics form separate but coupled mechanisms that can qualitatively alter elementary vortex interactions in two-dimensional gyrofluid dynamics.

authors.name: Manuel Rinner, Franz Ferdinand Locker, Markus Held, Alexander Kendl

papers.title: Experimental characterization of magnetic multipole fields up to octupole order using smartphone magnetometry
papers.summary: The multipole expansion is one of the organising ideas of electromagnetism: far from a localised source the field is dominated by its lowest non-vanishing moment, and each successive order decays one power of the distance faster. Although the dipole field is routinely measured in introductory laboratories, higher orders are seldom explored experimentally, because the fields are weak, decay very rapidly and require careful positioning. Here we show that with four identical neodymium cube magnets, a sheet of graph paper and the magnetometer of a smartphone, first-year students can build and characterise not one but three distinct magnetic octupoles (linear, planar and `square' arrangements), together with the dipole and the two quadrupoles that serve as reference. A simple notation and a compact set of formulae, based on the spatial Cartesian moments $M_{pq}=\sum_k m_k x_k^p z_k^q$ of the array, predict which field component survives at each measuring position and how it decays. The measured exponents are $n\simeq 3$, $4$ and $5$ for dipole, quadrupole and octupole arrangements, and the measured prefactors show fair quantitative consistency with the independently determined dipole moment of the magnets once nominal geometry and spacer effects are taken into account. We discuss the systematic effects that limit the octupole measurements (higher-order terms at short distance, residual lower-order moments at long distance, the location of the sensor inside the phone) and the ways in which the activity can be extended. The experiment generalises and unifies previous smartphone-based measurements of dipoles, linear quadrupoles and a linear octupole.

authors.name: Mart\'{\i}n Monteiro, Cecilia Stari, Arturo C. Marti, Enrique Arribas, Isabel Escobar, Raquel Ramirez-Vazquez, Augusto Bel\'endez

papers.title: Compressible gas flow through porous media under forced pressure and fluxes: compressibility number and pressure curvature
papers.summary: Gas compressibility induces a nonlinear relationship between boundary forcing and pressure evolution in porous media. This matters in operations and experiments where inlet pressure, volumetric flux or mass flux is controlled, as each forcing produces a distinct transient approach to steady state. We analyze this systematically for isothermal gas flow, using the porous medium equation (PME), nondimensionalized in terms of a Peclet-type number $\Pi$ that compares the time scales of gas flow and pressure diffusion and measures the steady flow compression. At steady state, increasing $\Pi$ leads to a boundary layer near the outlet, of width $\sim\Pi^{-1}$, where the velocity and flow expansion scale as $\Pi$ and $\Pi^2$, respectively. Since $\Pi$ fixes the steady compression for all three inlet conditions, their transients can be compared directly. We derive a semi-analytical perturbation series in $\beta=2\Pi/(1+2\Pi)<1$, valid for the three inlet conditions, which remains convergent at large $\Pi$. Numerical solutions for $10^{-2}\leq\Pi\leq10^3$ show that the effective pressure-squared diffusivity plateaus at boundary-condition-dependent values for $\Pi\ll1$, and scales as $\Pi^{1/2}$ for $\Pi\gg1$, explained by the slowest eigenmode of the linearized PME about its steady state. To resolve local flow compression, we introduce the pressure curvature, $\kappa=\nabla^2 p$, and interpret its evolution through a nonlinear advection-diffusion-reaction equation. Curvature fields reveal localized compression pulses that migrate downstream and dissipate as the system relaxes, while curvature moments highlight a $\Pi$-dependent crossover from compression- to expansion-dominated transients. Applications to gas chromatography and underground hydrogen storage are illustrated.

authors.name: A. F. Visentini, J. J. Hidalgo, M. Dentz

papers.title: Mechanical acclimation of bacterial growth and division across generations
papers.summary: Bacteria frequently encounter mechanical confinement in natural and engineered environments, yet how an abrupt change in mechanical conditions reorganizes growth and division across generations remains poorly understood. Using single-cell time-lapse microscopy, we tracked Escherichia coli across generations following transfer from liquid culture to glass-attached or glass-gel-confined conditions. This mechanical confinement causes an immediate reduction in elongation rate, followed by a multi-generational mechanical acclimation process whose dynamics depend systematically on confinement strength. During this relaxation, division behavior becomes more heterogeneous and cells temporarily depart from canonical adder-like size regulation, exhibiting timer-like correlation signatures. Using a stochastic cell-cycle model that resolves the generation-dependent correlation signatures of different size-control strategies, we show that changes in elongation rate alone cannot account for the observed transition in growth-division coordination. Despite this transient reorganization, the birth-size distribution remains bounded and largely preserves its shape throughout acclimation. Notably, adder-like regulation is restored before the elongation rate fully recovers, revealing distinct relaxation timescales for growth and size-control dynamics. These results establish bacterial size control under mechanical confinement as a dynamical nonequilibrium process in which growth and division can transiently reorganize while global size homeostasis is maintained.

authors.name: Chenyu Jin, G. H. Philipp Nguyen, Ren\'e Wittmann, Hartmut L\"owen, Anupam Sengupta

papers.title: Commercial AlGaAs diodes provide simplified feedback for adaptive femtosecond pulse compression
papers.summary: Maintaining high peak power in ultrashort laser pulses is essential for efficient nonlinear interactions, particularly in multiphoton microscopy. Dispersion introduced by optical components broadens these pulses and degrades their peak power, thus motivating adaptive pulse compression guided by pulse-width-dependent feedback. However, the conventional second-harmonic generation feedback requires a nonlinear crystal, spectral filtering, and careful optical alignment. Here, we investigate commercially available AlGaAs laser and light-emitting diodes as alternative two-photon absorption feedback sensors. Their photocurrent exhibits a quadratic dependence on average optical power and inverse dependence on pulse duration, which is consistent with the analytical model predicting maximum response for the shortest, single-peaked pulse. Both devices generated a measurable photocurrent at sub-milliwatt average power levels and showed a weaker polarization dependence than second-harmonic-generation-based solution. All three feedback methods achieved comparable mean compressed pulse durations of 210-228 fs. These results demonstrate effective adaptive pulse compression with a substantially simpler feedback.

authors.name: Patrycja H. Wysowska, Adrian Chlebowski, Lukasz A. Sterczewski, Jakub Bogus{\l}awski

papers.title: Scan-specific k-space interpolation using deep Koopman autoencoders
papers.summary: Purpose: To develop a scan-specific, interpretable k-space interpolation technique for the reconstruction of accelerated MRI data. Methods: A deep Koopman autoencoder for nonlinear k-space interpolation was developed consisting of an encoder, a linear layer for interpolation and a decoder. The resulting network is implemented using mean square error loss function on k-space neighbourhoods derived from the autocalibration signals (ACS), combining a prediction loss and an autoencoding loss. The approach was compared to GRAPPA and RAKI in 281 retrospectively undersampled brain datasets, using quantitative reconstruction metrics. In a subset of 52 randomly selected images, a clinical reader study compared the proposed approach and RAKI in a forced choice scenario and using a five-point ordinal scoring, assessing sharpness, SNR, aliasing and overall image quality. Additionally, the effect of varying parameters such as the number of autocalibration signals, the contribution of the autoencoding loss, the kernel size, and the latent space dimension for the proposed technique was studied. Results: The proposed approach showed improved quantitative metrics compared to GRAPPA and RAKI. Visually, the method showed higher resilience to noise amplification and improved preservation of sharp details. In the clinical reader study, the proposed approach was preferred overall to RAKI and yielded higher scores than GRAPPA and RAKI. The proposed method showed robustness to parameter variations. Conclusion: Deep Learning based k-space interpolation can be achieved using a Koopman autoencoder for k-space neighbourhoods. Keywords: Parallel imaging, Koopman autoencoder, nonlinear mapping, k-space interpolation, deep learning reconstruction

authors.name: Wassim Ben Salah, Jon Cleary, Sarah McElroy, Raphael Tomi-Tricot, Antoine Naegel, Sebastien Ourselin, Jonathan Shapey, Christos Bergeles, Radhouene Neji

papers.title: CGTransformer: A Topology-Aware Autoregressive Framework for Crystal Generation and Inverse Design
papers.summary: Autoregressive language models offer a unified route to crystal generation and inverse design, but their performance depends on how periodic structures are serialized. Symmetry equivalent and closely related crystals can receive different atomic orders under coordinate-based serialization, introducing variability unrelated to their structural connectivity. Here, we present CGTransformer (Crystal Graph Transformer), an autoregressive generative framework that addresses this challenge via a graph-embedded sorting strategy. Using quotientgraph topology and barycentric embeddings, Element Symmetry Graph (ESG) converts periodic crystal networks into topology-guided one-dimensional sequences that retain key local and symmetry-related structural information. CGTransformer achieves high generation validity and the highest single shot crystal structure prediction (CSP) match rate among the compared MP-20 baselines (63.24%), while same backbone comparisons show improved structure recovery over coordinate-based ordering. Furthermore, we demonstrate property-conditioned inverse design for wide-bandgap semiconductors, where ESG achieves a much higher stable, unique and novel (S.U.N.) rate and stronger target-property alignment than the coordinate-based baseline. These results establish topology-guided sequence construction as an effective route to improving crystal generation and property-directed design at fixed model capacity.

authors.name: Zhennan Zhang, Shaobo Yu, Haoting Zhang, Yu Han, Zhiyue Guo, Junjie Wang, Hao Gao, Jian Sun

papers.title: A Multiscale Analysis of an Interplanetary Shock from IMAP, SOLAR-1, and the L1 Constellation to Earth
papers.summary: Collisionless shocks are primary sites of particle acceleration throughout the Universe. Transient, mesoscale structures forming around these shocks influence their energy conversion efficiency, yet remain poorly observed at interplanetary (IP) shocks: spacecraft sample the shock transition briefly, and single-point measurements cannot disentangle temporal evolution from spatial structure. Here, we examine a fast, CME-driven IP shock of 2026 January 19, observed by IMAP, SOLAR-1, Wind, ACE, DSCOVR, and Aditya-L1 at L1 and by ARTEMIS and MMS near Earth, to determine its spatial and temporal structure. At MHD scales, a pre-existing solar wind flux tube is overtaken by the shock as it crosses the L1 fleet. This inflates the apparent magnetic compression ratio far beyond the ideal strong-shock limit of 4, showing that upstream and downstream intervals can sample different plasma and bias single-spacecraft estimates. At kinetic scales, IMAP and SOLAR-1, separated by only $\sim$7 $R_E$ ($\sim$340 ion inertial lengths), sample the same foreshock yet record localized structures that differ measurably; these are the first candidate signatures of large-scale foreshock transients at an IP shock. Further upstream, shocklets appear hundreds of $R_E$ ahead of the shock, consistent with steepening of ambient solar wind waves. Near Earth, the shock-to-flux-tube arrival lag increases to approximately six minutes, corresponding to a nominal sheath extension of $\sim$50 $R_E$, indicating sheath expansion over $\sim$200 $R_E$ of propagation. Together, these results show that the IP shock, its foreshock, and its sheath evolve across multiple scales from L1 to Earth, underscoring the need for multipoint measurements to resolve the underlying processes.

authors.name: Savvas Raptis, Drew L. Turner, Domenico Trotta, Vassilis Angelopoulos, James L. Burch, Dibyendu Chakrabarty, Eric Christian, Christina M. S. Cohen, Manuel E. Cuesta, Maher A. Dayeh, Robert W. Ebert, Hameedullah A. Farooki, Joe Giacalone, Matina Gkioulidou, Timothy Horbury, Immanuel C. Jebaraj, David J. McComas, Connor O'Brien, Srikar Paavan Tadepalli, Jamie S. Rankin, K. Sankarasubramanian, Nathan Schwadron, Bishwas L. Shrestha, Adam Szabo, Roy Torbert, Dimitrios Vassiliadis, Sarah Vines, Hanying Wei, Lynn B. Wilson III, Gary P. Zank, Lingling Zhao

papers.title: Bond Anharmonicity in a Caged Molecule Probed by Vibronic Core Spectroscopy
papers.summary: X-ray absorption spectroscopy and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering at the nitrogen K-edge show that the N$\equiv$N bond in N$_2$@C$_{60}$ is substantially more anharmonic than in free N$_2$, with the ground-state ($X^1\Sigma_g^+$) anharmonic constant $\hbar\omega_e x_e$ a factor of two larger ($3.8\pm0.3$~meV versus $\sim 1.8$~meV) despite an essentially unchanged harmonic frequency. The same enhancement is found across all three vibronic potentials accessible to the experiment---the electronic ground state, the core-excited intermediate state, and the spectator-decay final state---pointing to a common origin rather than an effect specific to one electronic configuration. High-level coupled-cluster calculations of the N$_2$@C$_{60}$ potential energy surface, however, find no significant change in anharmonicity upon encapsulation, ruling out a simple static distortion of the N$\equiv$N bonding potential by the fullerene cage. We propose instead that the dramatic increase in $\hbar\omega_e x_e$ above the gas-phase value -- which, taken literally, would imply an unphysical halving of the N$_2$ dissociation energy - reflects the breakdown of the single-molecule Morse description, as previously invoked to explain anomalous anharmonicities in N$_2$ clusters, and supported by the observation of shifts in the fullerene host's Raman modes.

authors.name: Connor J. B. Fields, Bang Huynh, Filipe Junqueira, Tyler James, Aleksandra Foerster, Ilya Popov, James Kerfoot, Graham Rance, Victor Por\'ee, Alessandro Nicolaou, David Duncan, Tien-Lin Lee, Gabriela Hoffman, Mark C. Walkey, Elizabeth S. Marsden, Malcolm H. Levitt, Richard J. Whitby, Michael W. George, Elena Besley, Brian Kiraly, James O'Shea, Philip Moriarty

papers.title: Radiation in relativistic plasmas via particle simulations
papers.summary: We investigate radiation in relativistic electron-proton isotropic plasmas using molecular dynamics, with velocity-dependent inertia, retarded interactions, and quantum-corrected pair potentials. Radiation spectra from the Li\'enard-Wiechert fields agree with analytical models. Successive scattering events suppress bremsstrahlung even at weak coupling, while jitter radiation becomes comparable at higher coupling for all resolved frequencies. This first-principles framework will help develop radiation models for suppression and field effects that are inaccessible in typical particle-in-cell methods.

authors.name: Efstratios M. Kritikos, Pontus Svensson, Daniel Plummer, Brian Reville, Bob Bingham, Gianluca Gregori

papers.title: Active flow control based on topological data analysis and a DMDc reduced-order model for drag reduction
papers.summary: Controlling and reducing undesirable vortical structures in unsteady flows is a major issue in aerodynamics. This paper presents an active control methodology that combines topological data analysis (TDA) through persistence diagrams, a reduced-order model based on dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc) and receding-horizon model predictive control (MPC). Vortices are detected and characterised by the persistence diagram of the absolute value of the vorticity, which makes it possible to define a target flow in which only the useful vortices are retained. This target flow is computed offline in the reduced space by gradient descent, the derivative of a persistence diagram being defined through a parametrisation of the space of diagrams. The control loop then reduces to a small-dimensional convex quadratic program, whose construction we detail and whose cost we compare with that of an approach that places the diagrams directly in the cost function. The approach is applied numerically to the flow around an oscillating aircraft wing for seven vibration frequencies, and yields a mean reduction of the drag coefficient while preserving the main vortices.

authors.name: Constantini Mbangue Lobe Yiphta, Dina Razafindralandy

papers.title: Potential Flow, Stress, and Straightness in Flow Matching: Euler Error on Gaussian-Mixture Targets
papers.summary: In linear flow matching, coupling straightness measures conditional displacement variance. The conditional covariance gives a kinetic stress in the Jeans balance. The virial identity relates the mean trace of the covariance to a radial moment of acceleration. Euler error also depends on how the flow propagates acceleration. On constructed Gaussian-mixture targets, closed-form couplings with matched straightness yield different median Euler errors. Learned fields from fresh minibatch assignments also yield different Euler errors from their partners at matched estimated straightness. The leading Euler coefficient accounts for more of the error variation than straightness in these experiments. We relate the additive-noise characterization of isotropic Gaussian sources to potential flow. A gradient constraint reduces velocity error on the independent isotropic Gaussian example and increases it on two examples with rotational exact fields.

authors.name: Zijian Liu, Julian Olszewski, Jie Xu

papers.title: The directions of science: How we search the unknown
papers.summary: Science is producing knowledge at unprecedented scale, while artificial intelligence promises to accelerate the generation of hypotheses, analyses, and scientific outputs further. Yet increasing the volume of research does not necessarily expand the range of directions science effectively explores. We argue that science can be understood as a collective search process in which finite resources are allocated across an evolving space of possible research trajectories. Careers, funding, organization, publication, attention, and technology act as interacting selection mechanisms that shape this allocation. This Perspective distinguishes the visible diversity of scientific activity from its effective diversity: apparently different researchers, institutions, or projects need not provide genuinely different routes of exploration or evaluation. Our principal contribution is to introduce cross-stage dependence, which occurs when selection processes operating at different stages of science are not fully independent in the grounds through which they favour scientific trajectories. We hypothesize that, under uncertainty, repeated filtering through overlapping criteria, information, prior selections, or technological infrastructure can reduce the capacity of science to maintain plausible alternatives and redirect effort when evidence changes their relative promise. Artificial intelligence makes this problem increasingly consequential because it can simultaneously expand scientific search capacity and participate across multiple stages of production and selection. The challenge is therefore not simply to produce more knowledge, but to preserve sufficiently distinct routes of exploration, verification and correction while retaining the ability to change direction.

authors.name: Nicola Cinardi

papers.title: Enhanced Hyperspectral Nano-FTIR Imaging by Neural-Network-Based Processing of Multiple Signal Harmonics
papers.summary: Nano-FTIR spectroscopy combines infrared spectroscopy with nanometer-scale spatial resolution and enables hyperspectral nanoimaging. However, quantitative measurements typically rely on higher-harmonic near-field signals, which are largely background-free but suffer from low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Lower harmonics provide substantially higher SNR but contain significant background contributions that distort the near-field response and hinder quantitative analysis. Here, we introduce a cross-harmonic neural network (CHNN) that exploits the complementary information encoded in multiple harmonic channels to denoise third-harmonic hyperspectral data. Trained directly on experimental nano-FTIR datasets, the CHNN uses first- and second-harmonic spectra to improve the SNR of the third-harmonic response. Applied to a PMMA/PS polymer blend, it substantially reduces noise while preserving spectral features and nanoscale spatial contrast. Compared with conventional single-harmonic denoising using an autoencoder, the CHNN achieves superior noise suppression. These results demonstrate the potential of lower-harmonic signals for improving hyperspectral nano-FTIR imaging without increasing acquisition time.

authors.name: Pablo Calvo-Barl\'es, Sergio G. Rodrigo, Luis Mart\'in-Moreno, Martin Schnell, Rainer Hillenbrand

papers.title: Generation of low-frequency flows by shear Alfv\'en waves in magnetohydrodynamics
papers.summary: Coherently forced, weak reduced-magnetohydrodynamic turbulence is studied in a uniform plasma to investigate the long-term nonlinear interactions of shear Alfv\'en waves. The 'pump waves' are chosen to model toroidal Alfv\'en eigenmodes, excited by suprathermal particles in magnetic fusion devices. Modes with zero frequency and no variation along the magnetic field are generated nonlinearly; these produce analogues of zonal flows and currents in a gradient-free system. This indicates that quasistationary flows can be generated by shear Alfv\'en waves in systems simpler than those previously considered, which relied on compressibility, finite-Larmor-radius effects, or complex geometry. The saturated amplitudes of the modes are found analytically and numerically as a function of pump-wave amplitude. This facilitates estimates of the critical amplitude above which toroidal Alfv\'en eigenmodes can generate sufficiently strong zonal flows to suppress microturbulence in the core of magnetic fusion devices. This threshold corresponds to magnetic fluctuations whose amplitude, relative to the background field, is comparable to $\rho_{\star i}$, the ion Larmor radius normalised to the minor radius of the device.

authors.name: James M. Edmiston, Michael Fitzgerald, Juan Ruiz Ruiz, Dmitri A. Uzdensky, Alexander A. Schekochihin

papers.title: Tunable Hybridization of Whispering Gallery Modes in High-Index Photonic Molecules
papers.summary: Photonic molecules formed by coupled dielectric microresonators provide a platform for controlling collective optical modes, yet the interplay between molecular topology, resonator detuning, and dielectric environment in determining their spectral response remains insufficiently quantified. Here, we systematically quantify the evolution of Whispering Gallery Mode (WGM) hybridization in high-index TiO$_2$ and perovskite coated TiO$_2$ microresonators with molecular topology, and establish the corresponding effective inter-cavity coupling using a combined numerical and analytical analysis. We further show that perovskite-shell incorporation provides a diameter and thickness-dependent modification of the effective coupling, producing a non-monotonic response rather than a uniform suppression of coupling. Despite the resulting closely spaced hybridized resonances in the high-index perovskite environment, the supermodes remain spectrally resolvable, with $Q$-factor of order \(10^3\) for representative modes. The observed spectral splitting is quantitatively related to the effective inter-cavity coupling strengths, revealing a non-monotonic coupling response to perovskite-shell incorporation that depends on resonator size and shell thickness. These results establish molecular topology and dielectric environment as distinct parameters for controlling WGM hybridization, inter-cavity coupling, and spectral response, providing a basis for the design of coupled resonator systems for applications in optical sensing, filtering, switching, and other resonant photonic devices.

authors.name: Ayusmin Panda, Birabar Ranjit Kumar Nanda

papers.title: The effect of particle shape on sunlight exposure in a wind-driven free-surface flow
papers.summary: We investigate how nonspherical marine particles, such as microplastics, phytoplankton, and ice, are exposed to sunlight near the water surface in wind-driven surface boundary layer conditions. We measure the depth and orientation of these particles in a laboratory wind-wave tank, then use this data to model how much sunlight the particles would be exposed to in an aquatic environment. In particular, we explore how their orientation affects their sunlight exposure in these conditions, since most studies to date do not account for orientation, turbulent shear flow, and wind-waves at the water surface. We find that in all cases, particles prefer certain orientations, and this causes the average sunlight exposure of the particles to be 5 to 40\% higher than would be expected if their orientations were random. Further, we find that the mean irradiance depends on the ratio of the particle mixing length $L_m$ to the light decay lengthscale $\lambda$, and the nature of this dependence differs between disks and rods. Disks experience disproportionately greater mean irradiance at smaller $L_m/\lambda$ due to the vertical variation in their orientations. These results have important implications for accurately estimating the sunlight exposure of particles in the surface boundary layer.

authors.name: Lucia Baker, Julio Ch\'avez-Dorado, Anusha Aggarwal, Inessa Garrey, Michelle DiBenedetto

papers.title: A charge-dependent electron emission yield from electron irradiated dielectrics
papers.summary: The total electron emission yield (TEEY) of dielectric surfaces may vary during electron irradiation owing to charge accumulation within the material. In the present work, the generation, transport, and escape formulation of Dionne is extended by introducing an additional attenuation of secondary electrons that depends on trapped positive charge. The resulting emission law is coupled to a charge-balance equation, allowing the TEEY to be calculated as a function of incident energy and injected charge. The model is examined using measurements on polycrystalline Al2O3, from which effective cross sections describing interactions between trapped charge and secondary electrons are determined. Their mean value is then used to predict the evolution of the TEEY curves without further adjustment. Finally, an analytical approximation of the nonlinear charging law is derived to facilitate the implementation in electron-irradiation simulations.

authors.name: M. Belhaj, A. M. Cavalca de Almeida, N. Fil

papers.title: Blind in-memory arithmetic with confined skyrmions: doubling and successor functions on a skyrmion byte
papers.summary: We present a skyrmionic-based computation platform, able to perform fully in-memory computing by collectively manipulating the skyrmions that serve as bits of the binary memory. The computation protocols are implemented through driving currents and adequately located anisotropy defects that modify the dynamics of the skyrmions along a magnetic track. Simulations demonstrating the feasibility of such an in-memory computing system are shown for several basic and simple mathematical operations with natural numbers, such as doubling and adding one (the successor function). We also discuss how further optimization of the geometry, barrier profiles, current amplitudes, and timing parameters could improve both the robustness and the overall practical feasibility of the system.

authors.name: Joan Revert\'e, Nuria Del-Valle, Jaume Cunill-Subiranas, Natanael Bort-Soldevila, Carles Navau

papers.title: Verifying the High-Energy Tail in Bi-Kappa Particle Loading: Three-Dimensional Tests, Velocity Bounds, and Finite Precision
papers.summary: The bi-Kappa distribution models anisotropic space-plasma populations with suprathermal power-law tails. Kinetic simulations represent such a population by computational particles, and a loader draws their velocities from the requested bi-Kappa distribution, which we call the target distribution. When $\kappa$ is close to 1/2, floating-point underflow can remove the largest draws, and a velocity bound changes the loaded distribution. Published Kappa loaders are usually verified by comparing histograms of the speed or of one velocity component with the analytic distribution. Such comparisons do not examine the direction of the velocity or whether the direction is independent of the speed. We build an anisotropic loader on an established Gamma-ratio construction and examine each of these problems. Near $\kappa=1/2$, evaluating the Gamma ratio on a logarithmic scale avoids the loss of draws to underflow in single and double precision down to $\kappa=0.5001$. When draws outside a bound on each velocity component are discarded and redrawn, a small rejected fraction can accompany a large change in the tail. At $\kappa=2$ and $\theta_\parallel=2\theta_\perp$, a bound at 20 times each component's thermal speed rejects a fraction $3.6\times10^{-4}$ of the draws and lowers the 99.9th-percentile speed by 11%. We test the loaded velocities through their direction and their normalized radius, the length of the velocity after each component is divided by $\sqrt{\kappa}$ times its thermal speed. The tests used nine values of $\kappa$ from 0.51 to 10, including $1/2<\kappa\le3/2$, where the second moments do not exist, with $\theta_\parallel=2\theta_\perp$ in double precision. At every $\kappa$, $\chi^2$ tests find the normalized radius out to its 99.999th percentile, the direction, and their joint distribution consistent with the target distribution.

authors.name: Keheng Zhu, Yuri A. Omelchenko

papers.title: KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids
papers.summary: Lagrangian particle tracking follows virtual particles in the velocity fields of an ocean model to study transport pathways, connectivity and dispersion. Setting up such a study takes many technical steps, and this work is increasingly done with coding agents, programs in which a language model writes code, runs it and checks the result. We present KELP v1.0, the Kinematic Engine for Lagrangian Particles, a tracker for unstructured ocean-model meshes and HEALPix grids that is built to be operated by such agents. KELP computes two- and three-dimensional trajectories with established methods on triangular, quadrilateral and mixed meshes, with global FESOM2 and coastal FESOM-C meshes as examples, and on HEALPix, the equal-area grid on which kilometre-scale digital twins distribute their output. Documentation and short task instructions, called skills, tell an agent how to prepare releases and configurations, run calculations and process the trajectories. An agent prepared and ran all experiments of this paper with these skills, and most of the preparation was completed within hours. In a controlled evaluation, the skills raised the completeness of study files prepared by five language models from 75-93% to 88-100%. KELP reproduced the particle distributions of two other trackers on the same fields. Trajectories on HEALPix fields converged to those on the model mesh as the pixels were refined. After one year, the median distance between the two was 1.6 km at a pixel spacing of 25.5 km. HEALPix output can therefore be used for Lagrangian studies of ensemble statistics when the original mesh is not available. In a 63-year calculation with 7.92 million particles released in the Beaufort Gyre, transport from the gyre to Fram Strait took years to decades, and the run took 3 h 36 min on one 128-core node. A test tracked $10^{10}$ particles on a HEALPix mesh of 35.5 million wet surface nodes.

authors.name: Ivan Kuznetsov, Alexey Androsov, Dmitrii Pantiukhin, Claudia Wekerle, Sergey Danilov, Thomas Jung, Nikolay Koldunov

papers.title: A Surrogate Boundary Condition for Improved Accuracy and Performance of Local Modeling in Radiation Transport Simulations
papers.summary: Monte Carlo neutronics analysis of tokamak designs is computationally expensive due to the complex CAD geometries required to accurately model them. Design iteration of port plugs using global transport in the full model is impractical because of the computational cost. To circumvent this, local modeling methods are used. In the local modeling method, a boundary condition is assumed on the port plug, such that particles that leave the port plug do not require transport in the surrounding global model. For this purpose, vacuum and reflective boundaries are assumed, both of which provide poor approximation of the true transport physics in the global model. To improve on current techniques, a surrogate model is presented that provides a physics-informed boundary condition for the component. A neural network is trained to reproduce the boundary condition on the component that represents the behavior of particles returning from the surrounding geometry. Monte Carlo transport is only necessary within the component, and approximate physics from the surrounding region are retained. This approach allows the design in the component to be iterated without requiring full model transport and joining of the component mesh to the global mesh in each iteration. In this work, the surrogate model is evaluated against vacuum and reflective boundaries-- outperforming both in accuracy, with surrogate predictions of the flux in the port plug differing less than 12% from the global transport solution in any given energy bin. The surrogate boundary condition is also demonstrated to be more performant than global transport for the simplified benchmark geometry.

authors.name: Jonathan Trieloff, Ethan Peterson

papers.title: AI4Plasma I: Data-Efficient Surrogate Modeling of Capacitively Coupled Plasma Fields
papers.summary: Reference capacitively coupled plasma (CCP) simulations provide spatially resolved plasma fields but are costly to generate across operating conditions. We compare the data efficiency of five surrogate architectures--Coordinate MLP, PCA-Net, U-Net, Fourier neural operator (FNO), and Transolver--for predicting RF-cycle-averaged electron density, ion density, electric potential, and electron temperature in 1D planar and 2D axisymmetric GEC CCP benchmarks. We assess the number of reference simulations needed to achieve 1% and 2% mean relative L2 error for parameter-interior and parameter-boundary test cases, and examine architecture-specific mechanisms. FNO achieves the lowest or joint-lowest reference-case requirement in seven of eight comparisons. In 1D, FNO reaches 1% interior error with 50 training cases, compared with 100 for Transolver and 200 for U-Net. In 2D, FNO and U-Net each reach 1% interior error with 100 cases; FNO and Transolver each reach 2% parameter-boundary error with 200 cases, compared with 400 for U-Net. At the stricter 1% 2D parameter-boundary target, Transolver requires 400 cases versus 800 for FNO. Additional analyses investigate FNO spectral modes and padding, U-Net skip connections, Transolver adaptive slicing, and PCA-Net projection versus prediction error. The results support FNO as a data-efficient baseline for the tested CCP settings, while showing that the preferred architecture depends on the accuracy target and operating-parameter region.

authors.name: Zhenyu Zou, Junjue Liao, Hao Yang, Luowei Yin, Chenyu Wang, Yufeng Wei, Zhichao Peng, Chun Chen, Daniel Zhengyu Huang, Kangxin Liu, Haoran Guan, Rubing Han, Yipei Chen, Peiting You, Yuwei Fan

papers.title: Remarks on Souriau's Geometric Thermodynamics for Weak Two-Dimensional Euler Flows
papers.summary: We examine infinitesimal symmetries of relative entropy on low-regularity vorticity spaces and compare them with symmetries of stationary laws of weak two-dimensional Euler trajectories.
