Relative-entropy invariance under sample-space transformations is equivalent to preservation of the reference law; the corresponding weak infinitesimal condition is a vanishing reference-divergence identity. White-noise vorticity has an infinite-dimensional family of such symmetries, generated by smooth area-preserving transport. At the level of path laws, however, marginal entropy symmetries need not preserve temporal correlations. We first give a continuous Gaussian counterexample, including its infinitesimal form. We then establish a counterexample directly for stationary white-noise weak Euler path laws: explicit non-isometric area-preserving shears preserve the white-noise marginal but cannot preserve an Euler path law satisfying the standard symmetrized weak vorticity equation. We also examine the reduction of guaranteed entropy symmetries under conditioning by renormalized energy. These observations distinguish thermodynamic symmetry, Hamiltonian covariance, and statistical path dynamics without asserting a selection principle for nonunique weak solutions.

authors.name: Jean-Pierre Magnot

papers.title: In-plane diffusion, spurious drift and a physics-structured gap predictor for a free colloidal pair
papers.summary: When the diffusivity of a Brownian particle depends on position, its mean displacement acquires a noise-induced (spurious) drift whose magnitude is set by the stochastic convention $\alpha$. We ask how much of this physics can be extracted from a pair of 1.95 $\mu$m polystyrene spheres released from blinking holographic optical tweezers at five bath temperatures between 2 and 40 $^\circ$C. The single-sphere diffusivity inside the pair stays between 0.093 and 0.098 $\mu$m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, whereas the Stokes-Einstein value for water rises from 0.126 to 0.361 $\mu$m$^2$ s$^{-1}$; an isolated sphere reproduces the deficit, which is therefore not a pair effect. From the measured gap-dependent diffusivities $D_\parallel(h)$ and $D_\perp(h)$ we build a Fokker-Planck predictor of the future gap and score it on held-out releases. It recovers the 90% width of the gap distribution up to 800 ms but cannot discriminate between $\alpha = 0$, $1/2$ and $1$, because the $\alpha$-dependent mean shift is an order of magnitude smaller than that width. The ensemble spurious drift is consistent with zero at both ends of the temperature range, and the regression for $\alpha$ never exceeds $R^2 = 0.22$. We therefore present a planar methods baseline and identify the measurements required to resolve $\alpha$.

authors.name: Juan Pablo Staforelli Vivanco, Cristobal Augusto Vald\'es Cruces

papers.title: Mean-field theory of neural networks: from spikes to firing rates
papers.summary: Connecting microscopic neuronal spiking to macroscopic brain function is a central challenge in computational neuroscience. Firing-rate models provide a framework for addressing this problem by describing neuronal activity at an intermediate level between individual spikes and large-scale population dynamics. Here, we introduce the foundations of firing-rate descriptions, formalizing their definitions through temporal, population, and trial averaging. We discuss experimental evidence for firing rates, from the input-output transfer functions of individual neurons to the tuning curves of different neuronal populations. We then establish the connection between spikes and firing rates in single neurons and recurrently connected excitatory-inhibitory populations using mean-field approximation. We illustrate how collective dynamics emerge from neuronal interactions, including population stimulus-response curves and bistability induced by recurrent coupling, and brain rhythms arising from synaptic depression. We briefly review extensions and applications of firing-rate models to learning, seizure-like oscillatory activity, visual selectivity, phase-amplitude coupling in neural oscillations, and whole-brain modeling. Together, these examples illustrate how firing-rate models provide effective descriptions of neural activity, linking the dynamics of individual neurons to collective computations across scales.

authors.name: Tawan T. A. Carvalho, Matheus Haas, Denis D. Caprioti, Luis A. R. Delgado, Artyom Kuznetsov, Henrique L. Schweitzer, Constantino F. Vasconcelos, Rodrigo P. Rocha, Mauricio Girardi-Schappo

papers.title: Deformation Kinetics of Charged Nanoclusters via Surface Diffusion
papers.summary: Low-temperature charged nanoclusters deform, primarily via surface diffusion, when surface electrostatic stresses and surface tension stresses are not balanced. We derive an analytical model for the kinetics of this process, based on the cluster size, net charge, surface tension, local curvature, temperature, and diffusivity. The model predicts the deformation time when either surface tension or electrostatic stress dominates, leading respectively to the collapse or elongation of the cluster. Comparison with molecular dynamics simulations of ice nanoclusters with solvated electrons shows quantitative agreement with a single fitted parameter. The model can predict the deformation kinetics of charged nanoclusters in atmospheric aerosols and complex plasmas.

authors.name: Efstratios M. Kritikos, William A. Goddard III, Paul M. Bellan

papers.title: Excitable mechanical lattice: from single-unit bifurcations to boundary-driven pulse propagation
papers.summary: We comprehensively characterize the dynamical regimes of a periodically forced excitable mechanical unit and subsequently investigate how the complex oscillatory responses generated in the first unit under periodic boundary forcing affect pulse propagation through a 1D lattice of such coupled excitable units. Our mechanical unit comprises a mass connected to a fixed frame by an elastic beam and interacting with a moving plate through a smooth, nonmonotonic friction, exhibiting an all-or-none response characteristic of excitable systems. Using two-parameter bifurcation analysis, we identify distinct dynamical regimes in the forcing parameter space and delineate regions of subthreshold and suprathreshold responses associated with intrinsic excitability. Small changes in forcing amplitude can induce rapid transitions between these regimes, with the threshold amplitude depending on the forcing frequency. Within the suprathreshold regime, the system exhibits mixed-mode oscillations (MMOs), characterized by alternating sequences of small-amplitude oscillations (SAOs) and large-amplitude spikes. We then investigate pulse propagation through a lattice of coupled excitable units under sinusoidal boundary forcing and find that the lattice selectively suppresses SAOs and closely spaced large-amplitude spikes within the MMO patterns generated at the first unit. Consequently, the complex boundary dynamics are transformed into pulse trains with nearly uniform spike amplitudes and interspike intervals. When the initial interspike intervals are nonuniform, propagation progressively reorganizes the temporal spacing of transmitted pulses, promoting more uniform intervals in sufficiently long lattices. These findings may also be relevant to other excitable media, where pulse-train regularization during propagation could improve signal transmission even when initial interspike intervals are nonuniform.

authors.name: K Prabith, Georgios Theocharis, Sylvain Barbay, Soizic Terrien

papers.title: A Unified Device-Level Physical Framework for DRAM Read Disturbance
papers.summary: Read disturbance in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) depends on both local device interactions and the electrical conditions imposed by shared array circuitry. Here, we combine DIMM-level characterization results, device measurements, and TCAD simulations to interpret RowHammer, RowPress, and ColumnDisturb within a unified device-level physical framework. We relate charge evolution at the floating storage node to three key mechanisms: trap-assisted electron migration (EM), capacitive coupling (CC), and sense-amplifier-mediated disturb (SAMD). EM is local and trap-sensitive, while CC weakens with wordline separation. SAMD extends disturbance through shared column circuitry by modifying unselected-cell leakage under rail-level bitline biases, a contribution supported by the approximately ninefold higher OFF-state leakage measured relative to retention-like conditions for a high-voltage storage state. These distinct spatial ranges account for localized RowHammer and RowPress failures and remote ColumnDisturb populations with abrupt changes at subarray boundaries. We further interpret prolonged RowPress activation as a transition from an initial RowHammer-like transient to sustained leakage driven mainly by SAMD under held wordline and bitline biases. Within this device-level framework, trap effectiveness and storage-state-dependent leakage provide an interpretation of previously puzzling failure signatures, including the earlier onset of 0-to-1 RowHammer failures despite the predominance of 1-to-0 failures at high hammer counts. The same framework explains the observed RowPress and ColumnDisturb polarities and the duration-dependent reversal of neighboring- and passing-wordline effectiveness. These results provide a physical basis for developing compact DRAM reliability models across access patterns and array configurations.

authors.name: Zhaoqiang Bai, Haocong Luo, Xinhe Wang, Xujing Li, Yuelin Jiang, Xuelu Huang, Guilei Wang, Hao Meng, Ataberk Olgun, Ismail Emir Yuksel, F. Nisa Bostanc{\i}, Jikun Wang, Onur Mutlu

papers.title: Foundation Tensor Networks Generalize Across Quantum Lattice Systems
papers.summary: Neural quantum states and tensor networks have emerged as leading techniques for simulating quantum many-body systems. However, disordered systems remain extremely challenging in both frameworks as they require computation of the ground state for every realization of the disorder. Recently, neural quantum states have been used to construct foundation models that generate the ground state directly from the Hamiltonian. Still, they are hindered by the need to perform extensive sampling to estimate observables. To address these difficulties, we introduce the foundation tensor network (FTN), which uses a neural network to generate the tensor network representation of the ground-state wavefunction from the Hamiltonian. To accelerate training, we develop a technique, called \texttt{GridBP}, based on iterated one-dimensional belief propagation that reduces the cost of computing the energy expectation value to just two tensor contractions. We use FTNs to calculate the critical parameters of the glass transition in the quantum Edwards-Anderson model via finite-size scaling analysis. To facilitate rapid averaging, we use a moment-generating function to evaluate the order parameter, lowering the cost to a single tensor contraction. We obtain high-fidelity estimates for the critical parameters by averaging over 500,000 disorder realizations.

authors.name: Ryan T. Grimm, Michael Lindsey

papers.title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus
papers.summary: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm$^2$/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm$^2$/s). The monolayer anisotropy is smaller than the calculated exciton dispersion alone would suggest, which first-principles calculations attribute to preferential exciton-phonon scattering to large momenta along the zigzag direction. These directly measured, layer-resolved diffusivities identify armchair-aligned monolayers as the optimal geometry for directional transport and show that transport anisotropy cannot be inferred from band dispersion alone.

authors.name: Stephanie M. Hart, Siddhartha Sohoni, Amal Mathew, Aidan L. O'Beirne, Bowen Hou, Reef Sweeney Ethan J. Dunsworth, Diana Y. Qiu, Tony F. Heinz, Naomi S. Ginsberg

papers.title: LHC Based Antimuon-Nucleus Collider LH$\mu$C: Nucleus Options
papers.summary: Nucleus options of the LH$\mu$C, an antimuon-hadron collider based on the LHC, are presented. Ultra-cold $\mu^+$ beams, based on the technology of the J-PARC muon $g-2$/EDM experiment as proposed for $\mu$TRISTAN, are accelerated to 1 TeV in either a $\mu$TRISTAN-type booster or a booster housed in the LH$e$C energy-recovery-linac tunnel, and collide with LHC nucleus beams in a 3 km main ring tangential to the LHC. Collisions with Pb, Xe, O and Ne beams provide centre-of-mass energies from 13.1 to 47.9 TeV, i.e. about 3.3 TeV per nucleon. Luminosities and beam-beam tune shifts are evaluated with the AloHEP software. For $\mu$-Pb collisions, the luminosity reaches $2.7\times10^{30}$ ($2.2\times10^{30}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ with the $\mu$TRISTAN-type (ERL-based) booster, i.e. $5.6\times10^{32}$ ($4.5\times10^{32}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ per nucleon, which a Brinkmann-Dohlus dynamic focusing scheme could increase by a factor of 2-3. The physics potential is discussed, including an extension of the kinematic reach by a factor of about 20 with respect to the LH$e$C, access to parton saturation at perturbative scales, nuclear parton distributions, photon-induced processes and charged-current flavour separation.

authors.name: Ali Can Canbay, Burak Dagli, Arda Goroglu, Yigitali Karaca, Umit Kaya, Bora Ketenoglu, Saleh Sultansoy, Frank Zimmermann

papers.title: Indefinite causal order with definite Bohmian trajectories for the quantum switch
papers.summary: We analyze the notion of indefinite causal order (ICO) from the standpoint of the deterministic de Broglie--Bohm theory, based on the notion of trajectories in configuration space. More precisely, we study the physics of the quantum switch (QS) interferometer within a Bohmian framework and show how the notion of causality is preserved in this approach. Furthermore, we investigate device-independent certification and causal inequalities applied to an entangled quantum system, and show that in this regime too, the notions of trajectories and of a strict causal order are perfectly preserved.

authors.name: Aur\'elien Drezet

papers.title: A Multiobjective Optimization Framework for Sensor Array Design in Magnetocardiography
papers.summary: Magnetocardiography (MCG) noninvasively measures cardiac magnetic fields. Conventional cryogenic systems use fixed multichannel arrays, whereas room-temperature sensors enable flexible placement to reduce array size and measurement redundancy. The present study aims at developing a scheme to identify the optimal sensor placements by utilizing three methodological sensor optimization frameworks such as physics driven, experimental data driven and a hybrid combination of both. The physics-driven method optimizes continuous planar coordinates using D-optimality, spatial correlation, and leastsquares error. The data-driven method uses measured spatiotemporal fields and pole-geometry metrics, while the hybrid method integrates both approaches. The evaluation is performed using training objective, Pearson correlation, normalized root-meansquare error (NRMSE) and pole separation(mm), orientation({\deg}) and trajectory(mm) errors, where physics-driven optimization identified 16 sensors with a correlation of 0.9914 and an NRMSE of 0.0139, with pole separation, orientation, and trajectory errors of 3.71 mm, 1.38{\deg}, and 3.55 mm, respectively. Data-driven optimization shows diminishing improvements beyond 17 sensors, achieving correlation 0.9840, NRMSE 0.0035, and pole errors of approximately 4.30 mm, 1.70{\deg}, and 6.80 mm. The hybrid method achieves correlation 0.9945 and NRMSE 0.0201 with 14 sensors, reducing sensor count by 12.5% relative to the physics-driven configuration. Its pole errors of 6.50 mm, 2.31{\deg}, and 7.50 mm satisfy the study-defined thresholds, balancing array compactness with magnetic-field morphology preservation. These results show that optimized placement helps alleviate the complexity of data redundancy and enhances the performance of MCG as a routine cost-effective clinical measurement.

authors.name: Kesavaraja C, Sammita Kashyap, Korak Biswas, Pranab Dutta, Kushal Patel

papers.title: BeST: Beta splatted tomography for direct reconstruction from coherent imaging measurements
papers.summary: Conventional coherent X-ray tomography requires the phase of each projection to be reconstructed with high fidelity. However, individual reconstructed projections might be flawed, e.g. due to positioning errors, yielding inconsistent tomographic reconstructions. By directly coupling phase retrieval and tomography, consistency is enforced through a common object volume. But reconstructing a full volume demands substantial computational resources. To reduce this demand, we introduce Beta Splatted Tomography (BeST), which represents the common object volume using compactly supported beta primitives with closed-form analytical projections, enabling efficient reconstruction directly from coherent scattering images. This representation substantially reduces the number of optimizable parameters compared to a voxel grid. We demonstrate BeST on experimental datasets from hard X-ray near-field holography and far-field ptychography measurements. In both cases, the joint technique improves reconstruction quality compared to two-step methods.

authors.name: Johannes Gruen, Philipp Paetzold, Andreas Schropp, Aknur Karabay, Shahin Sepanlou, Sebastian Eberle, Martin Seyrich, Felix Wittwer, Imke Greving, Silja Flenner, Ken Vidar Falch, Jan Garrevoet, Manuel Guizar-Sicairos, Christian G. Schroer, Johannes Hagemann

papers.title: A Concise Introduction to Quantum Electromagnetics
papers.summary: This book introduces quantum electromagnetics to readers trained in classical electromagnetics, without assuming a systematic background in quantum mechanics. The central question is when classical descriptions suffice, and when the quantum states of matter or the field must be retained explicitly. Starting from familiar electromagnetic modes and material response, the discussion develops atomic dynamics, field quantization, and the interaction of quantized fields with quantum matter. Particular attention is given to how mode profiles, Green functions, and scattering matrices obtained from classical electromagnetic calculations enter quantum models. Atomic coherence, photon statistics, spontaneous emission, and cavity coupling are developed through derivations that identify the physical assumptions and limits of each description. Examples drawn from atomic clocks, Rydberg-atom receivers, and single-photon devices connect these concepts to excitation, propagation, and measurement in practical systems. Loss and noise are included in relating internal dynamics to measured signals and correlations. The final discussion examines how sensitivity and claims of quantum advantage depend on bandwidth, measurement resources, and the classical reference used for comparison. The aim is to help readers choose an appropriate model, carry out the calculation, and understand what its predictions mean for an electromagnetic measurement.

authors.name: Wei E. I. Sha

papers.title: Latent resonances in oscillator networks
papers.summary: In networks of coupled oscillators, from neural circuits to power grids, damping is expected to suppress oscillations because of its dissipativity. Here we show that local damping can, counterintuitively, amplify oscillations along some input-output channels, while the network's global oscillation energy decreases and its spectral properties improve. The amplified oscillation arises from a latent resonance that lies in the spectrum yet barely manifests. The added passive damping reshapes this resonance by mixing it with adjacent eigenmodes. In random power-grid networks, damping can boost weakly responding channels by more than an order of magnitude, while subdominant channels can grow to exceed the originally strongest channel. Damping thus not only suppresses oscillations but also provides a way to redistribute oscillatory energy. For any passive network, the amplified response and its upper bound follow exactly from baseline quantities, offering a principled route for network design and control.

authors.name: Junjie Xiao, Renaud Lambiotte, Hiroshi Kori

papers.title: A Machine-learning-aided Workflow for Sampling Small Polaron Dynamics in Energy Materials
papers.summary: One of the defining characteristics of most energy materials, used as e.g.~battery electrodes, photovoltaics, or photocatalysts, is their ability conduct charges such as electrons and holes. The exact mechanism of this conductivity depends on the material, but is often dominated by the existence of mobile small polarons, i.e.~electrons or holes strongly localised through the polarisation of their environment. Computationally, small polarons can be treated with reasonably accuracy through the use of self-interaction corrected or hybrid density functional theory (DFT) together with local geometry optimisation. Similar approaches can be employed to determine the energy barriers to movement of the polarons through hopping. Unfortunately, realistic energy materials tend have very large numbers of symmetry inequivalent polaronic configurations and correspondingly large numbers of hopping barriers, making them hard to tackle explicitly. In this work we therefore extend the computational reach of DFT calculations with machine-learned (ML) surrogate models, which then feed into a kinetic model to quantitatively estimate the conductivity of a battery anode material (Li$_4$Ti$_5$O$_12$ or LTO) at realistic, defected conditions. We calculate the conductivity at room temperature to be 6.7 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ S/cm which lies well in the experimental range. To this end, we only needed a total of 154 polaron barrier calculations, out of 3649 symmetry inequivalent ones, achieving an over 20-fold increase of computational efficiency. Overall, our work demonstrates how DFT-trained ML surrogates can be used to quantitatively and efficiently sample the dynamics of small polarons in energy materials.

authors.name: Tavinder Singh, Harald Oberhofer

papers.title: Exact stochastic theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation mediated by RNA-binding proteins
papers.summary: While analytical theories of transcriptional feedback loops have been well established, exact stochastic analyses of post-transcriptional feedback loops remain relatively scarce and are notoriously challenging. Here, we develop an exact theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation, in which reversible protein-mRNA binding modulates both translation and mRNA stability. We derive the state-dependent protein burst-size distribution, the steady-state protein number distribution in terms of confluent Heun functions, and an exact criterion for sub-Poissonian fluctuations. By comparing transcriptional and post-transcriptional networks, we reveal a reversal in their relative advantages in noise suppression and rhythm transmission: negative feedback favors post-transcriptional regulation, whereas positive feedback favors transcriptional regulation. Our results reveal how the regulatory pattern fundamentally shapes gene expression fluctuations and dynamic responses.

authors.name: Chen Jia

papers.title: Linear-optical generation of approximate higher-component cat states
papers.summary: We propose a method for generating higher-component cat states by interfering two $N$-component cat states on a half beam splitter and measuring one output with a photon-number-resolving detector. The Fock components of the conditional output are restricted to a single residue class modulo $2N$. For $N=3$, an ideal six-component cat state can be generated exactly, while for arbitrary $N$, the conditional output approaches an ideal $2N$-component cat state for sufficiently large input amplitudes.

authors.name: Shohei Kiryu, Masahiro Takeoka

papers.title: Spin-adapted sample-based quantum diagonalization with randomized time evolution
papers.summary: Quantum algorithms based on the classical post-processing of measurement samples have emerged as effective and robust methods to approximate low-energy wavefunctions of many-body quantum systems on present-day and early-fault-tolerant quantum devices. This paper introduces a generic framework for enforcing spin symmetry within these approaches. We tailor this framework to SqDRIFT, a sample-based quantum diagonalization variant that uses the qDRIFT randomized compilation protocol to generate the quantum samples. We discuss how three key components of SqDRIFT (the initial-state preparation, the construction of the time-evolution circuits, and the classical post-processing) can be adapted to incorporate spin symmetry. We show that spin-pure circuits alone are not sufficient, since the sampled determinants generally span a subspace that is not closed under $\hat{S}^2$, and we restore this closure by completing the sampled electronic configurations. In classical simulations of 4-aminobenzonitrile and of an $[\text{Fe}(\text{NH}_{3})_{4}]^{2+}$ model complex, and in experiments on an IBM quantum processor for the oxo-Mn(Salen) complex, this spin-adapted post-processing yields roots that are exact spin eigenfunctions at every subspace size. On hardware, it does so with diagonalized subspaces two to three orders of magnitude smaller than those of the conventional constructions for the same circuit depth.

authors.name: Stefano Barison, Samuele Piccinelli, Alberto Baiardi, Francesco Tacchino, Ivano Tavernelli

papers.title: Few-Ion Schottky Power Scaling and Automated Reconstruction of Single-Ion Events
papers.summary: Non-destructive Schottky diagnostics at heavy-ion storage rings is broadly exploited to measure revolution frequencies and intensities of stored ions. The mean Schottky power of incoherent stored ions is expected to be proportional to their number. An empirical examination of this response in few-ion populations is important for interpreting individual occupancy changes. We present an automated staircase reconstruction of the power in a selected frequency band of time-resolved Schottky spectra. The procedure was applied to 7008 selected injections recorded with a resonant cavity pickup at the Experimental Storage Ring at GSI during an experiment on the nuclear two-photon decay of the first excited $0^+$ state in bare $^{98}\mathrm{Mo}^{42+}$. The distribution of freely fitted level heights exhibits maxima close to integer multiples of a single-ion power scale up to approximately five ions. This is consistent with an approximately additive mean power response under the present measurement conditions. The reconstructed occupancy histories also retain population dwell intervals and resolved disappearance times for subsequent lifetime analyses.

authors.name: Moritz Porstend\"orfer, David Freire-Fern\'andez, Anna Jule He{\ss}, Wolfram Korten, Yury A. Litvinov

papers.title: Reproduction of Simulated Acoustics Scenes Using Acoustics Room Transformer for speech intelligibility tests in Clinics
papers.summary: An Acoustic Room Transformation (ART) method is proposed for clinical applications to render simulated acoustic environments using six loudspeakers in a reverberant room. In typical clinical settings, testing rooms are not acoustically treated and only a limited number of loudspeakers are available. The ART approach enables control of the playback-room reverberation, allowing speech intelligibility tests to be performed under realistic and perceptually compensated conditions. The method focuses on the two most common Speech Reception Threshold (SRT) configurations: S0N90 and S0N90. One front and one side loudspeaker reproduce the direct sound components, while the remaining four loudspeakers (two in front and two behind the listener) generate the reverberant sound field. The direct sound is optimized in terms of energy, and the reverberant field is adjusted based on both energy and interaural coherence. An additional direct-sound gain is applied to match the clarity index (C50) of the reproduced signals to that of the reference target. Results from speech intelligibility tests demonstrate that, with ART processing, the reproduced scenarios achieve SRT values very close to those of the reference signal in both S0N0 and S0N90 conditions and therefore allow for comparable speech test results independent of the particular test room acoustics.

authors.name: Ali Fallah, Kirsten C Wagener, Pascal Pflueger, Steven van de Par

papers.title: Quantum phase estimation on a Rydberg quantum simulator
papers.summary: Determining the energy spectrum of a many-body quantum system is a central goal of quantum physics. Ground-state energies underpin materials science and quantum chemistry, whereas excited states govern dynamical phenomena such as quantum thermalization. Quantum simulators have greatly shaped our understanding of many-body systems, for example, by enabling access to microscopic mechanisms and nonlocal order parameters. However, experiments still struggle to access the full range of many-body spectral features and are typically limited to measuring energy gaps and excitations by spectroscopic means. Here, we address this challenge by demonstrating quantum phase estimation on an analog Rydberg quantum simulator. We reconstruct the complex-valued return amplitude, or Loschmidt echo, of an initial probe state. From its Fourier transform, we measure absolute ground-state energies and energy gaps in systems of up to 19 atoms in one and two spatial dimensions. Varying the initial probe state, we select distinct spectral windows within which we compute the longitudinal and transverse magnetization, and observe their competition across the many-body spectrum. Our results thereby demonstrate phase-sensitive many-body spectroscopy on an analog quantum simulator without auxiliary qubits or controlled evolution.

authors.name: Hendrik Timme, Benjamin F. Schiffer, Ohad Lib, Shijia Sun, Maximilian Ammenwerth, Dominik S. Wild, J. Ignacio Cirac, Immanuel Bloch, Johannes Zeiher

papers.title: Certificate-Based Verification of Pulsed Field Ablation Models
papers.summary: Computational models of pulsed field ablation predict the lesion as the tissue where the electric field exceeds a lethal threshold. Their numerical error is rarely bounded, and automated pipelines increasingly run them without an expert checking each result. To verify each run, we separate the question "was the stated model solved correctly?" from the solver that answers it. An untrusted solver returns with its answer a certificate, consisting of a potential with the correct electrode and ground values and an exactly charge-conserving current. A small independent checker verifies the certificate against a written specification of the physics. Using the Prager-Synge hypercircle theorem evaluated in ball arithmetic, it turns the certificate into guaranteed two-sided bounds on the impedance and on the root-mean-square field of every tile of a lesion map, also over a range of blood/tissue conductivity ratios. A vectorized version of the checker takes about a tenth of the solve time. For a focal electrode in contact, the tile-resolved depth at 1000 V and 700 V/cm is proven to lie in 3.50-3.75 mm for every ratio from 1.7 to 3.75. For a bipolar catheter, certified depths overlap published in-vivo depths. Where they differ from a published reference model, the certificates prove that the difference is not numerical error in our computation. We compare the certificate with a grid convergence study on the same solver. On graded grids the study is sharper for local fields but remains an estimate. On uniform grids it fails to converge at the electrode edge, where the certificate still gives a valid bracket. Solvers that deliberately solve equations other than the specified ones pass the grid convergence study, but the certificates refute their claims or leave them unsupported.

authors.name: Konstantinos Dovelos

papers.title: Fundamental and multihumped multimode solitons in fibers : new families of solitons and their properties
papers.summary: We describe multimode solitons made of purely spatial modes using the mathematical formalism developed for the elliptical polarization soliton, and we extend this formalism to solitons made of more than two modes. The main difference with the polarization mode case is the asymmetry in the nonlinear coefficients. Strictly speaking, these objects are solitary waves, whose modal temporal profiles remain invariant owing to the incoherent nonlinear interaction between modes. The approach consists of finding the trajectories of a unit-mass ball in an analogous potential, which correspond to stationary solutions of our set of nonlinear coupled equations. Our analysis reveals a rich variety of multimode solitons with more complex temporal profiles, so-called multihumped multimode solitons. These are new and highly complex nonlinear objects. While fundamental multimode solitons are stable against noise and symmetry breaking, the stability of multihumped multimode solitons depends on their position in the parameter space. The fission of multihumped solitons yields several less complex multihumped solitons, together with fundamental multimode solitons. For the latter, Raman nonlinearity can induce a net energy transfer between modes with different group velocities, whereas self-steepening only modifies the overall velocity of the solitary wave.

authors.name: Julien Dechanxhe, Pascal Kockaert, Spencer W. Jolly

papers.title: The Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth
papers.summary: We determine the Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for small-amplitude Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth. For the full water wave system, we derive an explicit instability index and rigorously classify its sign throughout the depth-vorticity plane. With gravitational acceleration and carrier wavenumber normalized to one, we identify a unique minimum depth $h_{\text{crit}}\approx1.36271$, below which Benjamin-Feir instability is absent for every vorticity. Above this depth, two vorticity thresholds delimit the unstable regime, outside of which the spectrum near the origin remains purely imaginary for all small Floquet exponents. In particular, at each fixed finite depth, constant vorticity of sufficiently large magnitude suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability. Moreover, any constant vorticity $\gamma\ge 2/\sqrt{3}$ suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability at every finite depth. The proof combines Hamiltonian spectral perturbation theory, symbolic computations, and formal verification in Rocq. Away from the transition set, our results rigorously confirm the stability criterion predicted by the nonlinear Schr\"odinger approximation of Thomas, Kharif, and Manna.

authors.name: Bowen Chen, Huy Q. Nguyen

papers.title: Reconciling global and local spin models
papers.summary: Magnetic interactions based on first-principles calculations can be casted either into global spin models, where the interactions are configuration-independent, or into local spin models, where the effective parameters depend explicitly on the underlying spin configuration. Although these two perspectives often yield seemingly inconsistent results, we demonstrate that they can be reconciled by restricting the analysis to transverse spin fluctuations. We develop a projection scheme that systematically removes spurious longitudinal contributions from local interaction matrices, thereby establishing a rigorous connection between the projected local interactions and the underlying global multispin Hamiltonian. Applying our approach to the prototype systems (i) a Cr trimer on Au(111) (ii) Fe and Cr dimers on Cu(001), we show that the projected local interaction parameters quantitatively reproduce those obtained from the global four-spin model. This work provides a unified framework to interpret local and global spin models on equal footing and resolves long-standing ambiguities in the identification of effective interactions such as the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) in a non-collinear framework.

authors.name: Bendeg\'uz Ny\'ari, Andr\'as L\'aszl\'offy, L\'aszl\'o Szunyogh

papers.title: Number fluctuations and particle loss in Dicke superradiance
papers.summary: Dicke superradiance, the collective spontaneous emission of identical quantum emitters into a common reservoir, produces a burst with a characteristic delay $t_{\mathrm{SR}}$ and a peak intensity that scales quadratically with the emitter number $N$. This strong dependence makes the burst sensitive to how many emitters actually participate. In experiments, however, this number is rarely fixed: it fluctuates between preparations and decreases during emission through atom loss. Here we extend the analytical treatment of superradiance to variable emitter numbers using the Schwinger-boson mapping of the collective spin onto two bosonic modes. In this formulation, collective decay annihilates an atom in the excited-state mode and creates one in the ground-state mode. We find that number fluctuations enhance emission and that the ensemble-averaged emission trace encodes the initial number distribution. We show how to reconstruct second-order correlations from photon counting with finite detection efficiency and temporal resolution, even when the full distribution cannot be resolved. For atom loss at rate $r$, we derive exact results for the population dynamics and show that the peak intensity scaling is governed by the single scaling variable $g_{\mathrm{r}}=r t_{\mathrm{SR}}$. The peak remains quadratic in $N$ for $g_{\mathrm{r}}1$, and crosses over to linear scaling under strong loss with $g_{\mathrm{r}}\gg1$.

authors.name: Christian Niehof, Nico S. Bassler, Claudiu Genes

papers.title: Topological phase diagram of an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with negative coupling
papers.summary: Recently, an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with three atoms per unit cell has been experimentally realized in perovskite exciton-polariton micropillars. A distinctive feature of this system is that the second and third bands undergo a topological transition through a band crossing at the wave vector $k=0$, associated with a negative coupling. In this work, we analytically determine the phase diagram of the model as a function of the on-site energy splitting and the ratio of intercell to intracell hopping amplitudes. We identify seven regions in this lane, with four distinct topological phases, characterized by different Zak phases of the three bands. Our results provide a useful theoretical framework for interpreting existing experiments and serve as a guide for future experimental investigations of this system.

authors.name: P. A. Grizzi, P. Roura-Bas, A. A. Aligia

papers.title: Fine-tuned atomistic foundation model for accurate sodium-carbon chemistry in Na-ion batteries
papers.summary: Atomistic foundation models have emerged as a promising route to DFT-level accuracy for materials simulation with complex chemical environments. However, their reliability across competing bonding regimes and, more importantly, how complex bonding affects predictions of material properties remain unclear. Among materials with competing bonding regimes, sodium storage in hard carbon poses a substantial challenge. Hard carbon features diverse local structural motifs, including defective and curved graphitic regions, amorphous regions, and closed/open pores. Motivated by its importance for Na-ion batteries, we systematically evaluate existing pretrained foundation models based on the MACE architecture across different local Na/C motifs. We find that the pretrained models fail to accurately capture Na-Na and Na-C interactions for metallic Na clusters on graphene. To recover a DFT-level energetic description, we employ targeted fine-tuning, showing that it can describe the energetic stability of local motifs and achieve sufficient transferability to unseen Na/C environments. With the developed fine-tuned model, we establish a correlation between closed-pore radius in hard carbon and plateau voltage, showing that the small pores contribute at larger voltages than large ones, suggesting thus how the developed fine-tuned foundation model can link atomistic information with materials design for complex bonding environments.

authors.name: Andres Felipe Usuga (Centre of Excellence ENSEMBLE3 Sp. z o. o), Ihor Radchenko (Centre of Excellence ENSEMBLE3 Sp. z o. o), Yuxin Tang (Qingyuan Innovation Laboratory, College of Chemical Engineering - Fuzhou University), Oleksandr I. Malyi (Qingyuan Innovation Laboratory, Centre of Excellence ENSEMBLE3 Sp. z o. o)

papers.title: Solution of the Qubit Marginal Problem from Fermionic Representability
papers.summary: Whether local reduced states are compatible with a global quantum state---the quantum marginal problem---is central to quantum information and simulation. Here we present a solution to the ensemble marginal problem for qubits based on the representability theory of fermions. Encoding each qubit as one fermion in two orbitals, we prove that the representable qubit marginals form an exposed face of the set of $N$-representable fermionic reduced density matrices, selected by the vanishing of every site-occupation variance. Complete hierarchies of fermionic representability conditions therefore transfer exactly to qubits. Applications to frustrated Heisenberg and transverse-field Ising rings show that the $(2,3)$-positivity conditions are exact at the Majumdar--Ghosh point and accurate to about 0.5% at criticality. Because the conditions hold for any quantum state, they also provide a framework for mitigating measurement errors on qubit-based quantum devices.

authors.name: David A. Mazziotti

papers.title: Restoring Consistency with Poynting's Theorem in Numerical MHD and RMHD
papers.summary: For perfectly conducting plasmas, Poynting's theorem states that the time rate of change of electromagnetic energy density equals the negative of the divergence of the Poynting flux. To the best of our knowledge, this involutive theorem has never been mimetically incorporated in codes. We show that there is an inconsistency in MHD and RMHD codes that evolve face-centered magnetic fields in globally-divergence-free fashion. This is because the face-centered flux of energy density, which incorporates a Poynting vector, is evaluated using one-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied at face-centers. However, the face-centered magnetic fields are evolved according to edge-centered electric fields that come from two-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied to the edges of a zone. While edge-centered electric fields are used to evolve the magnetic field, they have no influence on the face-centered Poynting flux. For situations where the magnetic energy is much larger than the thermal energy, this causes a negative pressure to be evaluated at the zone-centers. This paper restores consistency by using edge-centered variables to evaluate a face-centered Poynting flux. A simple accuracy-preserving correction is made to the face-centered flux of energy density. We show that it helps considerably in simulations that have very strong magnetic fields.

authors.name: Dinshaw S. Balsara, Deepak Bhoriya

papers.title: Complex fluid flow dynamics by bright scattershot boson sampling
papers.summary: Boson sampling machines have become a fruitful tool for establishing new concepts, which connect fundamental physics with computer science applications. Here, we exploit the intrinsically high-dimensional correlations generated by the measurement outcomes of a multiphoton boson sampling machine and demonstrate how a reconfigurable architecture can be programmed to autonomously model the time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems that describe complex fluid flows. By extending on the original scattershot boson sampling (SBS) scheme to include higher photon number components -- a scheme which we label bright scattershot boson sampling (BSBS) --- this scheme overcomes scaling issues inherent to SBS-based schemes by utilizing all randomly generated input photon number distributions. We illustrate the capability of this scheme for two complex fluid-flow models: an eight-dimensional Lorenz-type model of two-dimensional thermally driven convection and a 16-dimensional model of global atmospheric circulation. Using a digital twin of the BSBS architecture based on multiphoton statistics, we show that the photonic approach accurately reproduces the temporal dynamics of both systems while being resilient to photon losses of up to 50 per cent. We also verified that the BSBS case outperforms a comparable run with coherent light. Moreover, its prediction horizon exceeds that of a classical reservoir-computing model with the same query complexity. These results highlight the potential of near-term photonic quantum computing for addressing relevant real-world tasks on noisy intermediate-scale devices.

authors.name: Robert Schade, Shailendra K. Rathor, Tim J. Bartley, Benjamin Brecht, Christian Plessl, Jan Sperling, Michael Stefszky, Christine Silberhorn, J\"org Schumacher

papers.title: Experimenters' Free Will and Quantum Certainty
papers.summary: Physics has long lived with a split personality that desires determinism for measured systems while demanding that experimenters decide what to measure on a whim. Intriguingly, such a free will assumption for experimenters has thwarted many attempts to provide a satisfactory explanation of how quantum probabilities evolve to clear-cut measurements. An overview of this quantum measurement problem is presented without equations, and the lesson is drawn that denial of experimenters' free will may be the only workable solution. A holistic view is offered of a self-consistent superdetermined spacetime block universe of events. The goal of future research is to develop the underlying principle that generates this Escher-like global pattern.

authors.name: Joseph J. Bisognano

papers.title: Catenaries in viscous fluid
papers.summary: This work explores a simple model of a slender, flexible structure in a uniform flow, providing analytical solutions for the translating, axially flowing equilibria of strings subjected to a uniform body force and drag forces linear in the velocities. The classical catenaries are extended to a five-parameter family of curves. A sixth parameter affects the tension in the curves. Generic configurations are planar, represented by a single first order equation for the tangential angle. The effects of varying parameters on representative shapes, orbits in angle-curvature space, and stress distributions are shown. As limiting cases, the solutions include configurations corresponding to "lariat chains" and the towing, reeling, and sedimentation of flexible cables in a highly viscous fluid. Regions of parameter space corresponding to infinitely long, semi-infinite, and finite length curves are delineated. Almost all curves subtend an angle less than $\pi$ radians, but curious special cases with doubled or infinite range occur on the borders between regions. Separate transitions in the tension behavior, and counterintuitive results regarding finite towing tensions for infinitely long cables, are presented. Several physically inspired boundary value problems are solved and discussed.

authors.name: Brato Chakrabarti, J. A. Hanna

papers.title: Revealing the Nonlinear Amplification of Radiation Reaction Effects via Vortex Radiation
papers.summary: Radiation reaction (RR), the back-action of emitted radiation on an accelerated charge, dominates the dynamics of ultrarelativistic electrons in an intense electromagnetic field. We derive an analytical formula for the RR-inclusive harmonic spectrum of vortex $\gamma$-ray emission in monochromatic-wave nonlinear inverse Thomson scattering (NITS), extend it to finite pulses under the slowly varying envelope approximation (SVEA), and take the Landau-Lifshitz (LL) solution as the starting point. We find that once cumulative RR on the oscillation radius over hundreds of cycles becomes non-negligible, the laser intensity nonlinearly amplifies RR through the modified longitudinal drift velocity, reshaping the vortex emission. For monochromatic approximation of long pulse flat-top laser, harmonic band acquire MeV-scale red shifts and spectral compression, producing overlap; higher harmonics show anomalous polarization transitions, so the superposed ellipticity departs from the RR-free case. For a $\sin^2$ envelope, the lower edge red-shifts while the upper cutoff stays fixed, broadening the band, and individual polarization transitions remain analogous to RR-free case. These harmonic-resolved spectral and polarization fingerprints constitute a self-referenced multidimensional diagnostic of RR effects that complements energy-spectrum measurements and, through the RR-inclusive scaling law between the polarization and laser amplitude, provide an independent route to measuring the laser intensity. These results have direct implications for bright high-energy $\gamma$-ray sources and the modeling of extreme astrophysical environments such as neutron-star magnetospheres.

authors.name: Yi-Ju Kang, Yu-Meng Gao, Jia-Qi Wang, Mamutjan Ababekri, Qian Zhao, Jian-Xing Li

papers.title: Inertial forces and elastohydrodynamic interaction of spherical particles in wall-bounded sedimentation experiments at low particle Reynolds number
papers.summary: Unsteady, wall-bounded sedimentation of spheres at low particle Reynolds numbers under the influence of small elastic deformation was investigated experimentally. The complete kinematics of elastic and rigid spheres sedimenting from rest at various initial distances from a rigid plane wall in a rectangular duct were measured. Several previously unrecognized phenomena arising from fluid inertia and superimposed elastohydrodynamic effects were identified and analyzed. Among these is an \textit{inertial wall attraction}, whereby particles migrate towards the wall during the initial acceleration phase. After this initial phase, rigid spheres sedimenting at $Re_\text{P}\approx O(10^{-1})$ followed behavior consistent with classic wall-lift models, including approximately linear migration away from the wall. In contrast, at smaller Reynolds numbers, $Re_\text{P}\approx O(10^{-2})$, both rigid and elastic spheres exhibited persistently unsteady sedimentation, characterized by deceleration despite increasing wall distance. These results enable the formulation of a conceptual framework that classifies near-wall sedimentation regimes according to particle Reynolds number and the position of boundaries relative to the Stokes length scale. For increasing deformability, the unsteady behavior was further modulated by nonlinearities. The observations suggest the presence of an \textit{elastohydrodynamic memory} effect arising from the coupling of fluid inertial forces with particle deformability. The experimental findings are supported by computational fluid dynamics simulations that provide qualitative insight into the evolving flow field. Overall, the results demonstrate that classic assumptions commonly applied to particle sedimentation in creeping flows break down in the presence of nearby boundaries...

authors.name: Isabell Noichl, Clarissa Sch\"onecker

papers.title: GPU-acceleration of the Discontinuous Galerkin Shallow Water Equations Model (DG-SWEM) with OpenACC
papers.summary: This paper presents a porting of {DG-SWEM}, a first-order discontinuous Galerkin solver for storm surge based on the Advanced Circulation Model (ADCIRC), to NVIDIA GPUs. Time-explicit discontinuous Galerkin methods contain a large number of degrees of freedom but have been shown to exhibit a large amount of data parallelism due to the loose coupling between elements, and thus are naturally mapped to the GPU architecture. A previous framework in porting DG-SWEM to GPUs required converting subroutines from Fortran to C++ to be used with CUDA C++. By using OpenACC and Unified Memory, we simplify the porting process and maintain a single codebase for both CPU and GPU versions. We test the code using a large Hurricane Harvey scenario on NVIDIA's Grace Hopper chip, and compare the GPU code's performance on multiple H200 nodes to the CPU version on the same amount of Grace CPU nodes.

authors.name: Chayanon Wichitrnithed, Eirik Valseth, Ethan J. Kubatko, Shintaro Bunya, Clint Dawson

papers.title: Nonhomogeneous elastic turbulence in the two-dimensional Taylor-Couette flow
papers.summary: Elastic turbulence is a spatially and temporally disordered flow state appearing in viscoelastic fluids at vanishing fluid inertia and large elasticity. The resulting flows have broad technological interest, particularly to enhance mixing and heat transfer in microdevices. Although its experimental characterization is now well established in different setups, its theoretical understanding and numerical reproducibility remain challenging, especially in wall-bounded geometries. By means of numerical simulations, we investigate the onset of elastic turbulence and the characteristics of the developed turbulent-like states in the two-dimensional, confined, Taylor-Couette system. First, we characterize the purely elastic instability, addressing previously contrasting evidence. We then show that the fully nonlinear dynamics are weakly anisotropic and strongly nonhomogeneous. Indeed, they are confined in a dynamically active region adjacent to the inner wall, akin to the elastic boundary layer from previous predictions. Within this region, in spite of some non-negligible deviations due to the nonhomogeneity of our setup, the statistical and spectral turbulent properties are to a reasonable extent not far from the theoretical expectations and experimental observations.

authors.name: Zhongxuan Hou, Stefano Berti, Teodor Burghelea, Francesco Roman\`o

papers.title: A fast and rigorous numerical tool to measure length-scale artifacts in molecular simulations
papers.summary: The two-sided Bogoliubov inequality for classical and quantum many-body systems is a theorem that provides rigorous bounds on the free-energy cost of partitioning a given system into two or more independent subsystems. This theorem motivates the definition of a quality factor which directly quantifies the degree of statistical-mechanical consistency achieved by a given simulation box size. A major technical merit of the theorem is that, for systems with two-body interactions and a known radial distribution function, the quality factor can be computed by evaluating just three six-dimensional integrals. We present a numerical algorithm for computing the quality factor and demonstrate its consistency with respect to results in the literature obtained from simulations performed at different box sizes.

authors.name: Benedikt M. Reible, Nils Liebreich, Carsten Hartmann, Luigi Delle Site

papers.title: CP-violating non-linear electrodynamics and corrections to blackbody radiation thermal laws
papers.summary: Motivated by ideas from effective field theories, we conduct a twofold investigation in CP-violating non-linear electrodynamics models. On the one hand, features related to field equations and wave propagation in the presence of a magnetic background field are evaluated. Interestingly, we show that the CP-violating term in our framework induces a bi-anisotropic behavior of the vacuum. On the other hand, blackbody radiation thermal laws in this situation are studied. Here, we provide a general formalism for photons at low temperature, namely, with $k_{B}T\ll{m_{e}c^{2}}$. The deviations from standard values of the thermodynamic quantities, such as energy, pressure, entropy, and specific heat, are discussed. In addition, we investigate the modifications in the Planck distribution and the Stefan-Boltzmann law induced by a non-trivial CP-violating parameter.

authors.name: L. P. R. Ospedal, R. Turcati, S. B. Duarte

papers.title: Projected sensitivity to light WIMP-like particles of the BULLKID-DM experiment
papers.summary: BULLKID-DM is an experiment designed for the direct searches of particle dark matter candidates with mass around 1 GeV, or below, and cross-section with nucleons smaller than $10^{-40}$ cm$^2$. The detector consists of a stack of diced silicon wafers, acting as arrays of particle absorbers, sensed by multiplexed Kinetic Inductance Detectors. The target will amount to 800 g subdivided in more than 2000 silicon dice, with the aim of controlling the background from natural radioactivity by creating a fully active structure and by applying fiducialization techniques. In this work we present the projected sensitivity of BULLKID-DM to light WIMP-like particles considering also the other future experiments in the field.

authors.name: Matteo Folcarelli, A. Acevedo-Renter\'ia, L. E. Ardila-Perez, L. Bandiera, M. Calvo, M. Cappelli, R. Caravita, F. Carillo, U. Chowdhury, D. Crovo, A. Cruciani, A. D'Addabbo, D. Delicato, M. De Lucia, G. Del Castello, M. del Gallo Roccagiovine, F. Ferraro, S. Fu, R. Gartmann, M. Grassi, V. Guidi, D. Helis, T. Lari, L. Malagutti, A. Mazzolari, A. Monfardini, T. Muscheid, D. Nicol\`o, F. Paolucci, D. Pasciuto, L. Pesce, C. Puglia, D. Quaranta, C. M. A. Roda, S. Roddaro, M. Romagnoni, G. Signorelli, F. Simon, A. Tartari, E. V\'azquez-J\'auregui, M. Vignati, K. Zhao

papers.title: On the wake and flapping dynamics of different aspect ratio flags
papers.summary: The flapping of flags is a classical problem involving fast, large amplitude deformations of a thin flexible plate and unsteady flow phenomena. We perform systematic time- and space-resolved measurements of the deformation and drag acting on flapping flags for various aspect ratios and mass ratios. Flag deformations travel from the root to the tip while growing in amplitude. We present a robust method to determine the travelling wave properties, and reveal that the dimensionless wavelength $\lambda/L$ is constant for a given flutter mode, and that the wave speed equals the freestream velocity for aspect ratios above unity but decreases with decreasing mass and aspect ratio. We provide a mechanistic explanation of the influence of mass and aspect ratio on the flapping dynamics by introducing a mass-ratio-corrected dimensionless wave speed, which is proportional to the square root of the dynamic pressure difference across the flag. At smaller aspect ratio, the local dynamic pressure exerted by the fluid on the flag is reduced, leading to a decrease in the wave propagation speed and the tip frequency. Based on near wake flow field measurements, we identified two characteristic length scales, the ratio of flag area over its perimeter $L^*$ and the square root of area $\sqrt{HL}$ that scale the circulation of vortices shed per cycle. Values of the mean drag coefficient scatter widely, from \num{0} to \num{0.55}, when varying mass and aspect ratio. We can collapse the data when using a kinematics-based model with the mass ratio and the tip speed as inputs.

authors.name: Ga\'etan Raynaud, Karen Mulleners

papers.title: DD-03B: Target-level analysis of ligand-protein dissociation pathways reveals ligand-specific exit pathways weakly coupled to binding affinity
papers.summary: Protein-ligand interactions are conventionally described by a structure and a binding affinity (Kd). Kinetic simulation datasets have grown rapidly, but most analyses remain structure-centred and RMSD-based, and the kinetic information carried by the trajectories is rarely extracted. Here we analyse 766,550 complete dissociation trajectories for 15,540 protein-ligand complexes grouped into 3,687 UniProt accessions. Each trajectory is reduced to a uniform record of 119 descriptors-ligand and structure size, trajectory statistics, the pathway distribution of escape events, and pocket and escape-volume descriptors-so that records from different systems can be compared, joined and searched. This tokenisation shows that the pocket and the ligand act on the same quantity at different levels: the pocket defines the repertoire of exits, and the ligand sets the weights. In open sites the repertoire collapses to one broad mode and affinity tracks ligand size and contact; in confined pockets the exit ensemble splits into several channels whose weights follow ligand size rather than binding affinity. UniProt grouping is a convenient classification above the PDB entry but not the right final unit: two systems illustrate domain separation and degeneracy, and a structural classifier would be preferable. We present the framework as a general analysis paradigm for molecular dynamics trajectory libraries.

authors.name: Maodong Li, Keyu Gao, Yiming Chen, Zhe Wang, Runxiu Wu, Dechin Chen, Zhijun Pan, Yi Isaac Yang

papers.title: Symmetry-Engineered Magnetic Dipole Emission in Plasmonic Core-Satellite Resonators
papers.summary: Magnetic dipole (MD) transitions are intrinsically weak and highly sensitive to emitter orientation and position, making their controlled enhancement at optical frequencies particularly challenging. Here we show that structural symmetry provides a powerful route to robust magnetic light-matter interactions. We systematically investigate plasmonic core-satellite resonators composed of N metallic nanoparticles arranged on a dielectric core. We evaluate their performance using a unified figure of merit that accounts for magnetic Purcell enhancement, electric dipole suppression, quantum efficiency, and robustness to emitter orientation and fabrication tolerances. We find that the optimal structures correspond to the highest-symmetry geometries, which naturally produce spatially homogeneous and orientation-independent magnetic Purcell enhancement. In particular, the dodecapod configuration yields strong magnetic emission with Purcell factors approaching 590, good radiative efficiency, and suppressed electric dipole contributions. Quasinormal-mode and complex mode-volume analysis reveal that symmetry enforces uniform magnetic modal confinement within the core, explaining both the enhancement and its robustness. These results establish symmetry as a guiding principle for designing nanophotonic resonators with controlled multipolar light-matter interactions and provide a practical route toward bright and selective magnetic dipole emitters.

authors.name: Joshua Davis, S\'ebastien Bidault, Mathieu Mivelle, Mona Tr\'eguer-Delapierre, Alexandre Baron

papers.title: Evaluating a Large Language Model for Radiotherapy Patient Scheduling under Realistic Clinical and Operational Constraints: a Feasibility Study
papers.summary: Radiotherapy scheduling must balance clinical constraints and operational objectives. We evaluated the feasibility of using a large language model (LLM) to generate treatment schedules through simulation and retrospective clinical comparison. A one-year simulation modeled 1,400 new patients across 12 treatment categories and three linear accelerators (LINACs). Structured prompts provided ChatGPT with patient information, schedule status, clinical rules, and operational objectives. Scenarios assessed treatment-time consistency, LINAC continuity, gap reduction, and handling of infeasible requests. LLM schedules were compared with heuristic and constraint programming (CP-SAT) approaches under two objective settings. A six-week retrospective analysis included 2,043 clinical appointments. LLM-generated schedules met all predefined feasibility constraints in the evaluated scenarios, with 98.6-98.8% of fractions within preferred treatment-time windows. Prioritizing LINAC continuity reduced switching from 52.4 +/- 2.6% to 9.4 +/- 0.6%. Gap-constrained temporal relaxation reduced average daily gaps to 47.1 +/- 8.5 minutes and Friday gaps to 89.2 +/- 18.4 minutes while maintaining low overtime. The framework identified predefined violations in infeasible requests and suggested corrective actions. Heuristic and CP-SAT methods also generated feasible schedules, with performance dependent on objective weighting. In retrospective evaluation, all approaches scheduled appointments without overtime; LLM strategies reduced mean gaps by 50.8-77.1% and improved treatment-time consistency from 86.7% to 99.5-99.9%. These findings support further evaluation of structured LLM scheduling as a human-in-the-loop decision-support approach for radiotherapy.

authors.name: Eric Zhang, Youfang Lai, Wen Li, Annette Souranis, Georgia Paparoidamis, Michael Roumeliotis, Xun Jia

papers.title: Match classification in the last round of four-team round-robin tournaments
papers.summary: Classification of matches played in the last rounds of sports competitions is a well-established tool for evaluating tournament designs. Our paper offers the first comparison of deterministic and probabilistic match classification models by analysing the most prominent example of four-team round-robin competitions, the group stage of the FIFA World Cup. We show that both models are highly relevant in practice: all (four) deterministic and (six) probabilistic match types occurred in the 2014 and 2018 FIFA World Cups, respectively. The probabilistic model, which accounts for the relative benefits of attacking and defending, provides a deeper insight; for instance, the competitive matches from the deterministic approach can be of any of the six probabilistic types. Therefore, the probabilistic model is used to decompose the impact of three reforms introduced in the 2026 FIFA World Cup: the expansion to 48 teams, the modified qualification rules, and head-to-head tie-breakers.

authors.name: L\'aszl\'o Csat\'o, Andr\'as Gyimesi

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for kinetic shock waves: simultaneous accuracy of lower- and higher-order moments, with and without moment supervision
papers.summary: We investigate physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for one-dimensional kinetic shock waves governed by the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook (BGK) and Shakhov collision models, with and without moment supervision. The trace-free third-order and the fourth-order moments enter the fluxes of stress and heat flux through a shock; the aim, to our knowledge not previously examined for kinetic PINNs, is simultaneous accuracy of these and the lower-order moments of one predicted distribution. Data-assisted calculations, including anchor and closure studies, combine kinetic residuals with moment observations. For the BGK shock tube, a positive eight-moment representation whose spatial envelope follows the far-field decay of the initial condition gives heat-flux, stress and higher-moment discrepancies of $0.33\%$, $0.67\%$ and $1.8$--$2.0\%$ against the 6400-cell discrete-velocity method (DVM) reference supplying its observations; a five-field representation leaves the latter uncontrolled. Equation-trained characteristic-integral PINNs use analytic initial and incoming-boundary distributions and their own predicted moments. Their BGK and Shakhov shock-tube heat-flux and stress discrepancies are $0.41\%$ and $0.36\%$ against 3200-cell references; against the 6400-cell reference the BGK values are $0.21\%$ and $0.18\%$, and $0.4$--$0.9\%$ for the higher moments. Stationary neural continuation covers Shakhov Mach 2--5 and BGK Mach 6--7. Characteristic correction reduces the Mach-7 heat-flux and stress discrepancies from $3.37\%$ and $1.34\%$ to $0.42\%$ and $0.43\%$; at Mach~8 they are $0.62\%$ and $0.79\%$, and at Mach~12, across references, $0.40$--$1.03\%$ and $0.41$--$2.65\%$. Three independent Mach-2 initialisations assess repeatability. It is established that lower moments do not determine higher ones; the contribution is to quantify which moments each information regime recovers.

authors.name: Ehsan Roohi

papers.title: Symmetry-breaking and hysteretic transitions in an actively coupled optical trimerhrough chaotic hysteresis in a non-Hermitian optical trimer
papers.summary: We investigate the nonlinear dynamics of a non-Hermitian optical trimer consisting of three lossy waveguides with complex-valued coupling. Building on our previous analysis of its global dynamics, we adopt a site-resolved approach to elucidate the bifurcation structure and the organization of oscillatory states across the individual waveguides. We identify a hysteretic transition from reflection-asymmetric periodic states to periodic states exhibiting a combined reflection-translation symmetry. This transition involves a double-loop hysteretic regime characterized by the coexistence of multiple attractors. Analysis of the spatial intensity profiles and their Fourier spectra reveals distinct oscillatory behavior among the waveguides. In particular, in the regime with combined reflection-translation symmetry, the central waveguide exhibits a dominant spatial wavenumber approximately twice that of the edge waveguides. We further identify a third dynamical regime emerging through a pitchfork bifurcation of limit cycles, which breaks the combined reflection--translation relation and gives rise to two reflection-related periodic solutions. Despite this transition, the 2:1 relation between the dominant spatial wavenumbers of the central and edge waveguides persists. These results demonstrate how nonlinear interactions, complex coupling, and dissipation shape multistability, chaotic dynamics, bifurcations, and site-dependent oscillations in a minimal non-Hermitian photonic system.

authors.name: Johanne Hizanidis, Konstantinos G. Makris

papers.title: Breaking-induced energy dissipation of surface gravity waves at varying scales and co-flowing wind stresses
papers.summary: Breaking-induced energy dissipation is studied for individual unsteady breaking waves using laboratory measurements of unidirectional surface gravity wave groups across a range of wave scales and wind stresses. A refined framework to estimate breaking-induced dissipation $\Delta E_{br}$ is proposed that accounts for background dissipation from non-breaking processes. Using this framework, we show that variations in wave scale primarily influence breaking energetics, such as fractional dissipation $\Delta E_{br}/E_0$ and dissipation rate $\epsilon_b$, by modifying the breaking onset threshold. Also, co-flowing wind systematically reduces both $\Delta E_{br}/E_0$ and $\epsilon_b$ relative to unforced conditions, as wind-forced waves break earlier with reduced crest forward-leaning. Exploiting the crest-front steepness at incipient breaking $\mathcal{S}_{\text{front}}(t_b)$ to characterise breaking onset and local crest geometry, we formulate a scaling for $\epsilon_b$ based on this local measure. This then yields $\Delta E_{br}/E_0 \propto \beta^{*}\,\mathcal{S}_b\,(\tau_b/T_b)$, where $\beta^{*}$ is crest forward leaning, $\mathcal{S}_b$ local steepness, and $\tau_b/T_b$ non-dimensional breaking duration. This scaling highlights the important roles of crest asymmetry and breaking duration in setting the breaking energy dissipation. Finally, we consider the breaking strength parameter $b$ by assessing existing steepness-based scaling laws, and relate $b$ to $\mathcal{S}_{\text{front}}(t_b)$, yielding an approximately linear dependence once the breaking-onset threshold is considered.

authors.name: Rui Cao (Ocean University of China, Imperial College London), Enrique M. Padilla (Universitat Polit\`ecnica de Catalunya), Xu Chen (Ocean University of China), Adrian H. Callaghan (Imperial College London)

papers.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly -- Living with Priors in Bayesian confirmation
papers.summary: Bayesian confirmation faces a classic problem: where do initial priors come from? In cases with abundant data and repeated updating, different priors tend to converge to the same posterior. However, in frontier research this convergence often fails, and confirmation remains sensitive to priors. We examine how physics practice in the case of gravitational wave research deals with such cases and, normatively, when prior sensitivity should be regarded as epistemically problematic. We offer a practice-based account of the prior problem, drawn from a detailed case study in physics, of a kind so far absent from the philosophical literature on Bayesianism. One upshot is a clearer diagnosis of so-called `analogue confirmation'.

authors.name: Niels Linnemann, Christian W\"uthrich

papers.title: Exceptional Points of Temporal Coherent Perfect Absorption in the Momentum Bandgap of a Photonic Time Crystal
papers.summary: We report exceptional points (EPs) of temporal coherent perfect absorption (CPA) in the momentum bandgap of a photonic time crystal. Confinement of the photonic time crystal in a cavity with finite length gives rise to discrete momentum modes, and therefore enables coherent matching of a single light source to a selected decaying Floquet mode. Meanwhile, excitation of the corresponding growing Floquet mode is suppressed by destructive self-interference. Two CPA branches coalesce at second-order EPs, leading to a quartic absorption lineshape and enhanced robustness against momentum detuning. Phase control further reveals the nontrivial topology of the CPA manifold, in which CPA at the wavevector of maximum Floquet rate exhibits a double phase winding around a third-order EP. Compared to conventional CPA EPs that rely on material absorption, temporal CPA EPs transfer the source energy to the external modulation, providing the basis for high energy efficiency and suppressed local heating. These results indicate the great potential of photonic time crystals for coherent control of light in integrated nanophotonic devices.

authors.name: Yuhang Li, Zilong Bao, Yu Zhuang, Jingwen Cui, Junda Wang, Zhanchun Zuo, Xiulai Xu, Chenjiang Qian

papers.title: Wave collapse proliferation as a mechanism for anomalous dissipation and spontaneous stochasticity
papers.summary: Anomalous dissipation and spontaneous stochasticity are signatures of the roughness of the inviscid limit in fluid turbulence. Spontaneous stochasticity describes the selection of a probability distribution over possible solutions rather than a single deterministic trajectory. We investigate these phenomena in a nonlinear dispersive equation undergoing finite-time blowup, known as wave collapse. Collapse is arrested by two regularization mechanisms, one dissipative and one conservative. Heuristic arguments supported by numerical simulations show that an isolated collapse has a vanishing effect in the inviscid limit and cannot alone account for either phenomenon. However, simulations reveal that the number of collapse events diverges as the regularization vanishes. Their proliferation enables sustained dissipation in the dissipative case and prevents either regularization from selecting a single inviscid solution. We then introduce vanishingly small random perturbations and find numerical evidence for a well-defined statistical limit in which randomness persists. These results identify collapse proliferation as a mechanism connecting anomalous dissipation and spontaneous stochasticity in dispersive waves, allowing a formally deterministic equation to acquire a truly random limiting evolution.

authors.name: Wandrille Ruffenach

papers.title: Learning transferable event representations for charmed baryon physics at BESIII
papers.summary: Deep learning has become an essential tool in high-energy physics, where the ability to learn transferable event representations can significantly improve model generalization across related physics processes. In this work, we present a Particle Transformer-based framework for learning such representations for charmed baryon physics in the BESIII experiment. The framework is implemented through large-scale pre-training on Monte Carlo simulation samples and subsequent fine-tuning for downstream analyses. Using the production and decays of the charmed baryon $\Lambda_c^+$ as a benchmark, we develop pre-trained models for both event classification and momentum-direction regression. The classification model learns discriminative event representations for the dominant physics categories, rejecting $96.90\%$ of background events at a signal efficiency of 90.00\%. Across 12 benchmark $\Lambda_c^+$ decay channels, fine-tuning from the pre-trained model achieves performance comparable to or better than training from scratch, with particularly clear improvements in low-statistics regimes. For the regression task, the pre-trained model improves the average angular resolutions across the same benchmark channels. Further improvement is obtained after fine-tuning in the representative semileptonic decay $\Lambda_c^+ \to p K^- e^+ \nu_e$. In addition, the predicted momentum direction enables reconstruction of the parent kinematics without a recoil-side tag and thereby increases signal efficiency. For this semileptonic decay, the pre-trained regression model increases the signal efficiency by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the double-tag method. This strategy provides a scalable solution for a wide range of physics cases at BESIII and can be extended to other high energy experiments.

authors.name: Kaixuan Huang, Yangu Li, Junpeng Zhao, Peilian Li, Peirong Li, Xiao-Rui Lyu, Yunxuan Song, Shengsen Sun, Yangheng Zheng

papers.title: Compression of virtual spaces in transcorrelated methods via singular value decomposition: application to the G2 set
papers.summary: We introduce a new singular-value-decomposition-based scheme for constructing small virtual spaces out of large basis sets for transcorrelated (TC) calculations, termed SVD-TC. This work builds on the recent finding that the residual basis error in the TC reference energy converges more slowly than that of the correlation energy. Within the new workflow, the post Hartree-Fock TC calculation is performed in a compressed virtual orbital subspace, obtained by projecting the canonical virtual orbitals from a large basis set onto a smaller basis set through singular value decomposition (SVD). This allows us to achieve the high accuracy allowed by the large basis, whilst the bottleneck steps - TC integral calculation and post-HF correlation method such as CCSD(T) - incur the cost of only a small virtual space calculation. The method therefore is highly efficient, whilst avoiding the composite nature of the reference correction method. Using the new scheme, we widen the scope of benchmark-quality TC results into more complex molecules than previously considered: using the G2-1 set of 55 molecules with first- and second-row atoms, we apply SVD-xTC-CCSD(T) to compute atomization energies. We compare our results against the near-exact semistochastic heat-bath configuration interaction (SHCI) reference values and experiment. We find that SVD-xTC-CCSD(T) delivers chemical accuracy already with triple-$\zeta$ basis sets.
