papers.title: Precise Deep-Learning Reconstruction of Galaxy Cluster Mass Maps and Substructures from Optical Observations
papers.summary: Accurately mapping the total mass distribution within galaxy clusters, including dark matter, is fundamental to understanding structure formation and constraining cosmological parameters. Conventional mass-mapping techniques rely predominantly on gravitational lensing and often produce smooth mass distributions based on analytical profiles, potentially missing important internal substructures. We introduce a complementary, simulation-based inference approach to reconstruct detailed galaxy cluster mass maps and resolve their internal substructures directly from optical imaging. We trained deep learning models on realistic hydrodynamical simulations of galaxy clusters to infer their mass distributions from optical observations. We subsequently applied this framework to observations of real galaxy clusters obtained with the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) as part of the Cluster Lensing And Supernova survey with Hubble (CLASH) programme. The reconstructed mass maps successfully reproduce the overall shapes and radial mass profiles of the CLASH clusters, showing strong agreement with independent gravitational lensing measurements. Furthermore, the subhalo mass functions derived from the reconstructed maps exhibit power-law behaviour broadly consistent with predictions from numerical simulations. Our results demonstrate that combining optical imaging with deep learning provides a scalable and physically meaningful approach to mapping galaxy cluster mass distributions. This framework opens a new avenue for exploiting upcoming wide-field imaging surveys to systematically investigate dark matter substructures across large cluster samples, complementing traditional gravitational lensing techniques. Moreover, the model is inherently flexible and can incorporate multi-wavelength observations, including X-ray and Sunyaev--Zel'dovich data, to further improve total mass predictions.

authors.name: Atulit Srivastava, Weiguang Cui, Daniel de Andres, Guillaume Bonnet, Romeel Dav\'e, Stefano Ettori, Massimo Meneghetti, Carlo Giocoli, Gustavo Yepes

papers.title: Probing baryonic feedback using fast radio bursts and galaxy surveys
papers.summary: The dispersion measure (DM) of fast radio bursts (FRB) provides a noisy measure of the free-electron column density to the burst. With next-generation FRB surveys the number of bursts will drastically increase and measurements of the baryon distribution will be possible on the Mpc scales most relevant to Stage IV weak lensing surveys. Comparing the DM auto-spectrum, DM-shear cross-spectrum and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, we argue that the cross-correlation of FRB catalogs with galaxy surveys offers many advantages. Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT), often used in large-scale structure cosmology, is capable of modeling the clustering of electrons jointly with galaxies and matter to small scales. Using HEFT with the Pad\'e model of baryonic feedback, we forecast that next-generation FRB surveys (combined with galaxy samples) will be able to constrain feedback at a level informative for Stage IV weak lensing surveys. In particular we should not be limited by modeling the manner in which galaxies trace the matter field. Rather constraints of the higher-order electron biases and the electron-galaxy cross-stochasticity provide the dominant limitation, and are an obvious target for improvement in order to reach percent-level constraints. The same measurements also provide a valuable means of constraining feedback in hydrodynamic simulations of galaxy formation in a way that is not tied to the modeling of particular galaxy samples.

authors.name: Haruki Ebina, Martin White

papers.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
papers.summary: Recent observational investigation of cosmological Parity Violation (PV) through the galaxy Four-point Correlation Function (4PCF) has motivated a careful theoretical examination of potential systematic contributions. In this work, we demonstrate that parity-odd contributions to the isotropic 4PCF estimator induced by Redshift Space Distortion (RSD), up to the leading order $\mathcal{H}/k$ of general relativistic corrections, vanish upon averaging over all the Line-of-Sight (LOS). We analyse the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density, combining the biased tracer expansion and the dark matter gravitational dynamics within the framework of Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory (EPT) to third order in the density perturbation. Building on prior studies of the parity-odd mode of the trispectrum (the Fourier-space counterpart of the 4PCF), we extend existing results in three directions: incorporating the wide-angle effect by adopting a local LOS definition for each galaxy in the 4PCF, accounting for tidal bias in the galaxy population, and generalising the assessment to an arbitrary cosmological background. Expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, we show that angular momentum selection rules, encoded in the Wigner 3-j symbols, enforce that only parity-even contributions survive the integration over all LOS orientations, both in the plane-parallel approximation and in the full wide-angle case. This result is crucial for large-scale statistical analyses using isotropic estimators. It supports interpreting possible PV detections as a signal not due to a systematic RSD artefact. We conclude with a discussion of the caveats of our results and identify potential sources of PV.

authors.name: Chanasorn Kongprachaya, Nicola Bartolo, Daniele Bertacca, Sabino Matarrese

papers.title: Does Dark Energy Evolve $\textit{and}$ Cluster?
papers.summary: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in dynamical dark energy, and naturally raise the question of whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics. We address this question through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark-energy contribution to the expansion and the gravitational responses governing clustering and lensing, complemented by a combined covariance-mode analysis, without imposing model-specific relations between the sectors. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and Pantheon+ supernova observations, and subsequently adding large scale structure observations including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data and other surveys, we recover a broad maximum in the effective dark-energy density near $z\simeq0.6$--$0.7$. The gravitational responses exhibit suggestive low-redshift enhancements over their GR values, approximately coincident with the background feature. Adding large scale structure information preserves the background feature but favours a mildly reduced lensing response. The combined covariance-mode analysis identifies the combinations of background and gravitational responses most tightly constrained by current observations and quantifies their departures from $\Lambda$CDM. The leading modes are decisively background dominated, while the gravitational sector remains less precisely constrained. Thus, present data cannot yet determine whether the suggestive low-redshift features in the two sectors share a common physical origin, a question that ongoing Stage-IV surveys will be able to address

authors.name: Maria Luisa Gallavotti, Alessandra Silvestri

papers.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
papers.summary: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in non-standard late-time evolution. We investigate whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark energy density, $\Omega_{\rm X}(a)$, and the gravitational response functions $\mu(a)$ and $\Sigma(a)$. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+, and large scale structure observations, including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data, we perform reconstructions with and without a theory motivated correlation prior derived from stable Horndeski models. We find a persistent maximum in $\Omega_{\rm X}$ at $z\simeq0.5$--$0.7$, corresponding to a crossing of the effective phantom divide. This feature is already present in the CMB+BAO combination and remains robust when modifications to clustering and lensing are allowed. The reconstructed gravitational response exhibits suggestive enhancements in $\mu$ and $\Sigma$ over approximately the same redshift range, although these departures are less significant. Including LSS information instead favours a reduced lensing response, $\Sigma<1$, while leaving the background feature largely unchanged. An interpretation within Generalized Brans-Dicke theories illustrates how modifications to the effective gravitational coupling and a scalar-mediated fifth force may contribute to these trends. Our results indicate that current departures from $\Lambda$CDM are most significant in the expansion history, while leaving open the possibility of correlated modifications to gravitational dynamics that future Stage IV surveys can test.

authors.name: Maria Luisa Gallavotti, Alessandra Silvestri

papers.title: Depletion of Dark Matter Spikes by Massive Black Hole Mergers
papers.summary: Dark matter over-densities around massive black holes, known as dark matter spikes, can dephase gravitational waves emitted by intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs/EMRIs), offering a promising way to indirectly detect dark matter. This detection channel, however, requires the spike to survive over cosmological time-scales. We investigate the impact that a host black hole's merger history has on its dark-matter spike. We focus on how the inspiral of a massive-black-hole (MBH) binary modifies and disrupts these spikes within the central $\sim 100$ Schwarzschild radii of the black hole. We find that a single merger with mass ratio $q = 0.03$ is capable of reducing a spike's density by around 3 (5) orders of magnitude at 100 (5) Schwarzschild radii across all polar angles relative to the binary's plane, independent of the primary MBH's mass, with larger mass ratios inducing even stronger depletion. In fact, a single past merger with mass ratio as small as $q = 0.005$ reduces central densities by 2--3 orders of magnitude, making gravitational-wave dephasing difficult to detect. We relate these results to the MBH merger history by analysing cosmological simulation data from Horizon-AGN. We find that mergers become increasingly common as the MBH mass increases, with mergers of mass ratio q > 0.03 having occurred in 50% of MBHs of mass $3\times10^7M_\odot$ and 95% of mass $10^8M_\odot$ at z=0. These fractions are reached at even lighter masses ($2\times10^7M_\odot$ and $5\times10^7M_\odot$, respectively) at z=3. We find that accretion-induced adiabatic MBH growth is unable to cause appreciable spike re-growth between such mergers in {\tt Horizon-AGN}. Thus, in combination with previous studies of EMRI-induced depletion, this work constrains the mass range over which massive black holes can host detectable DM spikes to $10^6M_\odot$--$5 \times 10^7M_\odot$ for $z \leq 3$.

authors.name: Charlie Sharpe, Thomas F. M. Spieksma, Yonadav Barry Ginat, Ricarda S. Beckmann, Alexander Heger, Bence Kocsis

papers.title: WDM_GW_Wavelets: A fast, JAX-based Python implementation of the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer wavelet transform for the time-frequency analysis of gravitational wave data
papers.summary: This paper describes a JAX-based implementation of the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer (WDM) time-frequency transformation, intended for use in gravitational-wave data analysis.

authors.name: Christopher J. Moore, Tomasz Kinowski

papers.title: Combining spectral analysis and narrow band pass filtering to predict solar cycle parameters in the next solar grand minimum
papers.summary: The paper develops a method for forecasting grand minima in sunspot number (SSN). The method is applied to the annual SILSO SSN record, 1700 - 2024, to obtain a high resolution forecast and to a reconstructed annual SSN record, 971 - 1899, to obtain a low resolution forecast. Fourier analysis identifies eleven near-decadal periodicities, in the range from 8 to 15 years, in the SILSO record and four centennial scale periodicities, between 60 and 800 years, in the reconstructed SSN record. Components at each period are isolated by a new method of narrow band pass filtering. The components are fitted with sinusoids for back/forward projection. Forward projection from each record forecasts a grand solar minimum from 2030 to 2150. Short term features within the grand minimum are less certain. The eleven periodicities in the SILSO record are separated into octal, decadal and decadal-plus groups. The four components in the decadal group are, on average, higher in amplitude by a factor of three than components in the other two groups. During grand maxima the decadal group components constructively interfere and dominate SSN variation. Following grand maxima the four decadal group components move into destructive interference, a grand minimum in SSN occurs and the summed amplitudes of the octal and decadal-plus groups can match or exceed the summed decadal contribution. Short term change in SSN variation, specifically the Waldmeier Effect, is explained in terms of interference between the contributions of the octal and decadal groups.

authors.name: Ian Edmonds, Peter Killen

papers.title: The Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA)
papers.summary: We create the first large-scale mock spectroscopic survey of gas absorption sightlines traversing the interstellar medium (ISM), circumgalactic medium (CGM), and intergalactic medium (IGM) surrounding galaxies of virtual Universes. That is, we create mock, or synthetic, absorption spectra by drawing lines-of-sight through cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, using a new mesh-free Voronoi ray-tracing algorithm. The result is the Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA), which is publicly released on our online science platform. It spans a diverse range of ions, transitions, instruments, observational characteristics, modeling assumptions, redshifts, and numerical simulations. These include, but are not limited to: (ions) HI, OI, CI, MgI, MgII, FeII, SiII, CaII, ZnII, SiIII, SiIV, NV, CII, CIV, OVI; (instruments) SDSS-BOSS, KECK-HIRES, UVES, COS, DESI, 4MOST, WEAVE, XSHOOTER; (model choices) with/without dust depletion, noise, quasar continua, foregrounds; (redshift) from z=0 to z~6; (ancillary data) integrated equivalent widths, column densities, distances and properties of nearby galaxies; (simulations) IllustrisTNG including TNG50, TNG-Cluster, EAGLE, and SIMBA. We also provide Faraday rotation measure (RM) probing magnetic fields, and dispersion measure (DM) as traced by fast radio bursts (FRBs). The resulting dataset is generic and broadly applicable, enabling diverse science goals such as: (i) studies of the underlying physical gas structures giving rise to particular absorption signatures, (ii) galaxy-absorber and halo-absorber correlations, (iii) virtual surveys and survey strategy optimization, (iv) stacking experiments and the identification of weak absorption features, (v) assessment of data reduction methods and completeness calculations, (vi) inference of physical properties from observables, and (vii) apples-to-apples comparisons between simulations and data.

authors.name: Dylan Nelson, Celine Peroux, Philipp Richter, Matthew M. Pieri, Sebastian Lopez, Rongmon Bordoloi, Siwei Zou, Joseph N. Burchett, Rebecca L. Davies, Rahul Ramesh, Matthew C. Smith, Sanchayeeta Borthakur, Christopher W. Churchill

papers.title: A binary merger product as the direct progenitor of a Type II-P supernova
papers.summary: Type II-P supernovae (SNe II-P) are the most common class of core-collapse SNe in the local Universe and play critical roles in many aspects of astrophysics. Since decades ago theorists have predicted that SNe II-P may originate not only from single stars but also from interacting binaries. While ~20 SNII-P progenitors have been directly detected on pre-explosion images, observational evidence still remains scarce for this speculated binary progenitor channel. In this work, we report the discovery of a red supergiant progenitor for the Type II-P SN 2018gj. While the progenitor resembles those of other SNe II-P in terms of effective temperature and luminosity, it is located in a very old environment and SN 2018gj has an abnormally short plateau in the light curve. With state-of-the-art binary evolution simulations, we find these characteristics can only be explained if the progenitor of SN 2018gj is the merger product of a close binary system, which developed a different interior structure and evolved over a longer timescale compared with single-star evolution. This work provides the first compelling evidence for the long-sought binary progenitor channel toward SNe II-P, and our methodology serves as an innovative and pragmatic tool to motivate further investigations into this previously hidden population of SNe II-P from binaries.

authors.name: Zexi Niu, Ning-Chen Sun, Emmanouil Zapartas, Dimitris Souropanis, Yingzhen Cui, Justyn R. Maund, JeffJ. Andrews, Max M. Briel, Morgan Fraser, Seth Gossage, Matthias U. Kruckow, Camille Liotine, Zhengwei Liu, Philipp Podsiadlowski, Philipp M. Srivastava, Elizabeth Teng, Xiaofeng Wang, Yi Yang, Jifeng Liu

papers.title: Neutrino flux from collisions of red giant cores in globular clusters
papers.summary: The coalescence of degenerate helium cores during red giant collisions---a process we term \textit{erythrohenosis}---introduces a novel class of transient astrophysical sources of high-energy neutrinos. Using stellar models generated with MESA and SPH simulations of the final inspiral phase, we develop a semi-analytical model to estimate the amount of hydrogen mixed into the cores, the energy release ($\approx 4.28 \times 10^{49}$~erg) that heats the remnant to $T_f \approx 5.3 \times 10^8$~K, the magnetic field amplification ($B \approx 1.77 \times 10^{10}$~G), and the resulting neutrino flux. The predicted TeV--PeV neutrino signal may contribute to the diffuse IceCube neutrino flux; we estimate that the horizon at which a single neutrino event is expected on average at $\gtrsim 100$~TeV is $\approx 55$~kpc for individual merger events. Furthermore, we discuss the probability of a magnetized helium flash and assess the subsequent activation of the CNO cycle in the remnant core due to hydrogen mixing. In particular, neutrinos from the decay of $^{18}$F offer a direct observational test of the detonation (as sources within $\sim 4.4$~pc would produce a neutrino flux exceeding the solar CNO neutrino background). The simultaneous emission of high-energy hadronic neutrinos, gravitational waves, and---if the optical depth permits ($\tau_{\rm T} \sim 10^{14}$ in the core of the remnant)---an electromagnetic signal would constitute a unique multimessenger signature of red giant core collisions, positioning erythrohenosis events as exotic yet potentially observable phenomena in dense stellar systems.

authors.name: Cecilia Romero Rodr\'iguez, Pau Amaro Seoane

papers.title: Cosmological inference with halo clustering reconstructed from the redshift-space galaxy distribution
papers.summary: Accurate modeling of small-scale redshift-space clustering is crucial for full-shape redshift-space distortion (RSD) analyses, where satellite galaxies contribute to one-halo terms and Finger-of-God distortions. We investigate halo reconstruction based on the cylinder grouping method of Okumura et al., Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. 469, 459 (2017), which selects an effective halo center tracer from the observed galaxy distribution, and how it impacts cosmological parameter inference. Using luminous red galaxy mock catalogs from the AbacusSummit simulations at $z=1.1$, we perform effective field theory (EFT)-based full-shape modeling of the power spectrum of the reconstructed-halo sample. We show that the dominant reconstruction-induced systematics can be described and incorporated within the standard EFT framework. In particular, a simple multipole-dependent rescaling inferred directly from the data on large scales captures the dominant effect, while residual small-scale changes are absorbed by the standard counterterm and stochastic sector, without introducing additional reconstruction-specific parameters. The reconstructed-halo sample yields unbiased constraints on cosmological parameters, including the growth rate $f\sigma_{s8}$ and Alcock-Paczynski parameters. Compared to the galaxy sample, it enables both improved robustness and increased statistical precision: at the fiducial limit of $k_{\max}=0.2\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, the uncertainty on $f\sigma_{s8}$ is reduced by more than $20\%$, while the high-$k_{\max}$ diagnostics show comparatively stable goodness of fit and nuisance parameters.

authors.name: Ryuichiro Hada, Teppei Okumura

papers.title: SN 2023fyq: direct detection of a Type Ibn supernova progenitor and its multiwavelength environmental constraints
papers.summary: Context. Type Ibn supernovae (SNe) are characterized by narrow helium emission lines arising from ejecta-circumstellar medium interaction, yet their progenitors remain debated, with both massive Wolf-Rayet stars and low-mass helium stars in binaries proposed. Aims. We aim to directly identify the progenitor of the Type Ibn SN 2023fyq and to characterize its environment in order to constrain the progenitor's nature and evolutionary channel. Methods. We search for the SN progenitor based on pre-explosion and late-time HST and JWST images and derive its properties by fitting the spectral energy distribution. We investigate the SN environment by probing the stars, dust, ionized gas and molecular gas with a multi-wavelength dataset including HST and JWST imaging, VLT/MUSE integral-field-unit spectroscopy and ALMA CO (2--1) radio interferometry. Results. We discover a pre-explosion source at the SN position, which is consistent with a hot ($T>$15000 K) and luminous (log($L$/$L_\odot$) $\gtrsim$ 5.5) SN progenitor and a possible host star cluster. The progenitor is confirmed to have disappeared after explosion. Analysis of the SN environment implies that the progenitor likely has an age of log($t$/yr) = 7.1--7.2. These phenomena disfavor a very massive single-star progenitor and instead support a binary scenario involving a low-mass helium star and a compact object; the observed progenitor emission likely arises from binary interaction that began at least $\sim$12 yr before the explosion. Conclusions. SN 2023fyq is the first Type Ibn SN with a directly detected progenitor and a possible host star cluster. It adds to the diversity of Type Ibn SNe in terms of their progenitor channels and mass-loss mechanisms.

authors.name: Xinyi Hong, Ning-Chen Sun, Yali Shao, Ke Wang, Junjie Wu, Qiang Xi, Yi-Han Zhao, Justyn Maund, Xiaohan Chen, Anyu Wang, Linxi Zhang, Jifeng Liu

papers.title: A deep intrinsic decline of accretion activity in GRS 1915+105 during 2025
papers.summary: The canonical microquasar GRS 1915+105 has undergone unprecedented multiwavelength changes since 2018. Hard-X-ray NuSTAR observations in November 2025 failed to detect it, reaching flux limits several orders of magnitude below historical X-ray levels. The non-detection could reflect enhanced obscuration, a sharp decline in accretion power, or a combination of the two. Hiding an intrinsically luminous source requires effectively complete coverage by Compton-thick material to limit residual direct or scattered components to ~4 dex if the nucleus is now unobscured), and indicating a likely return of GRS 1915+105 to quiescence after 33 years, notwithstanding any rebrightening episodes in the near future. With disc veiling now minimal, the donor star, binary orbit, and residual accretion can be probed directly for the first time.

authors.name: Poshak Gandhi (U. Southampton), Peter G. Boorman

papers.title: Time-resolved leptonic modeling of the prompt emission of GRB 211211A
papers.summary: GRB 211211A is a long duration gamma-ray burst with a compact object merger origin. In this work, we model the time-resolved prompt-emission spectra of GRB 211211A within a leptonic radiation framework. Our goal is to infer the physical properties of the emitting region, study the temporal evolution of the radiating particle distribution, and make predictions for prompt emission at TeV energies. We perform Markov Chain Monte Carlo fitting of the time-resolved numerical spectral energy distribution (SED) models computed with the time-dependent non-thermal radiation code LeHaMoC. Our calculations include synchrotron emission and self-absorption, inverse Compton scattering including cooling in the Klein-Nishina regime, and photon-photon pair production. We find that the prompt emission of GRB 211211A between 10 keV and 10 MeV can be successfully reproduced by synchrotron radiation from a population of relativistic electrons. The spectral evolution during the first minute of the burst reflects different physical conditions in the emitting region. Our best-fit models favor fast-cooling solutions for the first 8 s, followed by a transition to slow-cooling solutions at later times. The accompanying synchrotron self-Compton emission extends to TeV energies, with predicted fluxes that would be detectable by CTAO for a burst similar to GRB 211211A, provided a sufficiently rapid response to a Fermi-GBM trigger or if the burst occurs within the CTAO field of view. The observed short variability of this burst requires very high Doppler factors ($\sim1000-2500$) throughout the burst evolution. Such extreme Doppler factors are difficult to reconcile with the jet Lorentz factor inferred from afterglow modeling unless the prompt-emitting regions are themselves moving relativistically with respect to the jet plasma.

authors.name: Maria Petropoulou, Maria Gkoni, Konstantinos Xyloportas, Stamatios I. Stathopoulos, Georgios Vasilopoulos, Apostolos Mastichiadis

papers.title: Bispectrum BAO and the baryon-dark matter relative velocity
papers.summary: We evaluate the Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) signal in the bispectrum as a tool to detect and characterize the relative velocity effect. We extend the existing framework by presenting an updated model for the redshift-space tree-level bispectrum that comprehensively incorporates all relative velocity terms. We introduce a novel, unbiased technique to extract the isotropic BAO dilation parameter ($\alpha_{\rm iso}$) solely from the bispectrum monopole. Validated against N-body simulations, this template-based extraction successfully recovers the acoustic scale and enhances the statistical constraining power by $\sim30\%$, when analyzed in tandem with the pre-reconstruction power spectrum, offering a powerful complement to standard post-reconstruction pipelines. We quantify how individual relative velocity components distort both two- and three-point statistics. We find that these effects induce distinct systematic shifts in the extracted $\alpha_{\rm iso}$ between the two probes. We find systematic discrepancies of up to $2\%$ for $b_{v^2}=\pm0.05$ and up to $20\%$ for $b_{\delta^{bc}}\le-2$. This differences demonstrate that a direct comparison of independent power spectrum and bispectrum BAO measurements can break parameter degeneracies and isolate the amplitude of these biases. Finally, we provide a concrete prescription to detect and constrain the three associated relative velocity bias parameters, showing that a joint analysis is highly sensitive to the $b_{v^2}$ and $b_{\delta^{bc}}$ amplitudes. This establishes the bispectrum BAO as a robust cosmological probe for current and next-generation galaxy surveys, serving both as a cross-check for standard analyses and a crucial diagnostic tool against systematic biases.

authors.name: Adriana Nadal-Matosas, H\'ector Gil-Mar\'in, Licia Verde

papers.title: Stream-Driven Ignition of a Realistic Undisturbed Helium Shell on a White Dwarf
papers.summary: The dynamically driven double degenerate double detonation (D$^6$) model has emerged as a promising progenitor scenario for Type Ia supernovae. In this model, a carbon-oxygen white dwarf (WD) in a close double WD binary undergoes a double-detonation triggered by dynamical mass transfer from its companion. The mass transfer stream directly impacts the surface of the primary WD, potentially igniting a helium detonation in the surface layer. The resulting shock converges in the core, triggering a carbon detonation that ultimately unbinds the star. While previous studies have demonstrated the viability of this mechanism, the conditions under which the helium shell ignites remain uncertain. We perform two-dimensional simulations using FLASH to study helium detonation ignition driven by stream impact on a carbon-oxygen WD with a realistic, unmixed composition profile left at the end of the previous helium-shell burning phase before the WD was formed. We model WDs with masses of 0.8, 0.9, and 1.0 $,M_\odot$ and vary stream properties for each case. We find that stream impact leads to helium ignition in all cases, with ignition occurring at varying distances from the impact point. Ignition consistently occurs near the core-shell transition, highlighting the importance of a realistic WD profile. However, the ignition mechanism differs between models and can arise from interactions of neighboring hot, mixed regions rather than a single point. Ultimately, all models but one sustain a propagating detonation capable of traversing the WD surface further reinforcing the viability of the D$^6$ model as a progenitor scenario for Type Ia supernovae.

authors.name: Nethra Rajavel, Dean M. Townsley, Ken J. Shen

papers.title: The road towards precision measurements of $H_0$ with bright sirens in the Einstein Telescope era
papers.summary: Gravitational-wave standard sirens provide an independent probe of cosmic expansion since their luminosity distances are inferred directly from the gravitational-wave signal and, for bright sirens (BSs), the source redshifts are obtained through the identification of electromagnetic counterparts. In this work, we forecast the constraining power of future bright siren catalogues on the Hubble constant using simulated binary-neutron-star mergers detected by the Einstein Telescope with associated electromagnetic counterparts. We construct mock catalogues with different numbers of events and redshift distributions, with GW170817 as a reference BS, and analyse the resulting constraints within a flat $\Lambda$CDM cosmology. We find that, when bright sirens are used as a standalone probe, most of the information on $H_0$ is provided by low-redshift events, with the improvement in precision saturating for sources above $z \sim 1$; beyond that redshift, the constraining power of BSs is increasingly limited by the degeneracy with $\Omega_m$, which prevents further gains in precision on $H_0$. In this case, approximately $90$ low-redshift BSs are required to reach $\sigma_{H_0} \sim 1\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, while about $45$ are sufficient for $\sigma_{H_0} \sim 2\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$. When external BAO information is included to reduce the $H_0 - \Omega_m$ degeneracy, intermediate-redshift sirens become more informative and the required number of events decreases substantially, to roughly $20$ and $15$ BSs for $\sigma_{H_0} \sim 1\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $\sigma_{H_0} \sim 2\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, respectively. These results highlight the importance of both electromagnetic counterpart identification and complementary background probes in making BSs a competitive, distance-ladder-independent test of the Hubble tension.

authors.name: Chiara De Leo, Elsa M. Teixeira, Vivian Poulin

papers.title: The Influence of Dust Composition on Accretion Outbursts
papers.summary: Context: Episodic accretion outbursts have been shown to occur in protoplanetary discs due to thermal instability at the inner edge of the dead zone. These outbursts periodically heat up the dead zone, significantly altering the composition/chemistry and accretion onto the star. Aims: We investigate how these accretion outbursts affect the inner disc composition and how different dust compositions and properties affect the outbursts' dynamics. Methods: We run vertically integrated axis-symmetric dust and gas evolution models using the TriPoD method, including dust opacity dependent heating and cooling, a dead zone model, and compositional tracking of dust, including the evaporation and condensation of volatiles. Results: When considering dust to be made up of a condensation sequence of silicates and volatiles, the outburst evaporates most of the dust within 0.5 au. The fast re-condensation and subsequent viscous evolution reset the disc between bursts. Additionally, we find that the burst cycle period and maximal accretion rate directly correlate with the dust sublimation temperature.

authors.name: Nicolas Kaufmann, Anna B. T. Penzlin, Alfie Robinson, Alexandros Ziampras, Tilman Birnstiel, Richard Booth

papers.title: The X-ray catalogue of FGK stars within 10 pc: The coronal temperature-brightness relation explained with the RTV scaling law
papers.summary: A comprehensive measurement of stellar X-ray emission has important implications for our understanding of stellar dynamos, exoplanet atmosphere loss, and evaporation of protoplanetary disks. We present a catalogue of X-ray detections of the FGK-type main-sequence stars within 10 pc, which accounts for stellar multiplicity and optical loading of the detectors. To build the X-ray catalogue, we analysed all observations from SRG (Spectrum Roentgen Gamma)/eROSITA and XMM-Newton for stars in the FGK 10pc sample, and we cross-matched the sample with ROSAT catalogues. We fit thermal plasma models to the X-ray spectra to derive X-ray fluxes and coronal temperatures. We investigate the relation between coronal temperature and X-ray surface flux and find the result to be consistent with the ranges covered by different types of solar coronal magnetic structures. The lower end of the temperature-brightness relation is defined by the Maunder minimum star HD 166620 and three other stars whose positions identify them as possible Maunder minimum candidates. We identify systematic differences between the temperature-brightness law derived from XMM-Newton and eROSITA data that we attribute to their different instrumental response functions. We study the impact of both short-term flaring and long-term activity cycles on the evolution of coronal temperature along with X-ray brightness. With the exception of three stars, a remarkably small scatter is observed in the temperature-brightness relation across the whole sample. A natural explanation of the empirical kT-FX relation is provided by the RTV scaling laws defined for solar magnetic loops. The small spread of the observed relation indicates a universal scaling between the length and the filling factor of coronal loops. The three observed outliers deviate from this invariance of the ratio of loop length to filling factor for an as of yet unknown reason.

authors.name: M. M. Bennedik, B. Stelzer, M. Caramazza, S. Orlando, A. Binks, J. Robrade

papers.title: Binary neutron stars in the next-generation era: multimessenger detection prospects and constraints on the equation of state, mass distribution, and cosmology
papers.summary: Next-generation gravitational-wave (GW) observatories will provide crucial insights into the nature of neutron star (NS) matter and the cosmological expansion history. We estimate the number of multimessenger detections of binary neutron stars (BNS) with the Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) and project the resulting constraints on the equation of state (EOS), BNS mass distribution, and cosmology using joint hierarchical Bayesian inference. Our results rely on specific assumptions for the merger rate, EOS, and mass distribution; we consider two different mass functions, a narrow one centred around 1.4 $M_\odot$ and a wide one ranging from 1.1 to 2 $M_\odot$, and a merger rate with a local value of 107 Gpc$^{-3}$ yr$^{-1}$. Under this setup, our mock follow-up algorithm results in between $\sim40$ and $\sim100$ short-term electromagnetic counterparts per year for ET, depending on the detector layout and mass distribution. In a joint network with CE, this number ranges from $\sim 100$ to $\sim500$. Additionally, we project tens to hundreds of late-time afterglow detections from gamma-ray bursts or kilonovae (KNe). Based on the generated multimessenger events, we perform an injection campaign to hierarchically recover the EOS, mass distribution, and cosmology in a fully Bayesian framework. Focusing on KN events from ET alone, the multimessenger data from our largest analysed catalogue with 78 events can constrain the canonical NS radius $R_{1.4}$ to $\lesssim 0.2$ km and the Hubble constant $H_0$ to $\lesssim 1$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, at least in absence of systematic modelling offsets. By comparing inference results that are solely based on GW data and those incorporating light-curve information, we find that while the latter has negligible impact on the EOS constraints, it can benefit the inference of cosmological parameters.

authors.name: Hauke Koehn, Thibeau Wouters, Gilad Sadeh, Peter T. H. Pang, Mattia Bulla, Chris Van Den Broeck, Michael W. Coughlin, Tim Dietrich

papers.title: Interacting Supernovae: a Radio and X-ray Strategy to Constrain the Structure of the Circumstellar Medium
papers.summary: The interaction of supernova (SN) ejecta with the dense circumstellar medium (CSM) converts shock kinetic energy into radiation across multiple wavebands. We investigate the dependence of the X-ray and radio emission on the CSM geometry, considering spherical, hourglass, and disk shapes for the CSM. We find that the spectral and light-curve properties, both in X-ray and radio, significantly differ for spherical and non-spherical CSM structures. For a non-spherical CSM, the radio light curve flattens out near the peak frequency, due to efficient free-free absorption by the unshocked CSM. Moreover, the early rise of the radio light curve is shallower when the CSM density along the observer line of sight is larger than that in other directions. If the CSM density is lower along the observer line of sight, the radio light curve flattens near its peak, and the reverse-shock component is negligible in X-rays. Building on these features, we provide a method to constrain the CSM structure based on the rising part the radio light curve in the proximity of its peak; we show that the decay part of the radio light curve, after its peak, carries insight on whether the CSM density profile is wind-like or not. We further adopt the X-ray signal to corroborate the information extracted from radio. We test our strategy on SN 1993j and SN 2023ixf. For both SNe, we find that an asymmetric CSM is in excellent agreement with radio and X-ray observations and provides a viable alternative to non-wind scenarios suggested in the literature. Our findings highlight the crucial insight provided by radio and X-ray signals into the mass-loss history of the SN progenitor.

authors.name: Shunke Ai, Irene Tamborra, Leonardo Dinoi

papers.title: Why is GN-z11 Bright, Compact, and Nitrogen Enhanced? Insights from UV Absorption and Emission Diagnostics
papers.summary: We investigate the UV spectrum of GN-z11, a luminous, compact galaxy with strong nitrogen lines, at $z=10.60$, using deep JWST/NIRSpec high-resolution IFU and medium-resolution MSA spectra assembled from the JADES, SPURS, and GO programs. After optimized reduction and extraction of the IFU data including an evaluation of statistical and systematic uncertainties, we obtain mutually consistent spectra from the high- and medium-resolution observations. After carefully accounting for the data quality limitations, we identify prominent P-Cygni profiles in NV$\lambda\lambda1238,1243$, SiIV$\lambda\lambda1394,1403$, and CIV$\lambda\lambda1548,1550$, together with broad NIV]$\lambda\lambda1483,1486$ emission (FWHM $\sim1600$ km s$^{-1}$). The P-Cygni profiles resemble those of massive stars such as O-type stars and luminous blue variables (LBVs), while the broad NIV] emission resembles that of nitrogen-sequence Wolf-Rayet (WN) stars. We fit stellar and active galactic nuclei (AGN) UV spectral models and find that the stellar models are strongly preferred over the AGN models ($\Delta$WAIC $=-20$), with the preference driven primarily by the NV P-Cygni profile. These results indicate that the luminous, compact UV continuum of GN-z11 is dominated by massive stars. We derive electron densities from CIII]$\lambda\lambda1907,1909$, NIII]$\lambda\lambda1747-1754$, and NIV], with the nitrogen diagnostics extending well beyond the CIII]-based limit and reaching densities of $\gtrsim10^{6.5}$ cm$^{-3}$ for NIV], indicating physically distinct carbon- and nitrogen-emitting nebular components. These findings suggest that the apparent nitrogen enhancement inferred for GN-z11 as a whole may arise when strong narrow nitrogen emission originates from dense gas locally enriched in nitrogen by WN stellar winds and photoionized by nearby massive stars within the same star-forming region.

authors.name: Minami Nakane, Masami Ouchi

papers.title: The descendants of $z \gtrsim 10$ JWST galaxies in the COLIBRE simulations
papers.summary: Recent observations with JWST have revealed a population of UV-bright galaxies at $z\gtrsim 10$. This discovery naturally raises the question: what do such early galaxies evolve into by the present day? In this work, we address this descendant question using the new-generation COLIBRE cosmological hydrodynamical simulations to trace bright galaxies selected at $z=10$ and follow their descendants to the present day. Most of the high-redshift galaxies do not survive as distinct, self-bound objects to $z=0$; instead, the majority are incorporated into more massive systems through merging or disruption. The surviving descendants span a broad range of present-day stellar masses, although they are most commonly intermediate- to high-mass, $M_\star\sim10^{10}$--$10^{11} M_\odot$. They typically reside in galaxy groups and clusters, with host halo masses, $M_{200c}\sim10^{13}$--$10^{14} M_\odot$. The large scatter in descendant stellar mass shows that present-day outcomes retain only a weak memory of the stellar mass of the high-redshift progenitor. We show that the evolution of descendant host halo masses is consistent with the forward conditional distribution predicted by extended Press--Schechter (EPS) theory, both in the median growth and in the large scatter in descendant mass. In particular, EPS confirms that massive present-day galaxies typically do not originate from the most massive objects at high redshift. A galaxy observed at $z\gtrsim10$ therefore cannot be interpreted as the direct progenitor of a single class of $z=0$ galaxies.

authors.name: Xu Zhao, Carlos S. Frenk, Andrew Pontzen, Kyle A. Oman, Evgenii Chaikin, Isabel Santos-Santos, Shengdong Lu, Joop Schaye, Alejandro Ben\'itez-Llambay, Filip Hu\v{s}ko, Alexander J. Richings, Matthieu Schaller

papers.title: SN 2025aedz: A typical short-plateau type IIP supernova with rapid post-peak decline
papers.summary: Type IIP supernovae (SNe IIP) are the most common subclass of core-collapse SNe in observations. However, SNe IIP with short plateaus of the order of tens of days are rarely observed. The progenitors for this kind of SN can help to address the red supergiant issue in stellar evolution. In this article, we report optical photometry and spectroscopy of SN\,2025aedz, a rapidly post-peak declining SN IIP with a typical short plateau. It exhibits a peak absolute magnitude of $M_r=-17.16\pm0.03$\,mag. The $r$-band light curve shows a steep early post-peak decline of $\sim5\,\mathrm{mag}\,(100\,\mathrm{d})^{-1}$ followed by a relatively short plateau, with a plateau duration of $\sim50\pm3$\,d. The overall spectral evolution is consistent with that of normal SNe~IIP, showing a blue continuum with prominent Balmer P-Cygni profiles during the photospheric phase, followed by the gradual strengthening of hydrogen and metal lines as the ejecta cools down, although the metal lines remain weak and the expansion velocities decline rapidly. SN\,2025aedz is similar to the short-plateau SN\,2018gj in its overall evolution, whereas its pronounced early decline resembles that of SN\,2023ufx, which has the shortest plateau duration known so far. The radioactive tail of the bolometric light curve implies a synthesized $^{56}$Ni mass of $\sim0.03\pm0.01\,M_\odot$. Motivated by the steep early decline, we performed radiation hydrodynamic modelling using \texttt{MESA+STELLA} by exploring different circumstellar material configurations to reproduce its early bolometric light curve. These simulations indicate that SN\,2025aedz originated from a progenitor with a relatively low-mass hydrogen envelope, possibly produced through enhanced mass loss or binary interaction, while the steep early decline is likely explained by additional luminosity from circumstellar interaction.

authors.name: Bo Wang, Luhan Li, Chengyuan Wu, Jujia Zhang, Yongzhi Cai, Yize Dong, Xuefei Chen, Zhanwen Han

papers.title: 3D Global Climate Simulations of Synthetic Mars Warming
papers.summary: Artificial warming via engineered aerosols presents a novel pathway to bypass volatile scarcity on modern Mars. Utilizing the Generic Planetary Climate Model, we evaluate the physical feasibility of aerosol-induced terraforming over a full Martian year (669 Sols). Unlike previous approaches that added aerosols to background dust or assumed continuous nanoparticle injection, we simulate the complete substitution of natural dust with a single-injection profile of radiatively active aluminium nanoparticles without continuous dumping. This tests whether initial infrared greenhouse forcing can overcome the severe ice-albedo cooling induced by a massive regional water-ice sheet ($3400 \text{ kg/m}^2$) localized in the Hellas Basin. Comparing this scenario against an unperturbed control run, we analyze surface temperature dynamics, sublimation fluxes, and water vapour concentration. Our 3D global climate simulations quantify the radiative-dynamical feedback thresholds and determine whether engineered aerosol forcing can trigger a self-sustaining water-vapour greenhouse effect or remains fundamentally limited by regional ice-albedo suppression in Hellas.

authors.name: Tom N. Landefeld, Harald Lesch

papers.title: First L-type Substellar Object Discovered in the Vicinity of the Embedded Cluster NGC 2023
papers.summary: We present the first substellar object in a star-forming region spectroscopically confirmed with Euclid, namely J054158.70-021031.4. This young and faint source is located close to the embedded open cluster NGC 2023. It has a spectral type of L3, a reddening of $A_V = 3$ mag, proper motion consistent with the nearby cluster NGC 2024, and a magnitude of $\sim24.5$ in the Euclid optical band. At the distance of 403 pc, its inferred mass lies close to the planetary-mass boundary. We discovered the object by searching for ultracool dwarf candidates in the Euclid Early Release Observations. The search was based on photometric criteria, followed by the analysis of slitless 2D spectroimages in order to distinguish features that indicate the nature of these objects. This work demonstrates the potential of Euclid to unveil previously hidden populations of very low-mass objects, located in obscured regions where star formation is ongoing.

authors.name: Styliani Tsilia, Carlos Dominguez-Tagle, Maru\v{s}a \v{Z}erjal, Eduardo L. Mart\'in, Herv\'e Bouy, Nafise Sedighi, Sara Mu\~noz Torres, Nikola Vitas, Khalid Barkaoui, Nicolas Lodieu, Jerry J. -Y. Zhang

papers.title: A first look at the protoplanet WISPIT 2 b with VLTI/GRAVITY+
papers.summary: Confirmed observations of young protoplanets actively undergoing the process of formation have remained rare to date. In this article, we present new insights into the nature of the recently identified protoplanet WISPIT 2 b (age $\sim5$ Myr) from Very Large Telescope Interferometer/GRAVITY+ observations. Through analysis of the spectral energy distribution (SED) and astrometry of WISPIT 2 b, with the inclusion of new GRAVITY+ data, we investigated the nature of the protoplanet's thermal emission and orbital properties. We performed an orbit fit with the inclusion of new high-precision GRAVITY+ astrometry to provide an updated orbital solution. We also analyzed the medium resolution GRAVITY+ $K$ band spectrum in combination with new Very Large Telescope/SPHERE and literature photometry, exploring both the atmospheric properties and the constraints on the circumplanetary environment. Finally, we checked for any signal from a resolved circumplanetary disk in the GRAVITY+ data. We detected the protoplanet WISPIT 2 b at $\sim322$ mas separation from its host star. The new GRAVITY+ astrometry prefers an orbit with moderate eccentricity. Analysis of the SED reveals an effective temperature in the 900 to 1300 K regime and a slight preference for atmospheric models including clouds over pure blackbody emission. The new GRAVITY+ observations independently confirm WISPIT 2 b as a self-luminous and point-like companion that resides within the gap of the transitional disk at $\sim60$ au from its host star. Further observations - either at higher signal-to-noise ratios or at longer wavelengths - are required to characterize the atmosphere and examine the presence of circumplanetary material from thermal emission of the dust.

papers.title: Convective Oscillations of Cosmic Rays
papers.summary: Turbulent motion of the background plasma can introduce fluctuations in the spatial distribution of cosmic rays (CRs). For an ensemble-averaged Gaussian CR distribution with a width $ \Lambda\left( t,p \right) $ at time $ t $ and momentum $ p $, it is found that $ P_\text{s}\left( t,k,p \right) $ and $ P_\text{d}\left( t,k,p \right) $, the fluctuation power spectra induced by incompressible and acoustic turbulent convection, respectively, have power-law asymptotics in wavenumber $ k $: $ P_\text{s}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^4 $ and $ P_\text{d}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^2 $ for $ k\ll 1/\Lambda\left( t,p \right) $; $ P_\text{s}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^{\gamma _\text{s}-4} $ for $ k\gg 1/L_\text{s} $, and $ P_\text{d}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^{\gamma _\text{d}-2} $ for $ k\gg 1/L_\text{d} $, where $ \gamma _\text{s} $ and $ \gamma _\text{d} $ are the spectral indices of the velocity power spectra of the incompressible and acoustic turbulence below their outer scales $ L_\text{s} $ and $ L_\text{d} $, respectively. These results have implications for probing interstellar turbulence via future high-resolution images of pulsar gamma-ray halos.

authors.name: Yiran Zhang, Siming Liu

papers.title: How reliable are automated X-ray reflection spins of supermassive black holes? A methodological study of 41 AGN with simultaneous \xmm\ and \nustar\ data
papers.summary: This is a methodological study: we test how reliable black hole spins from an automated, uniform reflection analysis are, not how spins are distributed. We fit one simultaneous XMM-Newton EPIC-pn and NuSTAR observation of each of 41 AGN with relxillCp, a distant reflector and a warm-Comptonisation soft excess, using quality criteria fixed in advance, 20 starting points, spin profiles scanned in both directions and two-dimensional (spin, inclination) grids. We test whether the relativistic reflection is detected, and test every result against four changes to the model, two sensitivity tests, two alternative models (a high-density disc and a lamppost corona) and simulations. The disc reflection is not detected in 21 of the 41 sources, and 5 sources pass all checks. Their 90% spin regions are 1 lower bound (NGC 4051, a*>0.75), 1 upper bound, 2 regions in separate pieces and 1 unconstrained profile; none is a two-sided interval. The accepted fits lie at 32-56 deg. No constrained region keeps its type under all of the inclination limit, the removal of pn data below 3 keV, and the two alternative models, so the spin depends on how the soft excess and the corona are modelled. In two accepted sources, including NGC 4051, the disc component is detected mainly below 2 keV rather than in the iron band. Of the 18 sources accepted by a previous version of this analysis without a soft-excess component, 14 are not accepted, 11 because their disc reflection is not detected; none of the accepted fits is now edge-on (10 of 18 before). In simulations with known spin the 90% regions contain the true spin in 0.82 of cases when the model is correct; fitting the previous model to spectra simulated from the new one gives spuriously high spins and, for one of two templates, edge-on inclinations. The sample is not complete, and we make no statement about the spin distribution.

authors.name: K. Balasubramaniam, H. -K. Chang, {\L}. Stawarz

papers.title: Temporal regularization of petal modes in single conjugate adaptive optics systems: The soft-limiter approach
papers.summary: Extremely large telescopes (ELTs) rely on segmented mirrors and thick support structures that fragment the pupil. In single-conjugate AO (SCAO), this produces differential pistons, or petal modes. The Pyramid Wavefront Sensor (PWFS), baseline for ANDES, MICADO, HARMONI, and GMT-NGSAO, has poor sensitivity to these modes in the visible under realistic residual turbulence. We aim to prevent the "Island Effect", where poorly observed differential pistons accumulate and degrade the PSF, without compromising continuous-mode correction. We propose the Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) Soft-Limiter, a deterministic, lightweight controller combining a subspace MMSE estimator derived from von K\'arm\'an priors with a continuous temporal regularization. It acts as a leaky integrator applied only to the relative petal degrees of freedom. End-to-end SPECULA simulations of ELT/ANDES show that, while a classical integrator loses lock and wanders across multiple fringes at seeing $\ge 1.0''$, the MMSE Soft-Limiter confines the differential piston within a single fringe over the $0.6-1.2''$ range. It bounds the petal excursion and its science-band impact under severe turbulence, while keeping optimal continuous-mode correction at good seeing, without the Strehl penalty of spatial mitigation such as Edge Actuator Coupling. We derive and verify the operating window for the leakage gain, $g \lesssim g_{\mathrm{eff}}/\pi$: below it, the fast loop retains genuine physical steps up to $\lambda_{WFS}/2$ with a small droop. This maintains a stable modulo-$\lambda_{WFS}$ wavefront on the fast sensor, letting a slower phasing sensor resolve integer ambiguities. As the window narrows with turbulence, its boundaries cross near $1.0''$ seeing; beyond this, retaining physical discontinuities becomes the sole responsibility of the phasing channel, a key design driver for segmented ELTs.

authors.name: Guido Agapito, Jueqi Lin, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Giulia Carl\`a, Enrico Pinna, Fabio Rossi

papers.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
papers.summary: Intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies are an important source of systematic uncertainty in weak gravitational lensing measurements and also serve as a test for models of galaxy formation and evolution. These galaxy alignments are usually modeled assuming that the IA are sourced by the tidal fields around the galaxies. However, galaxy properties, like their proximity to other galaxies and their mass, provide alignment contributions beyond the tidal field. In this work, we perform novel model-agnostic tests to determine the impact of density-weighting on the IA of galaxies using data from the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and SDSS-III (BOSS). We show that the primary effect of density-weighting is an increase of the alignment amplitude at large scales, whereas the small-scale impact is sample-dependent. We also assess the tidal alignment paradigm for IllustrisTNG galaxies using two-point correlation functions of galaxy shapes, tidal fields, and the sampled background tidal field of the simulation box. We find, given the precision of our measurements, that central galaxies align linearly to the underlying (non-linear) tidal field well into the 1-halo regime.

authors.name: Paul Rogozenski, Sukhdeep Singh, Jonathan Blazek, Rachel Mandelbaum, Hung-Jin Huang, Ananth Tenneti

papers.title: Fast and accurate false-alarm probabilities for linear detection statistics in Poisson noise
papers.summary: Detecting weak signals in noisy data often requires calculating the statistical significance, or false- alarm probability, of a detection statistic. When the underlying noise follows Poisson statistics, as in low-count measurements such as photon-starved astronomical images, this calculation becomes non- trivial, and existing approaches typically rely on extensive simulations to estimate detection thresholds. We derive an accurate and efficient solution for computing false-alarm probabilities for arbitrary linear detection statistics under Poisson noise. We show that the detection statistic is a compound Poisson random variable, which unlocks efficient implementations based on the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and the Panjer recursion. The method is exact up to numerical discretization, accelerates computation by several orders of magnitude compared with simulations, and enables evaluation of false-alarm probabilities computationally inaccessible through simulation. Although motivated by low-count astronomical imaging, the framework applies broadly to detection problems involving Poisson-distributed events. It transforms the computation of detection significance under Poisson noise from a simulation problem into a deterministic numerical calculation. We provide open-source Python and MATLAB implementations.

papers.title: Coherent radio emission at 45 MHz from the nearby planet-hosting star GJ 725A
papers.summary: Ultra-low-frequency (<100 MHz) coherent radio emission from exoplanet-hosting stellar systems carries information about planetary and stellar magnetic fields, as well as the space weather environment - information that is difficult to obtain at other wavelengths. We carried out the circularly polarized LOFAR LBA Sky Survey, the most sensitive circularly polarized survey in this frequency range, using the LOFAR low-band antenna system. As part of this untargeted search, we detected a signal in a 1h observation that is coincident with the quiescent, planet-hosting, solar-neighborhood M dwarf GJ 725A at a distance of 3.5 pc. The signal has a high circular polarization fraction of $74\pm16$% and a peak brightness of $B=135\pm17$ mJy/beam between 42 MHz and 50 MHz. It was undetected in the 50-66 MHz range, with a 3$\sigma$ upper limit of $B<48$ mJy/beam, corresponding to a drop of at least a factor 3 across 12 MHz, and indicating a strong spectral feature or cutoff around 50 MHz. Our detection represents the lowest-frequency confirmed detection of a stellar system. Based on the high estimated brightness temperature ($\sim10^{14}$ K), transient character and polarization fraction, the emission is most plausibly attributed to the electron cyclotron maser instability. The available observations are not sufficient to identify the astrophysical origin of the emission. We consider three plausible scenarios: auroral emission of a yet undetected wide-orbit giant planet with a magnetic field $B\geq18$ G, star-planet interaction with the known 11 d orbit terrestrial planet GJ 725Ab, or an origin due to stellar magnetic activity. Ultra-low-frequency monitoring, combined with new, preferably simultaneous observations in the X-rays, UV, and H$\alpha$, and a search for a wide-orbit (thousands of days) giant planet across the full allowed parameter space will allow us to distinguish between these scenarios.

papers.title: Fundamental Noise Processes in Pulsar Timing
papers.summary: The stability of spin rates and emission regions of radio-emitting neutron stars (pulsars) has enabled remarkable advances, including the detection of exoplanets, testing theories of gravity, and stimulating the vigorous exploration of a new window in gravitational wave astronomy an nanohertz frequencies. An ideal astrophysical clock would emit identical pulses at a constant rate, propagating along single geodesics through a perfect vacuum. In reality, the timing precision achievable with pulsars is limited by spin noise, variability in the beam produced in a complex magnetosphere, and multipath propagation through a turbulent interstellar medium, with additional limitations from uncertainties in the changing pulsar -- observatory vector and instrumental effects. Here we present the fundamentals of pulsar timing, its current limitations, and prospects for improvements in timing precision. We develop metrics to assess the timing quality of a pulsar and use them to evaluate sources currently included in pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) as a means for characterizing the quality of future pulsar discoveries. With increases in telescope sensitivity, pulsar timing precision will increasingly be limited by propagation effects in the interstellar medium. We identify sources of non-Gaussianity in timing residuals and separate out effects that are chromatic or achromatic, as well as effects that vary on short (seconds to minutes) and longer (days to months) timescales. Modern wide-bandwidth receivers provide simultaneous arrival times across a range of frequencies, enabling the robust mitigation of chromatic interstellar effects and the identification of non-Gaussian events superimposed on random fluctuations. We recommend changes to timing procedures that leverage instrumentation advances to improve timing precision.

papers.title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) -- Bayesian 3D shape inference of star-forming galaxy populations
papers.summary: Understanding the intrinsic 3D shapes of galaxies provides crucial insights into their formation and evolution, but determining these from projections remains challenging. We apply a Bayesian inference framework to optical images of galaxies from the Euclid Data Release 1, leveraging its large sample size to test the scalability and robustness of this methodology. Applying Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling to S\'ersic axis ratios and effective radii, we constrain the population-level mean 3D ellipticity, triaxiality, and size, together with their covariances for $40\,864\,304$ star-forming galaxies with stellar masses $M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{10.5}M_\odot$ at redshifts $0<z<1.2$. Our sample size exceeds previous shape inference studies by factors of $440$--$52\,800$ relative to early observations by JWST, and factors of $440$--$17\,600$ relative to legacy observations from HST in overlapping mass-redshift bins, enabling finer binning alongside improved statistical constraints on shape evolution. We additionally include over 9 million galaxies at $z<0.5$, a regime historically limited by sample size in previous shape inference studies. We recover key evolutionary trends identified in previous smaller-sample studies. We find high ellipticities ($\mu_E \sim 0.600$--$0.821$) across all bins, indicating that the underlying 3D shape distributions are statistically dominated by flattened geometries. Most notably, we recover the decline of the prolate fraction towards $z=0$ at low masses ($M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{9.5}M_\odot$) reported by previous studies. This trend is seen consistently in comparable analyses of independent data sets spanning different depths and resolution regimes, showing that it is not an artefact of small-sample statistics, suggesting it may be a genuine feature of galaxy evolution. We also identify future methodological improvements for subsequent Euclid data releases.

papers.title: Minimal vacuum histories beyond $\Lambda$CDM: model comparison within VCDM
papers.summary: Recent cosmological observations motivate alternatives to $\Lambda$CDM with evolving dark energy. We compare three such models, each introducing one additional cosmological parameter: F42, with equation of state $w(a)=w_0/\sqrt{a}$, and two smooth sign-changing effective dark-energy profiles, Ag and Qui. All models are implemented within VCDM, which determines the background and linear perturbations without introducing an additional propagating gravitational degree of freedom. We use CMB observations from SPT, Planck, and ACT, combined with DESI DR2 distance measurements, with and without the DESY5 Dovekie supernova sample. All three alternatives improve the best-fit likelihood relative to $\Lambda$CDM. When supernovae are included, the Akaike information criterion favors F42, while Ag and Qui remain nearly indistinguishable from $\Lambda$CDM on this criterion. The Bayesian evidence, however, does not establish a robust preference among the three alternatives. Our results show that improved fits to current observations can arise from physically different dark-energy histories, motivating complementary measurements of expansion and structure growth to distinguish them.

authors.name: Antonio De Felice, Eleonora Di Valentino, Luis A. Escamilla, Jack Zidich

papers.title: Radiation, Thermochemistry, and Stellar Feedback in DISPATCH
papers.summary: The growth of massive stars depends on whether their accretion flows survive radiation and outflow feedback from the forming stellar population. We present an extension of DISPATCH that couples directional stellar radiation, diffuse infrared transport, and thermochemistry to self-gravitating magnetohydrodynamics, individual stellar accretion, and protostellar jets. This AMR-based method uses DISPATCH's local timestepping, allowing stellar environments and their larger scale cluster environments to step on separate timescales, and providing the framework needed to scale to long-duration simulations of GMCs. Direct radiation is transported in multiple bands, including both ionizing and nonionizing radiation, and uses short characteristics to maintain source directions and shadowing. Diffuse radiation is implemented for IR reprocessed light, with M1 and stationary ray options for transport. The thermochemical model includes atomic and molecular hydrogen and helium chemistry, and metal cooling and dust. It also includes a composition-dependent equation of state. Stellar masses grow through accretion of gas rather than a prescribed IMF, allowing stellar masses to respond to the evolving gas supply and feedback. In tests, multiple-source illumination retains geometric shadows while diffuse reprocessing heats shielded material, and tests of jets, ionization fronts, and radiation pressure demonstrate expected behavior and convergence. Ionization fronts also cross asynchronous refinement boundaries with late-time propagation speeds within a few percent of analytic predictions. Together, these developments provide a framework for determining how radiative and mechanical feedback modify the duration and efficiency of accretion from turbulent clouds, connecting the gas supply to individual stars with the high-mass stellar initial mass function.

authors.name: William Lake, Paolo Padoan, {\AA}ke Nordlund, Troels Haugb{\o}lle

papers.title: Probing (sub-)solar-mass black holes and superspinars with current and next-generation gravitational-wave observatories
papers.summary: We investigate the detectability and parameter estimation prospects of (sub-)solar-mass collapsed binaries with current and next-generation gravitational wave detectors, allowing the dimensionless component spins to extend phenomenologically beyond the Kerr bound, $(|\chi|>1$) (where $\chi$ is the spin parameter). Using the inspiral-only TaylorF2 waveform and a Fisher-matrix analysis, we study binaries with component masses in the range $0.1\!-\!2\,M_\odot$ and compare the performance of Advanced LIGO with that of a third-generation network consisting of Cosmic Explorer and the Einstein Telescope. We find that third-generation detectors substantially improve the signal-to-noise ratio and the measurement of intrinsic binary parameters, particularly the component spins, while also providing significantly improved sky localization. For favorable configurations, the primary spin can be measured with precision $\Delta\chi_{1z}\sim10^{-3}-10^{-2}$, demonstrating enhanced sensitivity to potential Kerr-bound violations. However, strong anti-correlations between the component spins limit the interpretation of small marginalized spin uncertainties as definitive evidence for superspinars. We also examine formation scenarios for (sub-)solar-mass collapsed binaries and show that dense dark-matter environments, particularly the Galactic Centre, can significantly enhance their formation and merger rates. Our results demonstrate the potential of future gravitational wave observations to probe low-mass collapsed objects and possible departures from the Kerr bound, while highlighting the need for physically consistent superspinar waveform models and Bayesian model comparison for a definitive interpretation.

authors.name: K. S. Sruthy, N. V. Krishnendu, Chandrachur Chakraborty, Nami Uchikata

papers.title: The inclination cross-check: binary-pulsar timing and gravitational-wave polarimetry
papers.summary: Radio timing and gravitational-wave (GW) polarimetry provide independent measurements of a binary's inclination. We study their consistency through $\eps=s_{\rm Shapiro}-s_{\rm GW}$, where $s_{\rm Shapiro}$ is the Shapiro-delay shape and $s_{\rm GW}$ is inferred from the tensor polarization amplitudes. We combine a time-dependent, finite-arm detector response with radio timing averaged over each integration, retaining the amplitude--inclination covariance and the nonlinear orientation posteriors. For hypothetical 15-minute binaries at 5 kpc and $65^\circ$ inclination, four years of GW data and a 125-h radio campaign give $\sigma_\eps=5.4\times10^{-3}$ for a double neutron star and $1.0\times10^{-3}$ for a pulsar--black-hole binary when two static timing harmonics are fitted. An apsidally evolving radio model with $e=0.01$ and a free apsidal rate gives $4.5\times10^{-3}$ and $0.94\times10^{-3}$, respectively, with the circular GW covariance held fixed. Changes in the relative tensor amplitudes can be absorbed by the GW fit as an apparent inclination shift and revealed by the radio measurement. An inaccurate detector response can produce a similar discrepancy even when its Fisher errors are nearly unchanged. These forecasts use the $n=2$ GW harmonic and assume a fixed orbital plane, sustained radio visibility, and the specified timing precision; additional harmonics can provide further orientation information.

authors.name: Bhooshan Gadre

papers.title: Joule-Thomson Effect and Geodesic Structure of Charged AdS Black Holes in f(R,T) Coupled with Nonlinear Electrodynamics
papers.summary: We herein study both the Joule-Thomson (JT) expansion process and the geodesic properties of a charged anti-de Sitter (AdS) black hole arising in modified gravity with nonlinear electrodynamic (NLED) sources. Our thermodynamic study reveals that the black hole charge has the most pronounced impact on the JT behaviour. The nonlinear electromagnetic sector together with the modified gravity parameters introduces further corrections to the inversion temperature and the associated cooling characteristics. At astrophysically relevant distances, the geometry closely reproduces expected outcomes.

authors.name: Shyamalee Bora, Dhruba Jyoti Gogoi, Pralay Kumar Karmakar

papers.title: Dendro-GR at high mass ratios with high spins
papers.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) launches in less than a decade; it will detect spinning high-mass-ratio binary black hole inspirals annually, alongside other third-generation gravitational wave detectors. High-mass-ratio systems occupy a regime where numerical-relativity simulations remain computationally expensive and technically demanding, especially with high spins at precessing orientations. This portion of parameter space thus remains undersampled, leading to significant bias in parameter estimation. We must close these gaps. Here we report key progress in Dendro-GR toward reducing the computational cost of high-mass-ratio binaries with spin. We evolve the first Dendro-GR binaries at mass ratio $q=24$ (nonspinning) and at $q=12$ with spins up to $\chi=0.8$ on both black holes, spanning various configurations. These proof-of-concept runs show strong evidence that Dendro-GR can simulate in this regime and beyond. The simulations resolve the expected multipolar hierarchy in the gravitational waveforms through multipole modes up to $\ell=8$, remain stable, keep constraint violations low and largely constant, conserve horizon mass, and have high computational efficiency with relatively low wall-hour cost. These results establish our starting line for systematic exploration of the high-mass-ratio, high-spin binary black hole systems that are needed for gravitational wave analysis.

authors.name: William K. Black, David Neilsen, Eric W. Hirschmann, David F. Van Komen

papers.title: Accretion onto a moving black hole for stiff equations of state
papers.summary: We revisit accretion of an asymptotically uniform fluid onto a moving Schwarzschild black hole, the relativistic analog of Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion. Expanding on previous treatments, we focus on relativistic accretion of stiff fluids with adiabatic indices $\Gamma \geq 5/3$, which is particularly relevant for the treatment of primordial black holes captured by neutron stars. We perform numerical simulations to systematically explore the dependence of the steady-state accretion and drag rates on the asymptotic sound speed $a_\infty$ and relative speed $v_\infty$, and identify different regimes, both subsonic and supersonic, in which these rates either increase or decrease with respect to the spherical accretion rate for $v_\infty = 0$. We propose simple analytical approximations that capture the qualitative features observed in the dependence of the accretion and drag rates on $a_\infty$ and $v_\infty$.

authors.name: Elliott Ewell, Peter K. Harris, Thomas W. Baumgarte, Stuart L. Shapiro

papers.title: Coexistence of strange quark stars and neutron stars: metastability and nucleation in proto-neutron stars
papers.summary: If strange quark matter (SQM) is absolutely stable, hadronic neutron stars (NSs) and strange quark stars (QSs) may coexist in the so-called two-families scenario. A key issue is explaining how hadronic NSs can survive as long-lived metastable objects, rather than promptly converting into stable QSs. Since all NSs are born as hot proto-neutron stars (PNSs), a necessary condition for their existence is that the conditions for conversion, triggered by the nucleation of the first critical SQM droplet, are not reached in every PNS. We investigate the thermal nucleation of critical SQM droplets under representative PNS conditions, accounting for flavor-composition fluctuations and finite-size effects on color superconductivity by suppressing pairing in droplets smaller than the diquark coherence length. We define the nucleation conditions as the thermodynamic state at which a critical SQM droplet is expected to nucleate statistically within the characteristic dynamical timescale of the system. Under these conditions, the reduced nucleation barrier is nearly universal, with $W_*/T\simeq167$ to within a few units. Exploring the SQM parameter space of a bag-like model, with a fixed hadronic EOS compatible with a recent Bayesian analysis of the two-families scenario, we find parametrizations and surface tensions for which a canonical $1.4\,\text{M}_{\odot}$ NS survives the PNS stage, a necessary condition for the two-families scenario. For this specific combination of hadronic and quark models, requiring such survival sets a lower bound on the hadron--quark surface tension, $\sigma\gtrsim 67\,\text{MeV}\,{\rm fm}^{-2}$.

authors.name: Mirco Guerrini, Giuseppe Pagliara, Luca Passarella, Alessandro Drago

papers.title: Trainable sparse dendritic networks reveal regime-dependent roles for shunting inhibition and morphology
papers.summary: Neural circuits must compute with noisy inputs and adapt their responses to context. How dendritic structure and synaptic integration support these functions remains unclear. We introduce DendriNet, a trainable rate-based framework with sparse excitatory and inhibitory contacts, controllable dendritic architecture and alternative integration rules. In image-classification tasks, shunting networks transmit and rely on distal dendritic signals more strongly than additive networks. Distributing limited contacts across compartments improves classification in small populations, whereas greater serial dendritic depth provides no benefit on clean images within resource-matched trees. Robustness depends on input statistics: deeper shunting trees better tolerate independent pixel noise, while addition better tolerates strong global scaling. In a contextual task with gain variation and noise, shunting improves accuracy under the training corruption but depends less on context-specific inhibition than a separately tuned additive network. Learning leak conductances partly restores shunting accuracy on dim, noise-free inputs outside the training distribution. At AlexNet width, shunting integration and learned sparse connectivity support smaller deployed networks with accuracy comparable to retrained dense layers. These results distinguish the local action of synaptic integration from the computational roles acquired by inhibitory pathways through learning, and suggest experiments on dendritic function and design principles for brain-inspired networks.

authors.name: Houman Safaai, Maceo Richards, Ryan Whalen, Adi Madduri, Naeem Khoshnevis, Bernardo L. Sabatini

papers.title: Domain-repetition patterns in protein domain trigrams are uniform across chromosomes and conserved among multicellular eukaryotes
papers.summary: Proteins are built from domains, and the order of domains along a protein can be read like a sentence. We take every run of three consecutive Pfam domains (a domain trigram) and classify it by its pattern of repetition: all three the same (AAA), the first two (AAB), the last two (ABB), the outer two (ABA) or all different (ABC). We ask whether the proportions of these five patterns are conserved across the chromosomes of a genome and across genomes. We built a reproducible workflow and applied it to the UniProt reference proteomes of 16 organisms, from Escherichia coli to human, with Pfam 39.0. In Drosophila melanogaster, 3,107 distinct trigrams split into 63% ABC, 13% each of AAB and ABB, and 5% each of AAA and ABA. Every chromosome arm closely matches this pie: each lies within the range expected for a random set of genes of the same size. The human pie has less ABC (55%) and more AAB and ABB (18% each), and 23 of its 25 chromosomes and other components fall within the random-gene range. Pies of trigram occurrences vary more, mostly because of a few giant repeat proteins.
