For a broad class of fixed-generator variational gates and terminal-state losses, we show that the batch Krotov direction coincides with the exact gradient of the empirical loss. Under standard smoothness assumptions, this yields monotonic descent and convergence of the batch method, and convergence of the tail of the hybrid method after a finite switch to the batch phase. Empirically, we benchmark hybrid Krotov against the tuned PennyLane optimizer suite and L-BFGS-B on a four-bit parity classifier and on the P\'erez-Salinas data re-uploading classifier for the crown problem. Across matched hyperparameter sweeps with three seeds per configuration, hybrid Krotov dominates every tuned first-order baseline and matches the strongest structured PennyLane methods on parity, while approaching the accuracy of L-BFGS-B on P\'erez-Salinas at first-order per-iteration cost.

authors.name: Maximilian Fr\"ohlich, Martin Eigel, Michael Hinterm\"uller

papers.title: Quantum algorithmic framework for finite element analysis of isotropic linear elastic materials via efficient block-encoding
papers.summary: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to accelerating large-scale numerical analysis, including the finite element method. However, its practical application requires efficient quantum circuit implementations of discretized linear systems. In this study, we develop a quantum algorithmic framework for two-dimensional isotropic linear elastic materials discretized using the finite element method. The key contribution is an explicit construction of a normalized block-encoding of the shifted global stiffness matrix, which is essential for applying a quantum linear system solver based on the quantum singular value transformation with improved dependence on the condition number. By analytically diagonalizing the element stiffness matrix and expressing the global stiffness matrix through a factorized finite element assembly, we construct the required block-encoding using a constant number of ancilla qubits and a gate complexity logarithmic in the number of degrees of freedom. We further analyze the computational complexity of displacement state preparation, strain energy estimation, and low-resolution displacement reconstruction, identifying conditions under which polynomial quantum speedups may be achieved. Numerical experiments on cantilever beam problems verify the accuracy of the proposed quantum circuits and demonstrate agreement with conventional finite element solutions. These results establish an explicit and resource-efficient quantum framework for finite element analysis of isotropic linear elastic materials.

authors.name: Yuki Sato, Ruho Kondo

papers.title: Quantum Preparation without Disturbance: Information Costs and Hypothesis Testing
papers.summary: We determine the minimum information cost of preparing either of two quantum states with one common device while preserving its memory. Measured by the Umegaki relative entropy between the two possible memory states, this minimum is the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy of the target states. If the memory may instead be consumed, the minimum is their Umegaki relative entropy. More generally, for any divergence satisfying data processing, memory preservation selects the maximal extension of its classical restriction. We also study the cost of requiring only finitely many outputs, with the costs increasing from Umegaki to Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy as the number of outputs grows. Finally, we consider hypothesis testing of an unknown device over independent runs. The optimal Stein exponent per run converges to the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy whenever the number of outputs per run diverges. This gives an operational characterization of the Belavkin-Staszewski relative entropy in quantum statistics.

authors.name: Pablo Costa Rico, Robert Salzmann, Mario Berta, \'Angela Capel

papers.title: Entropic quantum error correction for independent and correlated amplitude damping errors
papers.summary: The idea of using quantum entropy for quantum error correction (QEC) has existed for a long time. However, its computational complexity has limited its practical use: even a $[[4,1]]$ code for standard independent amplitude damping errors involves a $256\times 256$ Hermitian matrix, so the approach scales poorly as the codeword length increases. For correlated errors, the situation is even worse. In this paper, we show that, by using the insights developed in our previous paper and exploiting certain structures of quantum conditional mutual information, we can solve these problems exactly by hand, using only $2\times 2$ unitary matrices. By examining the entropy, we identify the leakage channels and the amount of leakage exactly, then define the recovery map accordingly. The rules defining our recovery map are simple, intuitive, and computationally inexpensive: for independent errors, it is based on 16 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions; for correlated errors, it is based on 6 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions. Our method sacrifices little in terms of performance: for the widely used entanglement fidelity, our simple QEC recovery map achieves a sharp result; for the worst-case fidelity, the best result is about $9\%$ better than ours; for correlated errors, there are no comparable results for short codewords. Among the known techniques, our recovery map is the first non-global one. The calculations use elementary linear algebra and calculus, and is presented in great detail.

authors.name: Gang Zhou

papers.title: Spin Interferometry Generated by Cavity Memory
papers.summary: We report the control and observation of coherent spin interferometry generated by cavity memory using an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers coupled to a microwave cavity. The abrupt switch-on and switch-off of a detuned drive produce transient fields at the cavity frequency that supply the two spin rotations for Ramsey interferometry, observed using both microwave and fluorescence readout. Spectrally scanning the spin profile across the cavity and drive frequencies distinguishes cavity-generated Ramsey interference from conventional Rabi dynamics. Temporal weighting of the reflected microwave signal enables spectrally selective population readout at a single probe frequency. By programming the phase and amplitude of the drive envelope, we extend the same mechanism to more quantum control sequences, including spin-echo and Rabi control.

authors.name: Siyu Li, Yifan Shi, Yicheng Xiao, Haotian Xu, Shixuan Zhang, Aoqin Liang, Yanxi Wu, Xiaokang Li, Guoqing Wang

papers.title: Maximally Entangled Mutually Unbiased Bases in Bipartite Systems of Unequal Prime Dimensions
papers.summary: Mutually unbiased bases with prescribed entanglement properties are of fundamental interest in quantum information theory. In the interesting case of a bipartite Hilbert space of unequal prime dimensions, $\mathcal{H}_p\otimes\mathcal{H}_q$, with $p<q$ prime, the standard solution provides $p+1$ product bases. For any such dimension $d=pq$ we construct $p+1$ bases, such that $p$ of them are represented by complex Hadamard matrices, each equivalent to a Fourier matrix $F_d$, with all vectors maximally entangled. Our explicit construction is based on eigenvectors of suitable Weyl--Heisenberg operators, the Chinese Remainder Theorem and quadratic Gaussian sums. The obtained result establishes a lower bound for the number of maximally entangled mutually unbiased bases, $M(p,q)\geq p$.

authors.name: Bogdan S. Damski, Karol \.Zyczkowski

papers.title: An Incomplete-Preference Quantum Anscombe--Aumann Representation
papers.summary: This work develops a generalised Anscombe--Aumann framework in which acts map a finite set of states of the world into the effect interval of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, while preferences need not be complete. The construction keeps three logically distinct questions separate. First, an incomplete-preference multi-utility theorem supplies affine utility functionals. Second, finite-dimensional operator geometry determines the form of each affine functional. Third, admissibility identifies which normalised probability--state pairs are compatible with the full preference. We introduce behavioural state-independence as the natural Anscombe--Aumann interpretation of the idea that the identity of the states of the world should not affect how quantum consequences are compared. Because an incomplete preference makes this aggregate behavioural condition weaker than a utility-by-utility condition, the factorisation theorem requires a stronger, explicitly operational representation-level condition. Under that condition and Loewner monotonicity, every affine utility functional is positively affinely equivalent to a normalised utility of the form $U_{p,\rho}(f)=\sum_{s}p(s)Tr(\rho f(s))$. Consequently, a suitable incomplete preference relation is represented by a family of admissible pairs in $\Delta(S) \times \mathcal{D} ( \mathcal{H} ) $. We then identify a canonical maximal compatible family and show that the scalar-effect subspace carries an ordinary classical multi-utility representation, with scalar events appearing as the vertices of the scalar-act cube.

authors.name: Cristhiano Duarte

papers.title: Fer expansion converges almost twice as far as Magnus for qubits
papers.summary: The Fer expansion writes the propagator of a time-dependent Hamiltonian as a product of unitary exponentials whose error decreases doubly exponentially with the number of factors, while the Magnus expansion improves by one order at a time. Its convergence, however, was guaranteed only below a radius of about $2.6058$, smaller than the Magnus radius $\pi$. We establish a guaranteed convergence threshold of about $6.2106$, or $1.98\,\pi$, for a qubit. This is almost twice the optimal universal Magnus threshold $\pi$; the bound on a single Fer step is sharp, while the exact convergence radius remains open.

authors.name: Lorenzo Bagnasacco, Vittorio Giovannetti

papers.title: Observing Enhanced Entanglement in an Ising Quantum Register Beyond Weak Measurement
papers.summary: Measurements often yield a disentangled quantum state which is the most probable measurement outcome while the measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement could be exponentially less probable or absent. Higher probability in measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement is virtue in experimental observation of enhance entanglement in post-selected or Born-rule measurements with less resources in noisy quantum devices. We develop a periodic measurement sampling(PMS) protocol in the framework of uniform matrix product states. Using PMS, we identify a peak enhancement of entanglement in a uniform post-measurement state whose probabilistic outcome can be maximized by optimizing a measurement super-cell. A measurement super-cell is the smallest repeating building block of qubits defined by the measurement density, external field strength and exchange interactions between quantum register and ancilla qubits. The above prediction based on a classical description of the many-body quantum state is demonstrated in a quantum computing experiment in a loop of quantum register qubits with Ising interactions in the presence of transverse magnetic field. Further, we show the scalability of predictions of the periodic measurement sampling protocol in the thermodynamic limit to finite size systems. Especially, we present a rescaling ansatz which would enable predicting the possibility of observing enhanced entanglement in finite size systems.

authors.name: K. G. S. H. Gunawardana

papers.title: Chip-Based Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution with Uncertainty-Principle-Based Composable Security
papers.summary: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution offers a promising platform for scalable quantum networks through its compatibility with standard telecommunications technology and photonic integration. High-order discrete modulation facilitates practical implementation while approaching the key-rate performance of ideal Gaussian modulation, but its finite-size composable security analysis entails substantial computational overhead. Here, we develop an uncertainty-principle-based security framework that enables finite-size composable key-rate evaluation against collective attacks for constellations up to 256-QAM. By introducing a heterodyne-measured ancillary mode into the entanglement-based source description, we incorporate additional source correlations into the security analysis that allow the Heisenberg uncertainty principle alone to provide a tight bound for the unknown correlations in a covariance matrix characterizing the whole system. Matrix symmetrization further reduces the key-rate optimization to a one-dimensional search, while subsequent mode reduction yields an analytical lower bound requiring no numerical search. Experimental demonstrations using 256-QAM on discrete-component and silicon-photonic-receiver platforms achieve finite-size composable secret key rates of 17.436 and 0.519 Mbps, respectively, over a 50 km fiber link. This approach facilitates the practical deployment of high-speed, real-time and compact quantum key distribution systems. Beyond quantum key distribution, the principle of tightening uncertainty-constrained bounds via source-mode expansion offers a paradigm for exploring the information-theoretic properties of complex non-Gaussian systems.

authors.name: Jiale Mi, Yiming Bian, Zhengyu Li, Xuesong Xu, Song Yu, Yichen Zhang, Hong Guo

papers.title: Formulating Uncomputation Beyond Classical Ancilla Use
papers.summary: Ancilla qubits are routinely used to simplify quantum circuit construction and reduce implementation costs, but their use introduces the burden of designing proper uncomputation afterward. To alleviate this, prior work has developed automated uncomputation synthesis based on a computational-basis formulation of ancilla use. However, this formulation is tailored to classically structured ancilla computations. For more general circuits, it may be undefined, yield unintended functionality, or fail to synthesize uncomputation. It therefore falls short of providing a precise and general formulation of uncomputation beyond classical ancilla use. To address these limitations, we propose a new formulation of ancilla use that specifies the operation of each gate through two complementary aspects: (1) the functionality it implements and (2) the transformation it induces on ancilla roles. Based on this specification, we define uncomputation as restoring the initial ancilla role while implementing the identity functionality. This perspective enables a simple Use-first strategy for automatically synthesizing uncomputation in cases both within and beyond the scope of prior approaches. We further develop a complete inference system for reasoning about specifications, together with a derivation-directed procedure for automatically synthesizing efficient uncomputation, enabling systematic uncomputation synthesis even in challenging cases beyond the scope of our automatic strategy.

authors.name: Bonan Su, Shengyuan Yang

papers.title: Quantum thermometry with k-local Hamiltonians
papers.summary: In equilibrium quantum thermometry, the precision of temperature estimation increases with the heat capacity of the probe thermometer. For an n-body thermometer, the maximum heat capacity is attained by a Hamiltonian that requires n-local interactions, making its physical implementation challenging. In the thermodynamic limit, the optimal heat capacity scales quadratically with n. Although more experimentally accessible 2-local Hamiltonians can achieve this optimal scaling, their performance remains significantly below the theoretical maximum for realistic system sizes. Here, we restrict to this scenario and show a substantial enhancement in the thermometric performance with only a minimal increase in locality in some Hamiltonian models. We further introduce k-local generalizations of these models and show that their thermometric performance systematically approaches the theoretical optimum as the locality is increased. By analyzing their spectra, we relate this enhancement to the progressive emergence of the spectral structure underlying optimal equilibrium thermometry. Lastly, we discuss the heat capacity as a witness of Hamiltonian locality.

authors.name: Jorge L\'opez Gonz\'alez, Mohammad Mehboudi, Anna Sanpera, Mar\'ia Garc\'ia D\'iaz

papers.title: Efficient Parameter Estimation through Quantum Extreme Learning
papers.summary: Quantum sensing protocols rely on the efficient processing of measurement outcomes to infer unknown physical parameters. Conventional optimal estimators, such as Bayesian inference and maximum likelihood estimation, require to construct a likelihood function whose efficient classical construction requires full knowledge of the dynamics, which may practically be infeasible. Model-free experimental construction of the likelihood is also very resource intensive. Here, we propose a quantum extreme learning-based framework for quantum parameter estimation which avoids the explicit construction of the likelihood function. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach using the transverse-field Ising model for estimating the external transverse field. Our results show that high estimation accuracy can be achieved using measurements at only a small number of training points. We further develop an interrogation-time optimization strategy that minimizes the estimation inaccuracy while keeping sampling fluctuations below a prescribed threshold. We further extend the framework to a two-time measurement protocol, in which measurement outcomes obtained at two distinct times are combined to enrich the feature space, thereby significantly enhancing the estimation accuracy. Our analysis shows that the estimation precision improves monotonically with the number of training points, while increasing the system size generally enhances the sensing performance, albeit non-monotonically. Finally, the protocol is shown to be robust against dephasing, making it suitable for near-term quantum devices.

authors.name: Dingwei Zhao, Srijon Ghosh, Victor Montenegro, Matteo G. A. Paris, Marco G. Genoni, Abolfazl Bayat

papers.title: Quantum computational spectroscopy of complex resonances and optical residues
papers.summary: Optical spectra of dissipative molecular systems depend on both complex resonance energies and the way each resonance couples to an optical probe. In a non-Hermitian description, these con- tributions are determined by complex residues involving left and right eigenvectors. We introduce a quantum protocol that reconstructs the resonance poles and their biorthogonal optical residues within a common spectral-filtering and measurement framework. A Hermitian dilation embeds the left and right eigenvectors into a zero-energy subspace. Gaussian-filtered correlators evaluated with unitary circuits, together with ratios of complex off-diagonal measurements, yield the residues with- out separate variational optimisation of the eigenstates. We demonstrate spectral reconstruction for dissipative plasmon-molecule models on IBM quantum hardware, resolving how probe-dependent modal contributions produce interference-induced doublets or accompany a separation of resonance energies. We also analyse the sensitivity of residue reconstruction near exceptional points. By mak- ing complex optical residues an explicit computational output, the protocol connects non-Hermitian eigenstructure to measurable optical response.

authors.name: Payman Mahmoudi, Jiate Luo, Chonghao Zhai, Qiang Shi, Alexander Yosifov, Jinzhao Sun

papers.title: Tessa: Encoding Classical Data Across an Entire Quantum Processor
papers.summary: We present Tessa, a hardware-aware, device-wide scheme to encode classical data on quantum computers. We use it to experimentally encode and decode up to $1568$ real values using IBM's Phoenix and Fez quantum computers on a variety of data. Tessa's construction is an extension of QPIXL and QCrank. However, it checkerboards address and data qubits across a coupling graph with neighbouring data qubits sharing only a subset of address qubits. When using the device's coupling graph no SWAP gates or routing is required, but the construction works for any bipartite coupling graph. The shots required for readout are determined by the local coupling degree. As examples, we have used cat states (pixel art of cats), various pixel art, audio, MIDI, DNA sequences and protein amino acid sequences.

authors.name: Daniel Bultrini

papers.title: Nesting in additive manufacturing using quantum annealing
papers.summary: Nesting in powder bed fusion (PBF), an additive manufacturing (AM) process, determines the positions and orientations of parts within the build space and influences build height and build time. As the number of parts and feasible placements increases, the nesting problem becomes computationally demanding. Exact approaches are limited to small problem sizes as computational effort increases rapidly with the problem size, while heuristic and metaheuristic approaches involve a trade-off between solution quality and computation time. Quantum annealing (QA) offers an alternative for solving combinatorial optimization problems, but its application to nesting in AM remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a QA-based approach for nesting in AM to investigate its feasibility and its scaling behavior across three problem sizes. An iterative binary quadratic model based approach (IBQM) is developed to minimize build height while considering the geometric characteristics of AM parts. Geometric abstraction, iterative decomposition, and variable pruning are applied to address the computational complexity of the nesting problem. The approach is evaluated using three cases with increasing problem sizes and compared to a classical approach combining tabu search and simulated annealing (TBSA). Compared with TBSA, IBQM reduces the build height of the original parts by up to 13.32% and the computation time by up to 74.27%.

authors.name: Xiangqian Wua, Jannik Gayer, Marcel Wagner, Jan C. Aurich

papers.title: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
papers.summary: We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, {these matrices} can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories. The learning error can be further reduced by correcting the memory effect induced by the Galerkin projection. We numerically demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in extrapolating the dynamics of various many-body systems, including Langevin and Glauber dynamics for classical systems as well as Lindblad dynamics for open quantum systems. In addition, for a class of single-site Glauber dynamics, we establish error bounds for sparse-plus-low-rank compression and uniform-in-time bounds for connected-cluster approximation and observable propagation with compressed transition moment matrices.

authors.name: Yuehaw Khoo, Bowen Li, Yuguan Wang, Siyao Yang

papers.title: Symmetry-Controlled Quantum State Transfer in Poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene: From Heisenberg to Hubbard Dynamics
papers.summary: We investigate quantum state transfer in the poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene lattice using isotropic Heisenberg and Hubbard models. For a 16-site lattice, reflection symmetry separates the single-excitation Hamiltonian into independent triplet and singlet sectors, allowing analytical determination of the energy spectra. Although perfect state transfer is forbidden for positive couplings, appropriately chosen coupling ratios enable pretty-good transfer with arbitrarily high fidelity. Remarkably, the triplet transfer probability is independent of the interchain rung coupling, while singlet transfer can be selectively enhanced or suppressed, enabling symmetry-selective quantum transport without time-dependent control. Extending the analysis to the Hubbard model, we show that the Heisenberg transfer dynamics emerge in the strong-interaction limit, while finite interactions delay all high-fidelity transfer peaks of a symmetry sector by the same fraction of their transfer time, set by the spectrum, and reduce the peak fidelity, even at the corrected time, by an amount that grows with the transfer time. These findings are relevant to future quantum-network architectures, where symmetry-controlled state transfer could provide a building block for connecting quantum memories and emitter-based interfaces within quantum nodes. Overall, our results demonstrate how molecular network geometry and symmetry can be exploited to engineer and control quantum-state transport in interacting spin systems, providing a theoretical framework for quantum information transfer in molecular-inspired quantum architectures.

authors.name: Adnan Jaljuli, Pablo Serra, Ammar Ali, Sabre Kais

papers.title: Dissipation as a Resource for Entanglement via High-Spin Mediator Purification
papers.summary: We study entanglement generation between two spin qubits mediated by a single, thermally mixed, high-spin ($S=5/2$) magnetic impurity, using the Lindblad master equation to compare coherent and dissipative control of the mediator. We show that no coherent drive, however strong or resonant, can purify the mediator beyond its thermal value --- a direct consequence of unitary evolution exactly preserving state purity --- while a dissipative channel purifies it up to the limit set by the optical pumping cycle itself, $\mathrm{Tr}[\rho_M^2]\approx0.8$. Modeling this channel with rates fixed by the measured optical pumping of a single Mn spin, we find that the entanglement it enables is not monotonic in the pump strength: it peaks at a finite rate and then decreases, since the same channel leaks decoherence to the qubits through the coupling that mediates their entanglement. At the experimental pumping rate, a single $80$ns pulse purifies the mediator, the resulting polarization persists for a timescale three orders of magnitude longer than the entangling dynamics, and the first-recurrence negativity rises from $0.18$ to $0.64$ at $12$K, remaining above $0.6$ up to $30$K. These results establish dissipation, not as noise to be suppressed, but as the very resource that makes robust entanglement generation possible.

authors.name: Ellen Martins Fernandes, Fabricio Macedo de Souza

papers.title: Red-Blue Hamiltonian Tomography via the Operator Lightcone Wavemap
papers.summary: We introduce a model-free method for Hamiltonian tomography based on the operator spreading wavefront. Given two tensor network simulations of the same quantum lattice (one with the nominal Hamiltonian and one with one or more perturbed bonds), the signed cross-entropy of the non-identity Pauli weight field $\mathcal{L}(v,t) = -\ln(n_{\rm pert}/n_{\rm base})$ identifies each perturbed bond by its causal signature: a red-blue sign flip at the two endpoints, visible from the first wavefront crossing. Combining measurements from $p$ strategically placed observation centers via an ensemble log-likelihood sum, a single broken bond is identified with an 82-fold margin over the next candidate on a $7\times7$ lattice. Extending to realistic coupling degradation ($\delta J = -0.20$) and up to 8 simultaneous faults, the integrated log-ratio $\Lambda(v) = \ln(\mathcal{B}(v)/\mathcal{N}(v))$ achieves a per-bond detection rate above 90\% in a single seismic pass using only 6 simulations. An iterative re-scan strategy progressively resolves multi-bond cases as the signal clears with each recalibration pass. The method requires no model assumptions and no knowledge of the perturbation type or magnitude; the detection is deliberately blind.

authors.name: Paolo D'Alberto

papers.title: Compiling Matrix Formulas to Quantum Block Encodings
papers.summary: Realizing the promise of quantum applications such as chemistry or fluid dynamics requires building quantum circuits that efficiently encode and manipulate exponentially large matrices. This process forces researchers to grapple with the reality that a matrix expressible as one equation on paper can map to thousands of bit-level quantum logic gates, historically written by hand. Even worse, it often ends with a discovery that the needed resources grow so quickly with matrix size that the quantum algorithm loses its asymptotic speedup. In this work, we present MARBLE, a language that automatically synthesizes an efficient circuit from the publication-style formula for the entries of a matrix. MARBLE algebraically rewrites programs into symbolic combinations of simpler matrices that have known circuit realizations. It analyzes costs of possible representations, notably the subnormalization term that dominates time complexity. It then emits an OpenQASM circuit and certifies whether its cost is poly-logarithmic in problem size, as required by quantum algorithms. When evaluated on quantum applications ranging from fluid dynamics to physical Hamiltonians, MARBLE matches or surpasses 37 of 39 published baselines. On the low end, it automatically matches many theoretically optimal circuits, and on the high end, it improves on a published construction in fluid dynamics by 10,487x in subnormalization. MARBLE produces exponentially smaller circuits than the leading tool FABLE, and it successfully compiles matrices whose dimensions exceed 2^100 within five seconds on a laptop.

authors.name: Daksh Shami, Charles Yuan

papers.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
papers.summary: We study the asymptotic behavior of the spherically averaged density $\widetilde \rho$ for fermionic bound states of the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ with nuclear charge $Z$. For the density associated with an eigenfunction satisfying $H_{N,Z}\psi=E\psi$, we show that if the energy $E$ is below the bottom of the essential spectrum $\Sigma:=\inf\mathop{\rm ess.spec} (H_{N,Z})$, then \[ \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln \widetilde \rho(r)}{r} =\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{d}{dr}{\ln \widetilde\rho(r)} =-2\alpha_0, \] with $\alpha_0=\sup\{\alpha \ge 0\colon e^{2\alpha r}\widetilde \rho \in L^1(\mathbb{R_+},r^2dr)\}$. The same is true at threshold in certain cases. Moreover, we prove $\alpha_0^2=\Sigma-E$ for the ground states of $H_{3,Z}$ with sufficiently large $Z$.

authors.name: Yukimi Goto

papers.title: The Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment: classical and quantum optimization approaches
papers.summary: Efficient railway rolling stock management requires the coordinated planning of train-unit assignment, shunting movements, track occupation, service operations, and workforce allocation. These interdependent decisions give rise to a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly as the size of the fleet and the planning horizon increase. This paper introduces the Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment, a mixed-integer linear programming formulation that integrates these operational decisions within a unified optimization framework. To improve computational tractability, a preprocessing procedure is developed to reduce the size of the resulting model. The proposed approach is evaluated through computational experiments on instances of increasing size and under different objective-function weight and cost configurations. Classical optimization experiments using Gurobi show that filtering method reduces the number of decision variables and constraints, while its impact on computational time varies across instances. In addition, a constrained quadratic model representation is investigated using D-Wave's hybrid quantum-classical optimization solver.

authors.name: Alessia Ciacco, Francesca Guerriero, Eneko Osaba

papers.title: Transfer-Matrix Calculus for Infinite Matrix Product States
papers.summary: Long-range interactions, from the Coulomb repulsion between electrons to the power-law interactions of trapped ions and Rydberg atoms, are widespread in quantum many-body physics. For infinite systems, however, MPS algorithms, the standard classical reference in one dimension, conventionally rely on a computational compromise: replacing these interactions by fitted sums of exponentials. We develop transfer-matrix calculus (TMC), a unified framework for deriving infinite-MPS algorithms. In TMC, an interaction is written as a function of the transfer matrix, and one set of contraction rules then yields the effective Hamiltonians of DMRG and VUMPS, the tangent-space excitation action, and the energy variance, without an MPO. Long-range interactions thus enter with their prescribed distance dependence. For the half-filled lattice Coulomb chain with a $1/d$ interaction of strength $V$, theory predicts CDW order for all $V>0$, but at weak coupling this order is too weak for earlier numerics to resolve. Using TMC, we obtain infinite-MPS ground states at $V=2$ directly in the thermodynamic limit, with an energy variance per site of $2\times10^{-10}$. Our data, extrapolated to zero energy variance, indicate a small nonzero CDW amplitude, $m_0=0.002213(14)$, consistent with this prediction. The complete $V=2$ optimization workflow across the full series of bond dimensions takes less than a day on a single AMD MI250X GPU die. For an exactly solvable long-range hopping model, TMC reproduces the nonanalytic $|k|$ cusp of the one-particle dispersion that any fixed finite sum of decaying exponentials rounds off. We also use TMC to optimize first-quantized MPS directly in the thermodynamic limit. For half-filled free fermions, our entanglement entropy data show scaling consistent with central charge $c=1$ over the studied bond dimensions, as for second-quantized MPS.

authors.name: Qi Yang, Philippe Corboz

papers.title: Entanglement and information dynamics in charged dual-unitary circuits with impurities
papers.summary: Local parts of a closed, non-equilibrium quantum many-body system can reach stationarity through the buildup of entanglement between different regions. In this paper we investigate how this process is affected by the presence of a quantum impurity that breaks a global symmetry of the bulk. In particular, we study a charged dual-unitary quantum circuit perturbed by a symmetry-breaking, non-dual-unitary gate acting on a spatially fixed pair of sites. In this setup we calculate the entanglement entropy for a subsystem that does not contain the impurity, as well as the mutual information and logarithmic negativity for a bipartite subsystem that straddles the impurity. We obtain exact results in the early time regime for these quantities from the dual unitarity of the bulk system. Beyond this regime, we compute the predictions of the quasiparticle and entanglement membrane pictures, supporting them with exact calculations obtained by taking the corresponding limits of the bulk entangling power. We find that the presence of a symmetry-breaking impurity can lead to a richer behaviour of quantum relaxation, including non-monotonic evolution of the entanglement entropy, a modification of the long-time steady state, and persistent subsystem mutual information and entanglement negativity. This behaviour is understood in terms of long-range correlations generated by scattering from the impurity, and facilitated by the ballistic propagation of the conserved charges.

authors.name: Shachar Fraenkel, Colin Rylands

papers.title: Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
papers.summary: Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes. It combines algorithmic optimization through local predecoding, architecture-aware optimization, and pipeline-wide parallelism to reduce matching workload and execution overhead while preserving MWPM optimality. Across rotated surface codes with distances 9-33 and circuit-level physical error rates of 0.05%-0.3%, on a single CPU core, Beyond Blossom achieves a 4.23$\times$ geometric-mean speedup and up to 5.58$\times$ speedup over Sparse Blossom in PyMatching. At distance 33 and a physical error rate of 0.1%, with 8 CPU cores, decoding a block of 33 measurement rounds takes 21.40 $\mu$s on average, equivalent to 0.65 $\mu$s per round.

authors.name: Jiayu Fu, Zirong Shen, Lin Gan, Yiming Zhang, Wenjing Han, Xiaoming Sun, Riling Li, Guangwen Yang

papers.title: Unitary realization of wavefunction collapse
papers.summary: Recent quantum reconstruction projects demand pure unitary time evolution which seems to contradict the collapse postulate. Inspired by Zurek's environment assisted invariance idea, a natural unitary realization of wavefunction collapse is proposed using Grothendieck group construction for the tensor product commutative monoid.

authors.name: Florin Moldoveanu

papers.title: Quantum Channel Testing in Average-Case Distance
papers.summary: We study the complexity of testing properties of quantum channels. First, we show that testing identity to any channel $\mathcal N: \mathbb C^{d_{\mathrm{in}} \times d_{\mathrm{in}}} \to \mathbb C^{d_{\mathrm{out}} \times d_{\mathrm{out}}}$ in diamond norm distance requires $\Omega(\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{in}}} / \varepsilon)$ queries, even in the strongest algorithmic model that admits ancillae, coherence, and adaptivity. This is due to the worst-case nature of the distance induced by the diamond norm. Motivated by this limitation and other theoretical and practical applications, we introduce an average-case analogue of the diamond norm, which we call the average-case imitation diamond (ACID) norm. In the weakest algorithmic model without ancillae, coherence, or adaptivity, we prove that testing identity to certain types of channels in ACID distance can be done with complexity independent of the dimensions of the channel, while for other types of channels the complexity depends on both the input and output dimensions. Building on previous work, we also show that identity to any fixed channel can be tested with $\tilde O(d_{\mathrm{in}} d_{\mathrm{out}}^{3/2} / \varepsilon^2)$ queries in ACID distance and $\tilde O(d_{\mathrm{in}}^2 d_{\mathrm{out}}^{3/2} / \varepsilon^2)$ queries in diamond distance in this model. Finally, we prove tight bounds on the complexity of channel tomography in ACID distance.

authors.name: Gregory Rosenthal, Hugo Aaronson, Sathyawageeswar Subramanian, Animesh Datta, Tom Gur

papers.title: Genuine multipartite entanglement as a probe of many-body localization in disordered spin chains with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions
papers.summary: We study the genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) in a disordered system and its potential for detecting the transition from the thermalized to the localized phase. We demonstrate that the quenched average GME can approach its near-maximum value in the ergodic phase of a disordered quantum spin model. In contrast, GME vanishes in the many-body localized (MBL) phase, both in equilibrium and in the long-time dynamical regime, indicating lack of multipartite entanglement in the localized regime. To establish this, we analyze the disordered Heisenberg spin chain subjected to a random magnetic field along with the two- and three-body Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions. We exhibit that the behavior of GME, in both the mid-spectrum of the Hamiltonian and the dynamically evolved states from an initial Neel configuration, serves as a reliable indicator of the critical disorder strength required for the ergodic to MBL transition. The identified transition point aligns well with standard indicators such as the gap ratio and the correlation length. Moreover, we find that the presence of DM interactions, particularly the three-body interaction, significantly enlarges the thermal phase and delays the onset of localization with an extended correlation length. This shift in the transition point is consistently reflected in both static and dynamical analyses, reinforcing GME as a robust probe for MBL transitions.

authors.name: Triyas Sapui, Keshav Das Agarwal, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Leela Ganesh Chandra Lakkaraju, Aditi Sen De

papers.title: No-go theorem for maximally $\psi-$epistemic models using two pure states of a qubit
papers.summary: This work addresses the fundamental question concerning the nature of quantum states, specifically to what extent they represent an agent's knowledge about the system, that is, is \textit{epistemic} in nature. We show that, despite the existence of the Kochen-Specker model, which is a maximally $\psi-$epistemic model for single-qubit systems when projective measurements are employed, \textit{no} maximally $\psi-$epistemic model can reproduce statistics arising out of non-projective measurements on a pair of single-qubit states. This has been done in an experimentally robust way using only two pure single-qubit states and their equal mixture, by constructing a two-input, three-output game called \textit{Risk Aware Distinguishability} (RAD) and generalizing the notion of epistemic and quantum overlaps using RAD. Furthermore, we maximize the difference of generalized overlaps instead of minimizing their ratio, and in the process point out why that is a stricter criterion for refuting $\psi-$epistemic models.

authors.name: Sagnik Ray, Anubhav Chaturvedi, Debashis Saha

papers.title: Dynamical error reshaping for dual-rail erasure qubits
papers.summary: Erasure qubits -- qubits designed to have an error profile that is dominated by detectable leakage errors -- are a promising way to cut down the resources needed for quantum error correction. There have been several recent experiments demonstrating erasure qubits in superconducting quantum processors, most notably the dual-rail qubit defined by the one-photon subspace of two coupled cavities. An outstanding challenge is that the ancillary transmons needed to facilitate erasure checks and two-qubit gates introduce a substantial amount of noise, limiting the benefits of working with erasure-biased qubits. Here, we show how to suppress the adverse effects of transmon-induced noise while performing erasure checks or two-qubit gates. We present control schemes for these operations that suppress erasure check errors by three orders of magnitude and reduce the logical two-qubit gate infidelities by up to three orders of magnitude.

authors.name: Filippos Dakis, Shruti Puri, Sophia E. Economou, Edwin Barnes

papers.title: The Quantum Agreement Theorem
papers.summary: Intersubjective consistency asks when different observers of a physical system, reasoning from a shared theory, will agree on their probability assessments. Classical probability theory provides a benchmark in the form of the Agreement Theorem (Aumann, 1976). We study the quantum mechanics (QM) analog to the classical Agreement Theorem in a finite-dimensional tripartite setting in which two observers obtain information via local projective measurements. We represent their mutual awareness by common certainty, which is formally an infinite hierarchy of certainty operators concerning the probability of an event of interest. We first prove that if the observers' measurements commute with one another and with the property of interest, common certainty forces their probability assessments to coincide, thereby recovering a QM analog to the classical Agreement Theorem. We then construct a one-parameter family of qutrit-qubit-qubit models in which one observer's measurement does not commute with the property and common certainty of disagreement occurs -- a distinctively QM phenomenon. The mechanism is coherence between branches distinguished by one but not the other observer's measurement. When measurement outcomes are stored in a classical register, the resulting dephasing removes this coherence and restores agreement. Finally, we prove that QM does not permit the extreme 0-1 configuration in which Alice is certain of a property and is also certain that Bob is certain of its negation. These results aim to turn debate in QM about observer-dependent facts into precise mathematical conditions for when intersubjective agreement or disagreement in QM can be sustained.

authors.name: Mar\'ia Garc\'ia D\'iaz, Adam Brandenburger, Giannicola Scarpa

papers.title: On the Dynamics of Local Hidden-Variable Models
papers.summary: Bell nonlocality is an intriguing property of quantum mechanics with far-reaching consequences for information processing, philosophy, and our fundamental understanding of nature. However, standard Bell nonlocality is a statement about correlations at a fixed point in time only. It does not take into account dynamics, i.e., time evolution of those correlations. Consider a dynamic situation where the correlations remain local for all times. Then, at each moment in time, there exists a local hidden-variable (LHV) model reproducing the momentary correlations. Can the time evolution of the correlations then be captured by evolving the hidden variables? We make this question precise by defining dynamical LHV models and motivating additional physical attributes such as locality and continuity of the dynamics. We then establish a series of complementary go and no-go theorems that together map out which combinations of these properties LHV dynamics can and cannot have. In particular, noninteracting quantum dynamics can be represented on the hidden-variable level in a local way, but LHV dynamics can fail to exist for interacting systems: Even though the observed correlations are local at all times, their time evolution may nevertheless be incompatible with local hidden-variable dynamics.

authors.name: Nick von Selzam, Florian Marquardt

papers.title: Synthesis of Fault-tolerant State Preparation Circuits using Steane-type Error Detection
papers.summary: Fault-tolerant state preparation is essential for reliable quantum error correction, particularly in Steane-type error correction, which relies on robust ancilla states for syndrome readout. One method of fault-tolerant state preparation is to initialize multiple ancilla states and check them against each other to detect problematic errors. In the worst case, the number of states required for successful initialization grows polynomially with the code distance, but it has been shown that this can be reduced to constant ancilla overhead-in the best case, only four states are required. However, existing techniques for finding low-overhead initialization schemes are limited to codes with large symmetry groups, such as the Golay code. In this work, we propose a general, automated synthesis methodology for Steane-type fault-tolerant state preparation circuits that applies to arbitrary Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes and does not rely on code symmetries. We apply the proposed methods to various CSS codes up to a distance of seven and simulate the successful fault-tolerant initialization of logical basis states under circuit-level depolarizing noise. The circuits synthesized using the proposed methodology provide an important step towards experimental realizations of high-fidelity ancilla states for near-term demonstration of fault-tolerant quantum computation.

authors.name: Erik Weilandt, Tom Peham, Robert Wille

papers.title: Prodiabatic Elimination: Higher Order Elimination of Fast Variables with Quantum Noise
papers.summary: Adiabatic elimination plays a central role in cavity quantum electrodynamics by removing fast cavity degrees of freedom, but at the cost of losing their finite-time response in multi-time correlations. We introduce prodiabatic elimination, a systematic expansion of the quantum Langevin equations that retains vacuum-noise contributions alongside higher-order corrections to the eliminated cavity field. This provides controlled access to arbitrary time- and normally ordered multi-time correlation functions, including photodetection observables, beyond what can be recovered from effective atomic dynamics alone. In the driven-dissipative Jaynes-Cummings model, we identify a vacuum-mediated effective repulsion between detected photons that suppresses short-delay bunching. For a single-photon switch, we analytically resolve a finite heralded response time arising from the cavity field's delayed adjustment to the atomic transfer.

authors.name: Jan Neuser, Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, Patrick P. Potts

papers.title: Digital dissipative state preparation for frustration-free gapless quantum systems
papers.summary: Preparing algebraically correlated ground states of quantum many-body systems is an important, yet challenging task for quantum simulation. We introduce a protocol that employs local projective measurements and unitary feedback for frustration-free gapless systems. Our approach prepares a priori unknown ground states in time that scales polynomially with system size. We analytically show the performance of our protocol for the dynamics of a single particle; we argue the same mechanism generalizes to many-body systems based on the physics of quasiparticles. Our theory predicts that the transient cooling dynamics directly reveals the system's universal critical properties. In particular, the state preparation time is linear in the inverse of the finite-size gap (up to log correction) when the system's dynamical critical exponent is larger than or equal to the effective spatial dimension explored by the quasiparticles. We verify these predictions in numerical simulations of ferromagnetic Heisenberg models in one- and two dimensions, a Fredkin spin chain, and a two-dimensional model of resonating valence bond states. Our protocol stabilizes gapless many-body ground states fully digitally without requiring analog rotations, enabling access to high-fidelity states beyond conventional adiabatic approaches in near-term experiments.

authors.name: Johannes Feldmeier, Yu-Jie Liu, Mikhail D. Lukin, Soonwon Choi

papers.title: Thermalization Across Scales on a Digital Quantum Processor
papers.summary: Thermalization of isolated quantum many-body systems normally unfolds via dynamical spreading of entanglement across progressively increasing spatial scales. The speed of this dynamical process, however, can be affected by the presence of local disorder. Here we study the crossover between slow and fast thermalization in a disordered two-dimensional Heisenberg Floquet model using digital quantum simulations with up to 100 superconducting qubits. Our experiment measures subsystem purities and $Z$-basis marginal collision entropies for patches of up to $3\times 3$ qubits. We resolve the onset of thermalization across scales by tracking each quantity's approach to its asymptotic value. In regimes where the system is moderately entangled, we validate our calibrated quantum simulations against state-of-the-art classical simulations. Near the crossover to fast thermalization, the classical methods no longer reliably converge due to volume-law growth of entanglement. By exploring this computationally hard regime, our work establishes a frontier of applications for digital quantum computers in probing complex many-body thermalization.

authors.name: Faisal Alam, Marcos Crichigno, Elizabeth Crosson, Steven T. Flammia, Filippo Maria Gambetta, Max Hunter Gordon, Michael Kreshchuk, Ashley Montanaro, Alberto Nocera, Raul A. Santos

papers.title: Implementation of non-local arbitrary two-qubit controlled gates via geometric quantum computation with Rydberg anti-blockade
papers.summary: In the context of Rydberg anti-blockade, this paper proposes a new scheme for a high-fidelity controlled-unitary gate based on non-adiabatic holonomic quantum computation. Under specific detuning and interaction conditions, the scheme achieves a suitable evolution path for non-adiabatic holonomic quantum computation through reverse engineering of pulse parameters. This scheme can implement arbitrary two-qubit controlled gates with favorable robustness. We also evaluate the effects of spontaneous emission and laser intensity errors on the fidelity; numerical simulations show that the geometric gate scheme still exhibits excellent performance under these errors. Furthermore, we extend the local gates to non-local operations by combining entanglement transfer with auxiliary-atom measurements and classical feedforward, and demonstrate their application to interconversion among four-qubit entangled states (GHZ, cluster, and W states). This finding indicates the potential applicability of our scheme to complex quantum information processing tasks.

authors.name: Le-Jiang Yu, Jia Zheng, Kun Pu, Chao Gao

papers.title: Scalable topological quantum computing based on Sine-Cosine chain models
papers.summary: We propose a scalable framework for quantum information processing based on Matryoshka-type sine-cosine chains, a hierarchy of one-dimensional chiral-symmetric lattices obtained by repeated ($P$ times) square-root construction starting from the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain. A chain of order $P$ can host $2^{P+2}-2$ protected edge states, so a single physical device can encode a qudit of equivalent dimension (or, equivalently, several independent qubits) instead of one qubit per device. We show that (i) the adiabatic defect-transfer step underlying SSH-based topological gates carries over unchanged to the Matryoshka chain, transferring the full set of defect states simultaneously; (ii) a Y-junction braiding protocol then composes single-qudit gate operations in all energy sectors at once, increasing the operation density per physical device; and (iii) the same edge states provide a quantum memory whose capacity scales exponentially with the chain order at fixed physical length. Numerical fidelity analysis under on-site, hopping, and correlated angle disorder shows partial, chiral-symmetry-protected robustness.

authors.name: A. Lykholat, G. F. Moreira, I. R. Martins, D. Sousa, A. M. Marques, R. G. Dias

papers.title: Quantum simulation of a nonuniform Dicke model in a two-dimensional trapped-ion crystal
papers.summary: Existing experimental realizations of the Dicke model in atomic or ionic systems are based on global observables assuming uniform spin-boson coupling, while inevitable experimental nonuniformity on the one hand requires site-resolved measurement of spin states, and on the other hand provides potential quantum advantage in simulating multi-spin distributions. Here we report the quantum simulation of a nonuniform Dicke-like model, due to either the inevitable experimental imperfection or the engineered spin-phonon coupling pattern, in a two-dimensional (2D) crystal of up to 200 ions. We explicitly demonstrate the sensitivity of few-spin observables and multi-spin distributions to the spatial inhomogeneity of the model, and examine the relaxation dynamics of the nonuniform model by measuring the subsystem entropies of selected ion groups. Our work enables the study of Dicke-like models beyond the symmetric subspace, paving the way toward understanding the role of nonuniformity in its thermalization and quantum chaos behavior.

authors.name: S. -A. Guo, J. Ye, J. -Y. Tan, Z. -W. Zhang, L. Zhang, Y. -Y. Chen, Y. -L. Xu, C. Zhang, Y. Jiang, B. -X. Qi, L. He, Z. -C. Zhou, Y. -K. Wu, L. -M. Duan

papers.title: Distinguishability of locally diagonal orthogonally invariant quantum states
papers.summary: We study the distinguishability of quantum states under local operations with classical communication (LOCC), separable, and positive-partial-transpose (PPT) measurements, focusing on locally diagonal orthogonally invariant (LDOI) states -- those invariant under local diagonal orthogonal twirling. This class includes many important families such as Werner states, isotropic states, X-states, and Dicke states. We show that optimal PPT and separable measurements for distinguishing LDOI states can always be taken to be LDOI, and the LOCC supremum can be approached by LDOI LOCC POVMs, enabling a dimensional reduction from $n^4$ to $O(n^2)$ in the associated optimization problems. We establish efficiently computable bounds on the distinguishability of orthonormal LDOI bases and prove that for a broad class of such bases -- including all two-qubit cases -- the LOCC supremum equals the PPT and separable optima. More generally, we show the gap between PPT and LOCC distinguishability is at most $(n-2)/(2n^2)$ for local dimension $n$.

authors.name: Nathaniel Johnston, Vincent Russo

papers.title: Lagrange: Operating Italy's First Publicly-Accessible Quantum Computer for Research and Education
papers.summary: We describe the design, implementation, and nine-month operational experience of the software management stack for Lagrange, an IQM Spark five-qubit superconducting quantum computer jointly acquired by LINKS Foundation, Politecnico di Torino and the Italian National Institute of Metrological Research (INRiM), and managed by LINKS. Lagrange is, to our knowledge, the first quantum computer in Italy that is fully operational and accessible to students and researchers from multiple institutions under formal service agreements, and to the general public under commercial agreements. When installed in mid-2025, the IQM Spark hardware was delivered by the vendor with authentication only: no billing, project management or fair usage enforcement were provided. We developed a modular middleware layer that filled that gap without modifying any vendor client software, by intercepting API calls through a proxy that enforces project-based budgets, reservation-aware authorisation, and per-user fairness policies. The middleware adopts a plugin architecture that cleanly separates vendor-specific logic from site-specific policies, enabling reuse across different quantum hardware backends and deployment contexts. Since entering production in September 2025, the system has processed over 240,000 quantum jobs totalling more than 1 week of QPU execution time, with greater than 98% uptime. Notably, students at Politecnico di Torino regularly use the machine during both lectures and formal examinations -- a practice we believe to be unique in Europe. We report on the system architecture, the operational lessons learned, and the infrastructure choices that made this deployment possible.

authors.name: Paolo Viviani, Fabrizio Bertone, Giacomo Vitali, Emanuele Dri, Federico Stirano, Giuseppe Caragnano, Francesco Lubrano, Marco Cipollini, Martina Giovalli, Chiara Vercellino, Alberto Scionti, Virginia Ajani, Antonino Nespola, Olivier Terzo, Matteo Cocuzza, Bartolomeo Montrucchio, Giovanna Turvani, Gianluca Bertaina, Marco Coisson, Davide Calonico, Fabrizio Pirri, Pietro Asinari

papers.title: Quantum limits on squeezing
papers.summary: In our work, we show how, for a network of bosonic modes, canonical commutation relations constrain the coefficients relating input and internal modes. Based on these constraints, we derive a lower bound on the total steady-state squeezing achievable in reservoir-engineered (dissipative) squeezing schemes, quantified by the sum of mode-optimal quadrature variances each normalized to its corresponding input variance. The bound on this normalized sum follows solely from canonical commutation relations and stability, and is saturated in the strong-coupling limit at unity. Furthermore, we show that adding independent parametric driving terms for each mode changes the quantum noise--gain balance and yields, for the same normalized mode-optimal sum, a distinct optimum bound, approaching 1/2. In addition, we show how these constraints allow us to reformulate the Duan inseparability criterion for a three-mode bosonic system in terms of a single parameter-dependent figure of merit. Our results apply directly to current electromechanical and nanomechanical experiments and indicate that the two-mode bounds can be experimentally approached even at room temperature.

authors.name: Francesco Massel

papers.title: Efficient ensemble randomization by tuning chaos in a nonlinear spin-1 system
papers.summary: We present an efficient scheme to randomize a spin-state ensemble in a nonlinear spin-1 system by tuning chaos with an external periodic drive. Without modulation, the system exhibits a mixed phase space featuring regular islands embedded in a chaotic sea, where global mixing is inhibited by energy conservation. Using numerical simulations, we demonstrate that modulation of a linear Zeeman field not only facilitates transport between different energy shells but also drives ensembles toward a Haar-random distribution over spin states. Under optimized conditions, complete randomization at the level of the second moment is achieved on a timescale set by the inverse nonlinear interaction energy. In the overdriven regime, randomization is unexpectedly suppressed at specific modulation amplitudes, accompanied by the formation of sticky regions in phase space. We attribute this behavior to the dynamical cancellation of the leading low-order harmonic component of the periodic drive. These results illustrate how time-periodic driving can be used to engineer chaotic systems and achieve controllable randomization in nonlinear spin systems.

authors.name: Jongmin Kim, Minsung Jeong, Jongyoon Han, Y. Shin

papers.title: Universal photon blockade via two-photon light-matter interaction at chiral exceptional points
papers.summary: The photon blockade (PB) effect is a hallmark non-classical phenomenon in quantum optics and finds important applications for building quantum sources, while the control of PB by the non-Hermitian exceptional points remains largely unexplored. In this work, we theoretically investigate universal photon blockade in a microcavity harboring chiral exceptional points (CEPs) for building multiplexing quantum sources with nonreciprocal photon statistics. The results reveal that the presence of the CEPs leads to a stark contrast in the photon statistics of two whispering-gallery modes with opposite propagating directions. That is, one mode exhibits a strong PB effect while the other displays either sub-Poissonian or super-Poissonian distribution. Our findings thus may pave the way for advanced applications of photon blockade, and provide a theoretical foundation for the selective generation of single-photon and two-photon emission

authors.name: Hai-Tao Dong, Meng-Long Song, Si-Yu Zhang, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, Dong Wang

papers.title: A Quantum-Classical Surrogate Model for the Collision Operator of the Lattice Boltzmann Method
papers.summary: We introduce a hybrid approach utilising a quantum machine learning surrogate model to approximate the non-linear collision dynamics of the LBM. It offloads the non-unitary operations that challenge pure quantum solvers. The surrogate's expressivity relies on variational quantum circuits that implement partial Fourier series, while data re-uploading extends the representable frequency spectrum. Unlike previous approaches that use a fixed relaxation parameter, the relaxation step is embedded analytically in the circuit, allowing the learned equilibrium to be used for any relaxation parameter without retraining. We reassess standard VQC metrics, including expressibility, entanglement, and effective dimension, by relating them directly to task-specific surrogate performance and identifying the architectural parameters that determine approximation accuracy. The proposed surrogate is validated against the classical BGK collision operator using benchmark problems, including the Taylor-Green vortex for energy dissipation and the double shear layer for shear-driven instabilities and nonlinear flow evolution. Our results show that the surrogate closely reproduces the BGK reference on both benchmarks, using a single set of trained circuits across all relaxation parameters. These findings suggest that hybrid quantum-classical strategies offer a practical path toward realising the potential of quantum computing in fluid engineering.

authors.name: Lukas C. Birk, David M. Wawrzyniak, Josef M. Winter, Steffen J. Schmidt, Thomas Indinger, Christian F. Jan{\ss}en, Nikolaus A. Adams

papers.title: Susceptibility-kinetic uncertainty relations for quantum systems
papers.summary: Kinetic uncertainty relations bound current precision of stochastic processes by dynamical activity. The extension of these bounds to quantum systems has been impeded by coherence, strong system-reservoir coupling, and the subtlety of defining dynamical activity in the quantum regime. Here, we introduce a partial dynamical activity through the quantum Fisher information associated with the rescaling of the system-reservoir coupling and show that it bounds current precision via a universal susceptibility-kinetic uncertainty relation. The general validity of this relation is guaranteed by the natural contribution of a susceptibility term, which is experimentally accessible by tuning the system-reservoir coupling strength. We show how the partial dynamical activity encompasses previous definitions of activity in the weak-coupling Markovian limit and that it provides an information-geometric interpretation of correlator-based activities. We illustrate the tight constraint on precision that our bound provides with the example of the dynamics of a strongly interacting finite-size system and of steady-state coherent transport through a double quantum dot, where quantum effects invalidate previously developed kinetic uncertainty relations. We expect our bound to provide a powerful tool for optimizing precision in arbitrary quantum systems.

authors.name: Didrik Palmqvist, Janine Splettstoesser, Ludovico Tesser

papers.title: Revisiting the invariant ring of two-qubit mixed states
papers.summary: Local unitary (LU) equivalence classifies quantum states up to changes of local bases and preserves their entanglement properties. Polynomial LU invariants provide an algebraic approach to determining whether two quantum states are LU equivalent. We revisit the ring of complex polynomial LU invariants on the full two-qubit operator space, equivalently the invariant ring under the local conjugation action of $GL(2,\mathbb C)\times GL(2,\mathbb C)$. For the two-qubit system, King \emph{et al.} previously determined a generating set of 21 invariants and the Cohen--Macaulay structure of this ring. Using a unified notation, we provide a self-contained derivation of the known Molien series and a systematic graphical reconstruction of the known generators. The Molien series is derived by explicit contour integration over the maximal torus, supplying computational steps not given in the earlier treatment. We systematically reconstruct the known generators using the graphical tensor method and provide explicit algebraic reductions of the candidate invariants. This work clarifies the calculations and graphical construction underlying the established results.

authors.name: Bing Xie, Lin Zhang

papers.title: Qudit-ADAPT-VQE: an adaptive variational algorithm with counterdiabatic-inspired improvements for qudits
papers.summary: Variational quantum algorithms based on qudits have attracted significant attention in recent years due to their potential for more efficient quantum information encoding and processing. However, as in their qubit-based counterparts, challenges such as barren plateaus and the design of efficient ansatzes remain major obstacles. In this work, we propose to address these issues through a qudit implementation of the ADAPT-VQE algorithm, which constructs the ansatz iteratively. Specifically, we introduce an operator pool inspired by adiabatic evolution enhanced with counterdiabatic driving for ansatz construction and employ it to solve the Max 3-Cut and Multiway Number Partitioning problems. We show that the warm-start strategy inherent to ADAPT-VQE, together with an ansatz construction based on counterdiabatic operators, achieves higher accuracy than fixed-ansatz approaches and, at equal number of variational parameters, requires fewer native gates. Furthermore, we show that, in qudit-based quantum computing, ADAPT-VQE with a counterdiabatic operator pool can navigate rough optimization landscapes with local traps through the burrowing mechanism, suggesting robustness against local minima and providing a flexible framework for variational quantum algorithms with qudits.

authors.name: Joaqu\'in Molina, Herbert D\'iaz-Moraga, Dardo Goyeneche, Diego Tancara

papers.title: Approximate majorization and high-order capacity of quantum depolarizing channels
papers.summary: A central challenge in quantum information theory is to determine whether entanglement provides an advantage for information processing when coherent operations across multiple channel uses are allowed. For depolarizing channels, King's proof of the additivity of the minimum output entropy rules out such an advantage for classical communication at leading asymptotic order, while leaving open the possibility of an advantage for higher orders. In this work, we conjecture a majorization relation for the outputs of depolarizing channels and prove an approximate version of this conjecture. Our proof combines an exact ordering of shifted log-determinants with an anti-concentration bound for the spectrum of the product-state output, refining King's analysis based on Schatten norms. An additional logarithmic second-moment estimate controls arbitrary channel outputs. As a direct application, we obtain a tight third-order expansion for the classical capacity of quantum depolarizing channels. Consequently, entangled codewords and collective decoding can improve the logarithm of the message size over the product-coding strategy by at most $O(1)$ bits, sharpening our understanding of the role of entanglement in the finite-blocklength regime.

authors.name: Zhiwei Song, Xin Wang, Marco Tomamichel, Kun Fang

papers.title: A commuting operator self-test for exact entanglement embezzlement
papers.summary: We show that the optimal commuting operator correlation for a variant of Coladangelo's two-player generalized nonlocal game, based on the embezzlement of entanglement, is a commuting operator self-test. Our result gives the first correlation self-test for an exact entanglement embezzlement protocol in the commuting operator framework. Because the unique optimal correlation necessitates the exact embezzlement of entanglement, the correlation is unrealizable using quantum tensor-product models, even if the local spaces are allowed to be infinite dimensional. Our proof relies on Harris' unique abstract state characterization of exact embezzlement of entanglement involving Cuntz algebras.

authors.name: Connor Paddock, Simon Schmidt

papers.title: Fer expansion of driven spins: closed-form recursion and no-go theorems for termination
papers.summary: The Fer expansion factorizes the propagator of a driven quantum system into exponentials of time-integrated effective Hamiltonians, which govern the evolution left over by the previous factors. Every truncation is unitary, and adding a factor squares the size of the remainder, but each effective Hamiltonian is an infinite series of nested commutators of the previous one. For $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, in every representation, from qubits to spins of any dimension, we represent the effective Hamiltonians by time-dependent vectors in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and resum this series exactly. The result is a closed map from one vector to the next, in which the infinite series reduces to the previous vector crossed once and twice with its time integral, weighted by elementary functions. Using this map, we address the question of when the expansion can be stopped after finitely many factors. This is possible whenever the leftover evolution is known in closed form, for instance when the effective Hamiltonian commutes with itself at all times or precesses about a fixed axis with constant angular velocity. We prove that, for real-analytic drives, neither happens beyond the first factor unless the first exponential is already exact. Stopping the expansion therefore yields no new exactly solvable drives.

authors.name: Lorenzo Bagnasacco, Daniel Burgarth, Vittorio Giovannetti, Kazuya Yuasa

papers.title: Elementary proofs of quantum lower bounds for element distinctness, k-sum and k-distinctness
papers.summary: We give elementary proofs of quantum query lower bounds for three well-known problems: the $\Omega(n^{2/3})$ quantum query lower bound for element distinctness, the $\Omega(n^{k/(k+1)})$ lower bound for the $k$-sum problem, for fixed $k$ and sufficiently large groups and the $\Omega(n^{3/4-1/(4(2^k-1))})$ lower bound for the $k$-distinctness problem, even for small alphabets. The proofs use only basic properties of quantum states and linear algebra, analyzing the differences of algorithm states on different inputs.

authors.name: Andris Ambainis, Martins Kokainis, Jevg\=enijs Vihrovs

papers.title: Two exact quantum queries use at most six variables
papers.summary: We give a direct analytic proof that every total Boolean function computable exactly with at most two quantum queries depends on at most six input variables. This bound is sharp. A previous derivation relied on a numerical classification of Boolean functions on at most four variables; to the best of our knowledge, ours is the first unconditional proof. The main difficulty beyond the one-query case is that query-path vectors need not be mutually orthogonal, so interference prevents the scalar weight-counting argument from applying. We overcome this difficulty by establishing a rigid support-and-branch decomposition: after the coordinates in the first-query support are fixed, the second query induces a family of exact one-query branches. This structural description may be of independent interest.

authors.name: Yaqiao Li

papers.title: Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling for efficient quantum trajectories in metastable open quantum systems
papers.summary: Open quantum systems can display metastability, with multiple long-lived states coexisting. Examples include the bistability of bright and dim manifolds in nonlinear driven resonators, or the long-lived coherent states of opposite phases in parametrically-driven systems, the building block of cat-state-based quantum computers. Metastability often emerges at system sizes where density-matrix evolution is impractical. Quantum trajectories mitigate this issue by evolving wavefunctions rather than density matrices. Metastable states then emerge as attractors towards which the system rapidly relaxes until a rare switching event brings it to another attractor. Simulating them remains costly, as one must resolve fast intra-attractor dynamics over timescales long enough to gather switching statistics. To tackle this problem, we introduce the Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling (DiSLOU) method, which combines three optimization layers: (i) Switching among locally optimal unravelings that minimize the number of quantum jumps in each metastable region. (ii) Diagonal propagation: the no-jump evolution is accelerated by diagonalizing the non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian once per attractor. (iii) Local reduced eigenspaces: the no-jump state can be faithfully propagated in a truncated subspace of only slowly decaying eigenmodes. We benchmark DiSLOU on the driven-dissipative Kerr resonator, finding no measurable loss of accuracy and the largest speedup in the bistable regime, where standard trajectories are most expensive. We then apply the method to the more challenging problem of accurately simulating rare bit-flip events in the cat manifold emerging in a two-mode dissipatively stabilized parametric oscillator, obtaining a performance improvement of over one order of magnitude. An implementation of DiSLOU in Julia is available as an open-source package.

authors.name: Pietro Pacchioni, Alberto Mercurio, Patrick Winkel, Fabrizio Minganti

papers.title: Quantum query complexity of Hurwitz stability testing

authors.name: Maxwell Fitzsimmons, Mohamed Serry, Meenu Kumari, Jun Liu

papers.title: Quantum Advantage needs Multiple Perspectives
papers.summary: The origin of the quantum speedup is a topic of ongoing research. We propose a logical criterion for the possibility of a speedup within the continuous-variable and odd-prime qudit settings. There, Wigner function nonnegativity signals the possibility of efficient classical simulation in the state-injection scenario. We consider representations of quadrature/Weyl measurements in a single von Neumann algebra that reproduce the Born statistics in a particular state. If in that state, the set-theoretic universe of the algebra is ZFC-satisfiable, i.e. every ZFC-theorem holds with unit probability, all measurement contexts can be represented in a single commutative algebra of `beables'. Furthermore, the statistics admit a noncontextual hidden variable model, ensuring Wigner nonnegativity for two or more modes or qudits. For a single mode, a stronger notion of linear representation ensures commutativity, and with it, ZFC-satisfiability independently of the state, as well as Wigner nonnegativity. In consequence, in any setting that cannot be efficiently simulated, it must be impossible to merge the models associated with every context into a single ZFC-satisfiable one: quantum advantage needs multiple perspectives.

authors.name: Jochen Szangolies

papers.title: Quantum Relative Entropy and Information Flux Resolve Wavefunction Collapse in Spacelike-Separated QED Waveguides
papers.summary: Resolving how first-order quantum coherence and definite measurement outcomes emerge from entangled vacuum fluctuations across spacelike-separated regions is unified here by the principle that quantum relative entropy governs the energy-information flux across causal boundaries [P.~Dorau and A.~Much, Phys.~Rev.~Lett.~\textbf{136}, 091602 (2026)]. We establish the exact quantum-optical realization of this principle using dual, spacelike-separated entangled nonlinear biphoton sources implemented in quantum electrodynamics waveguides pumped by an optical frequency comb and seeded by a continuous-wave laser in a coherent state $|\alpha\rangle$. We demonstrate that single-photon-added coherent states (SPACS) generated via coherent seeding possess a quantum relative entropy that precisely quantifies the entanglement deficit between signal and idler fields. Tracing over the unmeasured idler continuum yields an exact spatial Lindblad master equation along the propagation axis, proving that spatial dephasing is driven by an information divergence flux determined by the SPACS overlap fidelity $F = |\alpha|^2/(1+|\alpha|^2)$. Uniting this relative-entropy flow with quotient measurement theory (detailed in Section~S3 of the Supplemental Material), we rigorously resolve nonlocal wavefunction collapse into local coset projections---explaining macroscopic state reduction without superluminal signaling.
