The encoder applies SNR-conditioned block attention residuals across all stages, aggregating intra-stage and cross-stage semantic representations. At the receiver, an adapter performs SNR-conditioned affine correction. We introduce a post-encoding rate-adaptive channel semantic budgeting (RCSB) module whose shared gate selects channels of the formed latent by image content, adjusts their gains, and keeps exactly the requested count. This keeps the encoder output independent of the rate request for a fixed image and SNR. Experimental results show that DecompJSCC outperforms SwinJSCC and SA-RA-JSCC in peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) across a range of SNR and rate settings, by 0.64 and 1.00 dB over SwinJSCC and by 0.97 and 0.96 dB over SA-RA-JSCC on Kodak and CLIC2021, while using only 7.5% of SwinJSCC's Adaptive ModNet parameters.

authors.name: Yunhao Liu, Jiancun Fan, Haojun Sun, Jie Luo, Qing Zhao

papers.title: CS-MPC: Contraction-Certified Sampling-Based MPC for Nonlinear Systems Under Uncertainty
papers.summary: We present contraction-certified sampling-based model predictive control (CS-MPC) for tracking and safety of nonlinear robotic systems under parametric uncertainty, disturbances, and safety constraints that are revealed online. CS-MPC uses a contraction-certified tracking feedback inside every sampled rollout, which concentrates the rollouts around the reference, and an execution layer that verifies the applied input using a quantile-tightened discrete-time control barrier function condition. We derive a verification procedure for nonlinear contraction of the feedback-closed dynamics, and we prove a finite-sample stochastic stability bound and a mission-level probabilistic safety guarantee. We validate CS-MPC in simulation on a rover, a quadrotor, and an asteroid landing. When compared with standard model predictive path integral (MPPI) control, CS-MPC attains the same tracking error with 7 to 20 times fewer rollouts for the rover, and a 2 to 4 times lower tracking error for the quadrotor, with no safety violations in 200 Monte Carlo missions.

authors.name: Yashwanth Kumar Nakka

papers.title: Joint Optimization of Antenna Partitioning and Distortion-Aware Precoding for Massive MIMO-OFDM with Peak Cancellation and In-Band Distortion Compensation
papers.summary: In massive MIMO-OFDM systems, peak cancellation (PC) reduces the peak-to-average power ratio but introduces in-band distortion, where compensation signals transmitted from a subset of antennas can suppress this distortion at the users. However, their effectiveness depends on the antenna partition and compensation precoder, while nonlinear power amplifiers (PAs) generate additional distortion. This paper proposes a joint optimization method for antenna partitioning and distortion-aware compensation precoding. To enable this joint optimization, we derive a covariance-based analytical model of PC and PA distortion to predict the per-user, per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plusdistortion- and-noise ratio (SIDNR). The predicted SIDNR is used to select the compensation precoder regularization, the disjoint antenna partition, and the number of compensation antennas. Numerical results demonstrate that joint optimization of the antenna partition and compensation precoder regularization improves BER and SIDNR-based spectral efficiency compared with fixed-partition designs, particularly at high signal-to-noise ratios.

authors.name: Zhuoran Li, Osamu Muta, Haris Ga\v{c}anin

papers.title: Grid-Forming AI Data Centers: Coordinated Grid Support Control from IT Loads and Energy Storage
papers.summary: To exploit the grid-support capability of AI data centers (AIDCs), this paper proposes a grid-forming (GFM) control scheme which coordinates the IT loads and energy storage (ES) in the AIDC. First, the framework of a grid-connected AIDC is presented, with the multi-stage power conversion from the grid to the IT loads presented. A dual GFM scheme is then proposed for the back-to-back converters to provide grid support through coordinated power adjustments from IT loads and ES. In addition, an aggregated power response model is established to characterize the IT-load flexibility considering multiple IT servers executing diverse tasks. Time-domain simulations of a 100 MW grid-connected AIDC demonstrate that the proposed control scheme can effectively support the grid.

authors.name: Xuechun Zhang, Zhiyi Zhao, Fei Teng, Zhen Wang

papers.title: Policy-Conditioned Koopman Representations for Parameterized Closed-Loop Systems
papers.summary: Predicting the response of a nonlinear system across different feedback controllers requires a model that captures how the closed-loop dynamics change with the controller parameters. In a finite-dimensional Koopman model, these changes may affect both the latent dynamics and the observable coordinates used to represent them. In this paper, we propose a policy-conditioned Koopman representation framework to address this problem. This framework allows a single learned model to predict a family of closed-loop trajectories without retraining for each controller. We test the framework on four nonlinear prediction benchmarks, where the model stays below a 15% error threshold on every system, while each baseline exceeds it on at least one. As an example application, the resulting surrogate supports one-shot feedback-parameter selection: an optimization at the initial state selects a controller that then operates with fixed parameters and ongoing state feedback. On nonlinear control benchmarks including MuJoCo, the selected controllers stabilize every system with 3 to 97 times less online computation than nonlinear model predictive control. These results demonstrate how policy-dependent coordinates can support both prediction across closed-loop systems and controller selection without repeated online trajectory optimization.

authors.name: Kiran G. Krishnan, Shankar A. Deka

papers.title: BladeSEI: A Multi-Channel and Multi-Day Dataset for Robust Specific Emitter Identification of Radars
papers.summary: This paper introduces "BladeSEI", a multi-channel receiver, multi-day dataset of radar pulses recorded over-the-air from 12 Software Defined Radios (SDRs) for the purpose of Specific Emitter Identification (SEI). The aim of this dataset is to enable investigation into robust SEI techniques that are able to generalise across different receiver channels and recording sessions. The dataset consists of two waveform types per emitter, a 50 microsecond chirped pulse of 40 MHz bandwidth and a 10 microsecond unmodulated pulse. Pulses are captured simultaneously on four synchronised analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) channels of a multi-channel receiver over three recording sessions on two days: a baseline session, an identical repeat on the following day, and a session in which the emitters were thermally conditioned to alter their operating temperature. Initial results using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Inception and ResNet based classifiers, trained and tested on a single ADC channel and recording session, show that the BladeRF emitters can be discriminated at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), with ResNet achieving a macro-F1 above 0.98 at 25 dB for both waveforms, and performance degrading towards random guessing at 0 dB.

authors.name: Ryan White, Robert Jones, Hassan Habib, Matthew A. Ritchie, Victoria Nockles, Adam Hosford

papers.title: EPIGRIDS: Documentation and Validation of Seven Open Synthetic Transmission Grid Cases
papers.summary: This paper documents and checks EPIGRIDS, seven open synthetic transmission grid cases from four independently built networks, made with an optimization-based construction method instead of the graph-statistics method behind most large public synthetic grids. The cases range from 250 to 78,484 buses, with geolocated substations, voltages up to 765 kV, and line parameters taken from conductor data. Each ships under an open license in three common power flow formats that agree at the solved operating point, and the six larger cases have a companion hourly, bus-level load series for one year. The Texas, Florida, and Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana cases are sub-networks of the Eastern case. Every case solves an alternating-current power flow from its stored operating point. With parallel circuits merged, the Eastern and Western cases are 9 and 16% denser than the real interconnections, while graph-statistics cases on the same footprints lie within 6% and meet more published realism criteria. A full single-outage contingency analysis completes on every case, and in an optimal power flow benchmark every case except the New England base case and one of its 12 operating points solves in polar form.

authors.name: Jonathan M. Snodgrass, Scott Greene, Thomas J. Overbye, Christopher L. DeMarco, Bernard C. Lesieutre

papers.title: An All-Digital Coherent AFSK Demodulator for CubeSat Applications
papers.summary: Audio frequency-shift keying (AFSK) is a widely adopted modulation scheme for CubeSat systems due to its favorable bandwidth efficiency and implementation simplicity. However, coherent detection usually is avoided because synchronization impairments, caused by intense line-of-sight (LOS) dynamics inherent in low Earth orbit (LEO), may significantly degrade the bit error rate (BER). This paper presents a new all-digital coherent AFSK demodulator based on a Kalman filter (KF) for carrier phase and timing delay synchronization and the Viterbi algorithm for bit detection. The Viterbi algorithm is employed for maximum likelihood sequence detection, and the detected bit statistics are fed back to the KF to estimate phase shift, Doppler frequency shift, and Doppler drift induced by the LOS dynamics. Original mathematical analyses are derived to provide a theoretical foundation for the proposed demodulator's operation, specifically addressing its synchronization accuracy in dynamic LEO environments. The proposed demodulator is evaluated considering an additive white Gaussian noise channel with real CubeSat orbits. The performance results obtained through computer simulations demonstrate that the proposed model can withstand such scenarios with a gain of 5 dB in terms of BER compared to the conventional noncoherent AFSK demodulator. The KF performance is assessed using a moving root-mean-square error (MRMSE) statistic and the trace of its state error covariance matrix estimate.

authors.name: Rubem Vasconcelos Pacelli, Rodrigo de Lima Florindo, Felix Antreich, Ant\^onio Macilio Pereira de Lucena

papers.title: Impact of Grid-Forming Inverter Placement and Penetration on Local and Aggregate Frequency
papers.summary: Modern power systems are undergoing a huge shift in generation mix, including inverter-based resources that are fundamentally changing the stability dynamics of the grid. Thus, synchronous Generators (SG) are gradually being displaced by Grid-forming inverters (GFM) that are proposed as a solution to continue supporting grid stability. However, the effect of GFM placement in the network on frequency performance and how well aggregate-frequency assessment captures placement sensitivity observed in local frequency metrics remains unclear. This paper evaluates all SG and droop-controlled GFM assignments in the IEEE 39-bus system. A reduced-order model is used for the exhaustive search with load disturbances applied separately at every eligible load bus while considering nadir and Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) derived from both device rating weighted aggregate frequency and local bus frequencies. Results reveal that at fixed GFM penetration, placement produced up to 104 mHz variation in worst-case local nadir and 0.21 Hz/s in maximum local RoCoF. Aggregate-frequency assessment reduced the apparent across placements by 89\% for nadir and 88\% for RoCoF at 50\% GFM penetration. These results indicate that aggregate-frequency assessment alone may obscure favorable or adverse placement effects on local frequency performance.

authors.name: Fatma Alfailkawi, Marena Trujillo, Bri-Mathias Hodge

papers.title: RF-Agent: A Practical Framework for Building Language Agents for RFIC Design
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have driven rapid progress in electronic design automation (EDA), yet their application to radio-frequency (RF) circuit design remains limited by the scarcity of domain-specific datasets and standardized benchmarks. We present RF-Agent, which addresses this gap through textbook-driven knowledge distillation. A multi-agent Question-Thinking-Solution-Answer (QTSA) pipeline converts a subsection-level corpus from seven canonical RF textbooks into the first-of-its-kind RF-domain reasoning dataset (over 11,000 samples) with a dedicated multiple-choice benchmark. On this benchmark we study two adaptation strategies: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and three retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) configurations (semantic, keyword, hybrid). Across multiple LLM families, domain-specific SFT significantly improves RF reasoning, especially for small and medium-sized models; among RAG configurations, semantic retrieval performs best, indicating embedding-based context alignment suits RF reasoning better than naive fusion. The dataset and benchmark provide a reusable foundation for future work on LLM-aided RF circuit design.

authors.name: Yueqi Xing, Houbo He, Jolie Wang, Erin Ni, Shikai Wang, Qiufeng Li, Weidong Cao, Taiyun Chi

papers.title: Prediction-Error-Tightened MPC for Socially Compliant Crowd Navigation
papers.summary: Autonomous navigation of mobile robots in crowded environments, while preserving pedestrians' psychological comfort, requires distinguishing pedestrians from other obstacles, predicting their future motion, and accounting for uncertainty in the predicted trajectories of both pedestrians and the robot. This work extends a previous MPC framework by integrating obstacle and pedestrian detection, Koopman-based motion prediction, and online prediction-error estimation directly within the collision-avoidance mechanism. To reduce collision-avoidance complexity in crowded scenarios, nearby obstacles are aggregated, thereby reducing the number of collision-avoidance constraints. Simulation studies evaluate the prediction-error margins and the computational benefits of semantics-aware aggregation. In a paired 300-seed closed-loop comparison with a moving generic obstacle, Markov residual tightening reduces the fraction of runs with physical contact from $10.0\%$ to $1.33\%$, at a mean travel-time cost of $0.68$ s. In a separate crowd-navigation semantic ablation, the offline robot-footprint/personal-space overlap occupies $2.11\%$ of observed time with pedestrian-aware handling versus $22.84\%$ with generic-obstacle handling.

authors.name: Alessandro Febbraro, Federico Rollo, Marcello Farina, Luca Bascetta, Navvab Kashiri

papers.title: Natural Swing-Up of an Underpowered Double Pendulum
papers.summary: Robots with weak motors must ride their natural dynamics rather than fight them. We swing up a direct-drive planar two-link robot, whose motors deliver only about 6\,\% of its shoulder gravity torque, along its nonlinear normal modes, two-dimensional invariant manifolds consisting of periodic orbits. On a non-strict mode, injecting energy necessarily moves the state off the manifold, so pumping and stabilization compete for the same bounded torque. We split the input torque into a power-neutral steering component and a scalar pumping input, the only component that changes the energy. The allocation then becomes a linear program in two variables: maximize pumping subject to the torque limits and one control-Lyapunov constraint. The constraint uses the model-based rate of the error, so no stabilizing feedback gain is needed. Experiments in hardware show swing-ups along both modes and compare the allocation with summing-and-clipping and with prioritized stabilization.

authors.name: Arne Sachtler, Manuel Keppler, Florian Loeffl, Alin Albu-Sch\"affer

papers.title: uhd-rfsoc: Bringing Off-the-Shelf RFSoC Boards to Unmodified UHD Applications
papers.summary: Next-generation wireless research relies on software-defined radios (SDRs) with more channels and larger bandwidth. The USRP family is one of the most widely used SDR platforms, and much of the wireless software ecosystem is built on top of the USRP hardware driver (UHD). However, each USRP model comes with a fixed channel count, bandwidth, and streaming capability. Off-the-shelf radio frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) boards, on the other hand, integrate up to 16 analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) and 16 digital-to-analog converters (DACs) operating at several gigasamples per second (GS/s), but existing UHD applications cannot directly use them. We present uhd-rfsoc, an open-source FPGA design and host software stack that turns these boards, including the 16-channel ZCU216 and the RFSoC 4x2, into standard UHD devices without modifying UHD. Through standard UHD calls, applications can configure the carrier frequency, channel count, the per-channel I/Q sample rate, and the wire format. uhd-rfsoc combines timestamped, flow-controlled sample transport in the FPGA with data plane development kit (DPDK) packet processing and vectorized sample conversion on x86 and Arm hosts. The built bitstreams for a number of RFSoC board configurations with varying RF data converter rates, channel counts, I/Q sample rates, and wire formats all successfully pass UHD's built-in streaming benchmarks. We further demonstrate compatibility with unmodified GNU Radio flowgraphs, a custom GPU-accelerated transceiver digital signal processing pipeline, as well as the OCUDU and Duranta 5G radio access network stacks using both software and commodity user equipment.

authors.name: Wei Cheng, Yiming Li, Junyao Zheng, Cheng-Bin Chen, Tingjun Chen

papers.title: Inferring Sensitive Events in Multi-Mode Cyber-Physical Systems via Scheduling Side Channels
papers.summary: Many cyber-physical systems (CPS) are multi-mode: they switch between operating modes with different tasksets and timing parameters in response to physical events or user activity. We show that these mode changes create a timing side channel: by altering the interference experienced by co-running tasks, they let an unprivileged co-resident observer infer sensitive events, such as a homeowner's arrival or a vehicle's route, from its own execution timing and, on multicore platforms, its core assignment. Existing schedule-based attacks and defenses miss this channel because they assume single-mode systems or target a specific, known victim task. We present STAMP, a lightweight attack that needs no knowledge of task parameters or scheduling policy, and works whether or not the system exposes its modes. On a ZoneMinder home-security deployment, STAMP identifies the modes with 94.7% accuracy on unseen hardware, using under 0.5% of one core. On ROS 2 AMCL with the Oxford RobotCar dataset, it identifies which of seven route segments a vehicle traversed with 86.0% accuracy on unseen platforms. A schedule-randomization defense lowers detection recall to 0.53, at which setting only 53.9% as many jobs finish on time. At higher noise ($\epsilon=10$), on-time job completion reduces to 14.4%, while introducing new leakage in 14.1% of the tasksets.

authors.name: Yifan Cai, Linh Thi Xuan Phan

papers.title: OrbitWeaver: LLM Agent Planning with Simulation Feedback for Optically Interconnected Orbital GPU Clusters
papers.summary: Space-based data-center designs increasingly consider GPU computing formations connected by inter-satellite optical links. With limited neighboring connections, jobs assigned disjoint GPUs can still contend on shared relay paths. Rank placement and communication priorities jointly affect this contention and the readiness of downstream computation. We present OrbitWeaver, an offline large language model (LLM) agent planner that jointly optimizes rank placement and communication order. Guided by communication structure, execution dependencies, and simulation feedback, the agent constructs and refines plans that coordinate shared-link access with computation progress. This coordination reduces contention and dependency blocking, shortening mean job completion time (JCT). Simulation experiments on optically interconnected orbital GPU clusters show that OrbitWeaver reduces aggregate mean JCT by 6.2-33.5% relative to the state-of-the-art baselines CASSINI, Crux, and Symphony. These results demonstrate the value of LLM-guided planning for efficient concurrent computing in orbital GPU clusters.

authors.name: Pengcheng Luo, Bowen Zhang

papers.title: Safety Certificates for Systems under Attack via Stackelberg Set Games
papers.summary: We study a Stackelberg set selection game for linear systems subject to bounded disturbances and additive attacks. The defender selects the vector parameter of a polytopic safe set template; the attacker, after observing this choice, selects the vector parameter of an admissible attack set. The payoff is a signed, facet-normalised invariance margin that tests invariance exactly and quantifies either the available contraction or the facet inflation needed when invariance fails. Both controlled and robust controlled invariance are treated, corresponding to different information patterns for the control input. Exploiting the structure of parameterised polyhedra, we show that within each validity region the margin is concave in the attack parameter, which reduces the follower minimisation to finitely many extreme parameters. The complete max--min game is then solved by a finite family of LPs, one per defender validity region, each enforcing all attacker regions under a common defender decision and guaranteed margin. The framework handles hard state constraints and additional costs related to the safe set size, and recovers optimal set parameters together with state and attack realisations that activate the certificate. A load frequency control example under false data injection illustrates the construction, the validity decomposition, and the two information patterns.

authors.name: Nikolaos Athanasopoulos, David Laverty, Gregory Provan, Quanyan Zhu

papers.title: Symbolic Control for Stochastic Systems via Finite Parity Games
papers.summary: We consider the problem of computing the maximal probability of satisfying an omega-regular specification for stochastic nonlinear systems evolving in discrete time. The problem reduces, after automata-theoretic constructions, to finding the maximal probability of satisfying a parity condition on a (possibly hybrid) state space. While characterizing the exact satisfaction probability is open, we show that a lower bound on this probability can be obtained by (I) computing an under-approximation of the qualitative winning region, i.e., states from which the parity condition can be enforced almost surely, and (II) computing the maximal probability of reaching this qualitative winning region. The heart of our approach is a technique to symbolically compute the under-approximation of the qualitative winning region in step (I) via a finite-state abstraction of the original system as a 2.5-player parity game. Our abstraction procedure uses only the support of the probabilistic evolution; it does not use precise numerical transition probabilities. We prove that the winning set in the abstract 2.5-player game induces an under-approximation of the qualitative winning region in the original synthesis problem, along with a policy to solve it. By combining these contributions with (a) a symbolic fixpoint algorithm to solve 2.5-player games and (b) existing techniques for reachability policy synthesis in stochastic nonlinear systems, we get an abstraction-based algorithm for finding a lower bound on the maximal satisfaction probability. We have implemented the abstraction-based algorithm in Mascot-SDS (Majumdar et al., 2020), where we combined the outlined abstraction step with our recent tool FairSyn. We evaluated our implementation on the nonlinear model of a perturbed bistable switch from the literature. We outperform a recently proposed tool for solving this problem by a large margin.

authors.name: Rupak Majumdar, Kaushik Mallik, Anne-Kathrin Schmuck, Sadegh Soudjani

papers.title: An iterative tangential interpolation algorithm for model reduction of MIMO systems
papers.summary: We consider model reduction of large-scale Multi-Input, Multi-Output (MIMO) systems using low-rank barycentric tangential interpolation on the frequency axis. Our scheme is related to the recently-developed Adaptive Antoulas--Anderson (AAA) algorithm, which is an iterative algorithm that uses concepts related to the Loewner framework. One feature of our algorithm is optimization of the interpolation weight matrices to minimize a proxy for the \(L_2\) system error. We use the freedom in interpolation point selection to provide multiple minimum-error-based algorithms with trade-offs between computational complexity and approximation performance. We prove that a weighted \(L_2\) norm of the proxy error system is non-increasing as interpolation points are added, and that the reduced-order system is stable whenever the original system is. Computational results are provided demonstrating the closeness of the proxy system and true system \(L_2\) errors. Comparisons with prior work demonstrate performance on par with standard model reduction methods.

authors.name: Jared Jonas, Bassam Bamieh

papers.title: Integrating Planning and Predictive Control Using the Path Feasibility Governor
papers.summary: The motion planning problem of generating dynamically feasible, collision-free trajectories in non-convex environments is a fundamental challenge for autonomous systems. Decomposing the problem into path planning and path tracking improves tractability, but integrating these components in a theoretically sound and computationally efficient manner is challenging. We propose the Path Feasibility Governor (PathFG), a framework for integrating path planners with nonlinear Model Predictive Control (MPC). The PathFG manipulates the reference passed to the MPC controller, guiding it along a path while ensuring constraint satisfaction, stability, and recursive feasibility. The PathFG is modular, compatible with replanning, and improves computational efficiency and reliability by reducing the need for long prediction horizons. We prove safety and asymptotic stability with a significantly expanded region of attraction, and validate its real-time performance through simulated case studies of unicycle and quadrotor navigation in cluttered environments. \c{opyright}2026 IEEE. authors.name: Shu Zhang, James Y. Z. Liu, Dominic Liao-McPherson

papers.title: Expert-Guided Online Reinforcement Learning for Stable and Sample-Efficient Control of Dynamical Systems
papers.summary: Online reinforcement learning (RL) often requires extensive interactions with the environment, which makes the training costly. Additionally, exploration can destabilise the dynamical system, which may be unsafe. On the other hand, offline learning from expert demonstrations avoids unsafe exploration but is limited by the quality and coverage of the offline dataset. In this paper, we propose a model-free RL approach that combines expert demonstrations with limited online interactions. Specifically, we optimise a policy objective consisting of an online performance term and a behavioural cloning regulariser computed from offline expert demonstrations. The regulariser encourages the learned policy to stay close to expert behaviour, reducing the need to explore unfamiliar actions. Expert demonstrations guide policy learning and reduce the need for many online interactions and exploration. For stochastic linear time-invariant (LTI) systems, we establish conditions for linear convergence of exact policy gradient updates and for all intermediate policies to remain stabilising. Although our theoretical analysis focuses on linear systems, we also evaluate the proposed approach on nonlinear systems to demonstrate its effectiveness beyond the linear setting. \rev{Numerical results show that the proposed method reaches comparable performance in fewer gradient steps and with less number of samples than a purely online RL baseline.

authors.name: Supratim Manna, Arunava Naha, Farnaz Adib Yaghmaie

papers.title: Strong nonlinear detectability and moving horizon estimation for nonlinear systems with unknown inputs
papers.summary: This paper investigates state estimation for general nonlinear discrete-time systems subject to measurement noise and possibly unbounded unknown inputs. To approach this problem, we first propose the concept of strong nonlinear detectability, which proves to be a nonlinear counterpart to strong* detectability. Based on the proposed detectability notion, an unknown input state estimator (UISE), which yields bounded estimation error even for unbounded unknown inputs, is designed via a moving horizon estimation strategy using past and current measurements. Next, we tighten this detectability notion to develop a two-stage MHE-based UISE that is computationally more efficient. In a simulation example, both variants of MHE-based UISEs are compared with a conventional MHE to illustrate the merits of the proposed methods.

authors.name: Yang Guo, Jaime A. Moreno, Stefan Streif

papers.title: Coordinated Cooling and Compute Management for AI Datacenters
papers.summary: The AI datacenters are currently being deployed on a large scale to support the training and deployment of power-intensive large-language models (LLMs). Extensive amount of computation and cooling required in datacenters increase concerns about the energy use and carbon emissions of AI datacenters. Although current state-of-the-art has examined the energy efficiency of LLM inference, most prior research focused on optimizing compute-side scheduling without considering thermal objectives or constraints. Since GPU-intensive inference generates substantial heat that can degrade datacenter performance, ignoring thermal effects can increase total energy consumption and reduce the efficiency of LLM serving. To fill this gap, we profile the characteristics of GPU servers under varying cooling and AI jobs, and develop a joint cooling and computing modeling approach for AI datacenters. Built upon such workload and thermal dynamics models, a novel hierarchical control framework is proposed to co-optimize computing and thermal management by identifying the optimal GPU parallelism, frequency (DVFS), and cooling control knobs. Using real Azure inference traces and detailed GPU profiling, our model balances serving latency and thermal constraints in AI datacenters while significantly improving AI datacenters' energy efficiency.

authors.name: Nardos Belay Abera, Yize Chen

papers.title: Toward Operationalizing Rasmussen in Evolving Software Systems
papers.summary: Rasmussen's qualitative drift model explains how successive, locally successful adaptations under efficiency pressures can move a system toward unacceptable operation. Brooker and Hochstein applied this perspective conceptually to software operations without specifying a quantitative procedure for observing drift. We take a step in this direction and propose a runtime observer that quantitatively operationalizes the model's observable part for evolving software. The proposed observer is intended to give engineers evidence for pausing or revising adaptation before declared operating limits are crossed. It tracks how activity or resource use is distributed across components and types of work. Measurement history quantifies accumulated change and recent movement toward or away from current limits. Assuming that direction and limits remain unchanged, the proposed observer calculates the first constraint ahead and the amount of further change required to reach it. Measurements remain comparable across supported component changes, while policy revisions are distinguished from changes in execution. Preliminary runtime studies demonstrated these distinctions under annotated software changes and revised retry limits. A separate multivariate exponentially weighted moving average (MEWMA) experiment detected CPU redistribution earlier with log-ratio coordinates than with raw shares, motivating investigation of representation-dependent observation. Further work will ground constraints in service outcomes, investigate runtime-model acquisition, and test whether decisions informed by observed drift reduce violations at acceptable useful-work loss and intervention cost.

authors.name: Anatoly A. Krasnovsky

papers.title: Multi-Band Sensing in FR3 with Background Dense Multipath Components
papers.summary: Multi-band sensing has emerged as a key enabler of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), one of the six primary usage scenarios defined for IMT-2030 (6G). The introduction of frequency range 3 (FR3, 7-24 GHz), comprising non-contiguous sub-bands across a wide frequency span, further reinforces the importance of multi-band operation. In such scenarios, frequency-dependent propagation effects that are collectively referred to as dense multipath components (DMC), including clutter, diffraction, and diffuse scattering, must be carefully considered. Building on prior literature and our experimental observations, this paper proposes a novel ISAC channel analysis tailored to multi-band sensing, based on a channel model with background DMCs. It also assesses the sensing trade-offs among sub-bands by analyzing Cram\'er-Rao bound (CRB)-based fundamental limits. Furthermore, a scalable multi-band estimator is proposed that resolves angular ambiguities arising from the grating lobes effect. Simulation results of the multi-band estimator demonstrate substantial gains in estimation accuracy and reductions in false alarm rate over single-band estimators operating on each constituent sub-band within the CRB-achieving regime. In a representative test case, the proposed estimator achieves reductions of 37.41% and 17.04% in the root mean squared error of delay estimation compared to single-band estimators operating at 8.75 GHz and 21.7 GHz, respectively.

authors.name: Dexin Wang, Roberto Bomfin, Ahmad Bazzi, Marwa Chafii

papers.title: Timing-Aware Satellite Association for Multi-LEO Direct-to-Handset Communications
papers.summary: The rapid deployment of large-scale low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations has positioned direct-to-handset (D2H) communications as a key enabler of future non-terrestrial networks. However, the limited link budget of handheld devices makes broadband service delivery challenging, and multi-satellite cooperative transmission is often required to provide sufficient power gain. In practice, such cooperation is severely hindered by asynchronous reception across satellites. This paper analyzes the received-signal model under the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) transmitter structure and shows that satellite-dependent propagation delays prevent simultaneous timing alignment for multiple user terminals (UTs). This timing mismatch induces severe inter-carrier interference (ICI) and inter-symbol interference (ISI), even from the intended signals, which fundamentally constrains the achievable cooperative gain. To address this issue, we propose a timing-aware satellite association strategy that enables cooperation only with satellites expected to satisfy a UT-side timing tolerance, thereby avoiding dominant asynchronous interference by design. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy improves throughput performance compared to single-satellite transmission and fully connected multi-satellite baselines.

authors.name: Hyunwoo Lee, Incheol Hwang, Daesik Hong

papers.title: System-wide Dynamic Performance Metric for Converter-Dominated Power Systems
papers.summary: Fast controller dynamics in Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs)-dominated power networks couple frequency and voltage, making traditional decoupled analysis inadequate. We introduce a unified system-wide metric---the complex frequency of system losses-to evaluate dynamic performance and synchronization. Composed of device- and network-driven terms, it expresses voltage and injected-current phasor variations weighted by bus complex powers. Validated on an IBR-modified IEEE 39-bus system and the Irish transmission grid, the framework effectively assesses R/X sensitivities, dynamic support limits, and data-center load impacts.

authors.name: Rodrigo Bernal, Taulant Kerci, Federico Milano

papers.title: A Control Barrier Function-Constrained Model Predictive Control Framework for Safe Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Ensuring safety under unknown and stochastic dynamics remains a significant challenge in reinforcement learning (RL). In this paper, we propose a model predictive control (MPC)-based safe RL framework, called Probabilistic Ensembles with CBF-constrained Trajectory Sampling (PECTS), to address this challenge. PECTS jointly learns stochastic system dynamics with probabilistic neural networks (PNNs) and control barrier functions (CBFs) with Lipschitz-bounded neural networks. Safety is enforced by incorporating learned CBF constraints into the MPC formulation while accounting for the model stochasticity. This enables probabilistic safety under model uncertainty. To solve the resulting MPC problem, we utilize a sampling-based optimizer together with a safe trajectory sampling method that discards unsafe trajectories based on the learned system model and CBF. We also derive a finite-horizon exit-probability bound using tail information for centered barrier increments. We validate PECTS in various simulation studies, where it outperforms baseline methods.

authors.name: Ali Umut Kaypak, Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Farshad Khorrami

papers.title: Multi-Objective Adaptive Beamforming Using Partial Knowledge of Dynamic Dielectric Media for Non-Invasive Microwave Hyperthermia
papers.summary: We investigate multi-objective adaptive beamformer design strategies for non-invasive microwave hyperthermia. Our focus is to address the challenges of maintaining focused power deposition in desired locations while reducing unwanted heating elsewhere under conditions of changing dielectric properties. The process of heating the media causes changes in the dielectric properties of the media, which can degrade the effectiveness beamformers with static weights. Typical hyperthermic beamformer designs calculate antenna beamforming weights using patient-specific high resolution dielectric maps obtained by MRI or microwave tomography, however this process is time consuming and difficult to perform in real-time. In this work, we explore the efficacy of microwave hyperthermia in various inhomogeneous media under changing dielectric conditions, with the goal of informing the design of future adaptive real-time microwave hyperthermia techniques. We aim to achieve cell apoptosis by obtaining temperatures of $\sim$ 45 $^\circ\text{C}$ through selective absorption of electromagnetic wave focusing at a 2.5 GHz carrier frequency with little to no knowledge of the changes in the dielectric media and simultaneously place nulls to avoid unwanted heating outside of the treatment zone. We investigate the effectiveness of the linear constrained minimum power (LCMP) algorithm for near-field multi-objective beamforming and examine the power density obtained from finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations on simple analytical models and anatomically realistic numerical breast phantoms. To gain a comprehensive knowledge of the efficacy of the beamformer we evaluate the resulting thermal maps of the models in simple homogeneous cases, heterogeneous cases and MRI-derived phantom breast models.

authors.name: Ahona Bhattacharyya, Tessa Haldes, Jeffrey A. Nanzer, Susan C. Hagness

papers.title: Sensing-Aided Beam Selection for UAV Networks
papers.summary: Fast and low-overhead beam management is essential for the practical deployment of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication networks operating at millimeter-wave and higher frequencies. In this paper, we propose a radar-assisted beam selection framework for UAV networks that exploits spatial sensing information, including angle-of-departure and distance estimates, to efficiently identify communication beams. Specifically, a digitally beamformed radar array with a relatively small number of antennas provides rapid, coarse UAV localization, while an analog-beamformed communication array, requiring fewer radio-frequency chains, exploits coarse localization to narrow the beam-search region and establish a communication link with the UAV. To provide theoretical insight into the expected overhead, we conduct a probabilistic analysis in which an approximation of the nearest-first beam selection overhead under idealized conditions is proposed and its statistics are derived for a Gaussian error model. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed radar-assisted beam selection significantly reduces the number of beams that need to be examined, requiring on average at most 1.64 candidate beams even under per-element radar phase errors of up to 100{\deg}.

authors.name: Bora Bozkurt, Ali Gorcin, Cevdet Tosun, Mehmet Nuri Akinci, Ibrahim Hokelek, Mehmet Kemal Ozdemir

papers.title: RCOA Extension and Applications
papers.summary: The Relaxed Convex Obstacle Avoidance (RCOA) formulation is the first approach to enable a fully convex optimal control problem (OCP) for obstacle avoidance. Convergence analysis of RCOA yields an analytical framework that defines a unique characteristic: the ability to maintain obstacle avoidance (OA) efficacy even when obstacles reside beyond the controller's prediction horizon. In this paper, RCOA is extended to three-dimensional environments and apply it to Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) navigation. Furthermore, the formulation is enhanced to incorporate vehicle geometries, moving beyond point-mass representations to enable collision avoidance between 3D objects. Numerical simulations demonstrate that RCOA provides computational performance on par or exceeding state-of-the-art methods. Notably, RCOA is demonstrated to enable a Nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (NMPC) to execute aggressive maneuvers through narrow passages with reduced prediction horizons, ensuring real-time feasibility at frequencies exceeding 30~Hz.

authors.name: Ricardo Tapia, Iman Soltani

papers.title: A Theory of Information Architecture for Networked Decisions: Freshness, Locality, and Coordination
papers.summary: A broader view of a network can help agents coordinate, but collecting that view takes time. When is a fresh local observation more useful than an older view of the whole network, and when should an agent look only partway across it? We study agents that repeatedly minimize a shared quadratic cost in an environment that evolves independently of their actions. An information architecture specifies what each agent observes and how old those observations are. Each agent uses a synchronized neighborhood snapshot, so extending its scope also ages the nearby readings used in the decision. We assume that the optimal action with complete information is affine in the state, and that the conditional mean of the current state equals the old state scaled by a common exponential decay factor. Using the classical Marschak--Radner decomposition, we derive the delay threshold beyond which fresh local information outperforms a complete but older global view. This comparison allows non-Gaussian states and nonlinear decision rules. We then determine how far an agent should look by balancing the benefit of additional observations against their greater age. In a Gaussian spatial model on a line, we derive the optimal observation radius: looking beyond the local node pays only when information travels more than twice the spatial correlation length in one coherence time. The preferred information architecture also depends on the decision being made. On a fixed 64-node ring, increasing only the reach of the decision weights from 0.7 to 6 hops shifts the optimal observation radius from one to five hops.

authors.name: Scott Moeller, Bhaskar Krishnamachari

papers.title: Contract-Based Decomposition of Temporal Logic Specifications for Networked Systems under Arbitrary Partitions
papers.summary: Computational complexity is an inherent limitation of formal synthesis for networked systems, and decomposing the global specification into local ones relaxes this limitation at the cost of conservatism. Since the granularity of the partition governs this trade-off, it is reasonable to treat the partition as a design variable, which calls for local specifications that remain correct for every partition. To this end, this paper gives each agent a local specification, written as an assume-guarantee contract that the agent can establish from local information. We first derive a necessary and sufficient condition for these contracts to decompose the global specification under a given partition. Building on this, we then present a condition under which the decomposition is correct for every partition, so that the partition becomes a free design variable. For linear dynamics and signal temporal logic formulas with affine predicates, we further synthesize a controller for each coalition by a tube-based approach. Finally, simulations on a network of input-coupled tanks show how the choice of partition trades computational cost against conservatism.

authors.name: Kodai Kanno, Kenta Hoshino, Takeshi Hatanaka

papers.title: Symbolic-Permutation-Based Direct Sparse Jacobian Assembly for Accelerated Power-Flow Analysis
papers.summary: The repeated assembly of the sparse Jacobian matrix constitutes a primary computational bottleneck in the Newton-Raphson power-flow analysis. Through an algebraic operator equivariance analysis of the Jacobian matrix, this paper formalizes the reduction process and proposes a direct sparse Jacobian assembly method based on symbolic permutation. By pre-applying the permutation to the admittance matrix during a fast one-time symbolic phase via its sparse prefix-sum property, the runtime bus-type projection overhead and indirect mapping caches are entirely eliminated. Consequently, complex Jacobian differentiation and global matrix assembly fuse into a single operation, yielding a single-pass, branchless algorithm that streams values directly into contiguous memory. The proposed algorithm is implemented in the open-source RustPower solver. Benchmarks on IEEE test systems and PEGASE 9241 demonstrate that the proposed assembly is 28.1-37.9 times faster than the MATPOWER-style baseline and 8.9-9.7 times faster than the in-house Sch\"afer-Braun-inspired assembly (V1); on PEGASE 9241, it outperforms optimized traditional C++ assembly routines by 3.72 times in cold construction and 2.59 times across iterations. End-to-end, the iteration-loop solve time with KLU is 1.16-1.97 times faster than the native C++ LightSim2Grid and up to 95.5 times faster than pandapower, while leaving numerical results and convergence behavior unchanged. The method extends directly to general problems where a sparse Jacobian inherits its structure from a static network operator, including transient stability analysis, EMT simulation, and OPF Hessian assembly.

authors.name: Tianshi Cheng, Venkata Dinavahi

papers.title: Beyond TR 38.811 for 6G NTN Channel Models
papers.summary: As the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) expands 6G non-terrestrial network (NTN) to S, Ku, and Ka bands for integration with existing terrestrial cellular networks, the necessary satellite channel model for link and network performance evaluation remains tied to TR 38.811, last revised in 2020. We identify issues on multiple fronts: inappropriate parameter specifications based on very limited site-specific environments considered, omission of satellite-induced Doppler spread and directional antenna effects and lack of a transparent channel model generation procedure. To address these limitations, we re-derive the channel parameters using ray tracing (RT) over urban and rural environments based on ITU-R building statistics. Our results show that TR 38.811 substantially overestimates the K-factor at low elevations and predicts a decreasing trend with elevation, which is inconsistent with RT. The Ka-band clutter loss (CL) also exceeds the RT estimates by more than 15 dB in urban cases. It also underestimates rural delay spread (DS) at low elevations and predicts an elevation trend inconsistent with RT. We further quantify the previously neglected satellite-induced Doppler spread. Finally, we demonstrate that the conventional TR 38.811 channel generator significantly underestimates the K-factor in the presence of directional antenna (beamforming), while our modified generator substantially reduces this discrepancy.

authors.name: Kuan-Po Chiu, Aaron Jacob Buck, Sumit Roy

papers.title: Analytically Characterized Optimal Power Control for Signal-Level-Integrated Sensing, Computing and Communication in Federated Learning
papers.summary: In next-generation wireless edge systems, efficient functionality integration is essential to address the growing demands of communication, computation, and sensing. Signal-level integrated sensing, computing, and communication (Sig-ISCC) is envisioned, where a single waveform simultaneously supports sensing, computing and communication via over-the-air computation (AirComp). Meanwhile, federated learning (FL) is widely regarded as a promising distributed machine learning framework that enables network intelligence in a privacy-preserving and secure manner, and exhibits strong synergy with AirComp, which alleviates the communication bottleneck of FL. In this paper, we study uplink Sig-ISCC design for AirComp-FL with joint target detection. We formulate the joint power and receive-scaling control problem, where edge devices' transmitted signals should serve both sensing and AirComp purposes. The goal is to minimize the AirComp aggregation distortion subject to a joint target-detection requirement. Although the resulting problem is non-convex in the original variables, we show that it admits an equivalent convex reformulation after a suitable variable transformation. By exploiting analytical optimality properties, we develop a robust, optimal, and polynomial-time-complexity algorithm that efficiently achieves the optimal transmit powers and receive scaling factor. Simulation results validate the optimality and numerical robustness of the proposed algorithm and show its superior FL performance compared to baseline methods.
